datasets.title: Interpersonal Relations among Indian Antarctic Expedition Members in Isolated and Confined Environment.
datasets.abstract: With the advancement of technology, interpersonal factors take on increasing importance in relation to long duration missions in isolated and confined environments. This study explores the interpersonal orientation at the feeling and. The behaviour level during prolonged residence in Antarctica. Twenty-four volunteers from winter-over team of Indian Antarctic Expedition served as participants. FIRO-F and FIRO-B questionnaires were the tools used in this study. The interpersonal orientation at feeling level showed that feeling of lovability was greater than feelings of significance and control. Besides, the feeling of warmth and the respect for competence were low when compared to the feeling of significance desired from others. At the behaviour level, the need for association was greater than the need for personal intimacy with others. On the other hand, the desire for affection from others was higher than the preference for social interaction.
datasets.purpose: 1. To evaluate the interpersonal orientation related to feelings of significance, competence, and lovability over extended residence in isolated and extreme environment.

datasets.title: Space Weather Program at Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The use of GPS (Global Positioning System) in diverse areas such as surveying, enroute navigation and precision approach of aircraft, deformation monitoring, and various land/marine navigation applications necessitate high accuracy and availability. In the presence of time varying irregularities in ionospheric degrades the performance of the GPS receiver. During the 26th ISEA (Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica), the effect of ionospheric irregularities on GPS performance were studied. This includes, standalone GPS receiver positioning at Maitri, a real time kinematic position on board ship in auroral storm region.

datasets.title: Effect of Antarctic Environment on Immune Response of Indian Expedition Members.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctica presents the coldest (temperatures between ?25 ?C and ?89 ?C), driest (average RH 0.03%), and windiest (chilly all-year Katabatic winds averaging 15-50 km/h) environment on Earth - a continent at the highest average elevation (2300 m above MSL). Due to its extreme weather system, and unique geo-location around the South Pole, it is one of the last frontiers for the human race. Medical research in recent years has focused on the life-style of Antarctic expeditionary members, exposed to harsh environmental and psychological conditions over a prolonged period of time [1]. The Antarctic milieu comes with extreme cold, intense UV radiation, white-outs, varying magnetic fields, sleep deprivation, altered circadian biorhythms, memory loss, and isolation - causing significant physiological and psychological stresses [2-4].

datasets.title: Recessional history of the Polar Ice sheet in the Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The margin of the grounded ice sheet around Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica was thicker during glacial advances due to a lower sea level. This has resulted in more grounded ice shelf area. In contrast, during the warming periods, the recession leads to a less ice shelf area, which is grounded. Since supraglacial moraines are deposited during the recession phase, their characteristics and distribution often coincides with the different glacial events. A number of moraines are exposed in and around the Schirmacher Oasis, the detailed study related to their nomenclature and origin has not been attempted so far.The heavy mineral from the lakes of the Schirmacher Oasis indicate a short distance of sediment transport (Srivastava 2010). The heavy mineral studies of the glacial valleys can be carried out to understand the processes of heavy mineral settlement as well as the nature and rate of material transport.
datasets.purpose: Nomenclature of the moraines with respect to geomorphological set up and establishing the chronology of their formation, evaluation of the sequence of glacial valley sedimentation and establishing recessional history of the Polar Ice sheet from these two proxies to ascertain its implications on paleoclimate.
datasets.project_name: Recessional history of the Polar Ice sheet in the Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica

Spare parts for the DG sets can only be brought in once during the summer, when the new expedition team arrives with supplies from India. datasets.title: Some Features of Aerosols and Pre-cursor Gases Observed over Antarctic Region during 24th Indian Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The aerosols and pre-cursor gases data sets have been utilized to investigate the aerosol optical, physical and radiative properties, and their interface with simultaneously measured gases. Data over the Oceanic region has been collected on ship?s front deck. The daily mean AOD at a characteristic wavelength of 500 nm was found to be 0.042 with an average Angstrom coefficient of 0.24, revealing abundance of coarse-mode particles. Interestingly, the January fluxes were found to be less by about 20 per cent as compared to those in February. The average short-wave direct radiative forcing due to aerosols showed cooling at the surface with an average value of -0.47 W/m2 during the study period. The total column ozone increased from about 252 DU around 38o S to about 312 DU at 70o S, showing a gradual increase in ozone with increasing latitude.

datasets.title: Monitoring of Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide (C02) at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The changing behaviour of the atmospheric greenhouse gases, which are very fundamental to climate change, can be understood with the coverage of global measurements. In light of this an automated gas chromatograph has been set up in January 2002 at Maitri (70? 46'S, 11? 45'E) Antarctica for the measurements of greenhouse gases, such as Carbon Dioxide (C02), and Methane (CH4). Annual average C02 found out to be 368.5 ppm. The C02 concentration was found to vary in between 360 ppm to 377 ppm during observational period. Monthly average C02 concentration showed rising trend however no seasonal variation was observed during the year 2002.
datasets.purpose: The possibility of global warming due to anthropogenic and natural variations of greenhouse gases has been debated increasingly in the last few decades. The current important issues, which are dangerous for the survival of life on the earth, are global greenhouse warming, regional increase in tropospheric ozone, urban and regional atmospheric pollution and the decrease in stratospheric ozone and ozone hole over Antarctica. Carbon, in the form of C02, carbonate and organic compounds, is cycled between three main reservoirs, namely the atmosphere, the terrestrial biosphere and the oceans. The observed increase of C02 in the atmosphere has come largely from fossil fuel combustion and cement production.
datasets.project_name: Monitoring of Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide (C02) at Maitri, Antarctica.

datasets.title: R&DE(E) Tasks during Tenth Antarctic Expedition
datasets.abstract: The R&DE (Engrs) has been associated with the Indian Scientific Expeditions to Antarctica since Third Expedition. It has contributed towards the logistic/scientific programme by designing and fabricating the DRDO complex, Dobson Hut, sledges and the systems for Dakshin Gangotri Complex at Antarctica. In continuation of the support, R&DE (Engrs) has designed and fabricated the entire Maitri station which stands today majestically as a totally indigenous station. Three representatives of this establishment were nominated as members of Tenth Antarctic Expedition to provide technical assistance to the team in construction and repair/setting up of refrigeration systems.

datasets.title: Sleep Studies of Summer Members in Antarctica : Cardiovascular Responses.
datasets.abstract: Six summer and four wintering members of Indian Antarctic expedition underwent heart rate (HR) and galvanic skin resistance (GSR) recordings during sleep. A total of three night recordings were performed on each subject at three different sessions during the period of four months of austral summer. As the subjects slept in the laboratory, they showed disturbance in sleep pattern. In all the subjects during summer, the sleep bradycardia increased with absence of periodic fluctuations of HR indicative of temporary loss of REM sleep. The subjects tended to show increase in slow wave sleep during summer. The winterover subjects showed disturbed sleep variables which was not related to HR and GSR changes during sleep. However, due to the limited number of subjects no affirmative answer could be made to prove relationship of sleep disturbance with prolonged daylight or psychological reaction with prolonged isolation.

datasets.title: Digital picture transmission between Antarctica and India.
datasets.abstract: The communication team of the XVI Antarctic expedition took up the task of establishing the first ever picture transmission link betweeen Antarctica and India over a band-limited telephone channel. The link was set up between the MAITRI Station and the Prime Minister's residence at New Delhi on 26 January 1997 when inaugural pictures of the installation of the bust of Mahatma Gandhi at the Indian Antarctic Station MAITRI were transmitted in near realtime to the Prime Minister in India. In this describes the techniques and the steps involved in engineering the picture transmission link using a portable INMARSAT satellite terminal. The authors also highlight the problems and limitations associated in working at the fringe areas of INMARSAT footprint.

datasets.abstract: Installation, commissioning of an INMARSAT maritime satellite terminal and installation of an ERNET node over the satcom were the assigned tasks. In addition to this, experimental internet connectivity, installation of an ethernet based local area network, configuration of a weather server were carried out successfully.
datasets.purpose: INMARSAT is a 72 member co-operative organisation with headquarters x in London. INMARSAT offers communication services to the mobile users around the globe. INMARSAT operates in four ocean regions namely Atlantic O c e a n Region East (AOR-E), Indian Ocean Region (IOR), Pacific Ocean Region (POR) and Atlantic Ocean Region West (AOR-W). An INMARSAT communication neceessarily involves the Mobile, the Satellite and the Land Earth Station (LES). A land earth station provides the interface to National or International Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN). INMARSAT has a wide range of mobile terminals?Standard-A, Standa r d - B , Standard-C and Standard-M. Users can have a choice on the basis of service required and the space/weight limitation. The terminal can be either l a n d based or maritime, based on the application. Standard-A and Standard-B h a v e an option of High Speed Data (HSD) connectivity.

datasets.title: Thermal Acclimatization to Cold in Men Exposed to Antarctic Environment during Summer.
datasets.abstract: The finger skin temperature (Tsk) and blood flow (FBF) alterations before and after cold immersion on exposure to Antarctic environment for 8 weeks were studied in 64 subjects. Cold immersion test was performed at non-Antarctic and Antarctic conditions by immersing the hand for 2 min in 0- 4?C cold water. The result of this study indicated that continuous cold exposure in Antarctica resulted in vasodilatation which overrides the stronger vasoactive response of acute cold exposure, thereby preventing cold injuries. Besides these circulatory acclimatization to cold there was increase in body mass associated with redistribution of subcutaneous fats.

datasets.abstract: Ground based observations of extremely low frequency ( E L F ) and very low frequency ( V L F ) emissions, at the Indian station Maitri in Antarctica have been reported here. T h e E L F - V L F recording experiment was successfully installed during the 1 8th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (ISEA) and observations were carried out during the Jan-Feb., 1999 using the T-type antenna installed during the 17th ISEA. The spectrograms of analyzed data have revealed the occurrence of various events like, discrete chorus emissions, emissions of rising type, falling emissions of hook type, multiple emissions, periodic and quasi-periodic emissions.

datasets.title: Temporal and Spatial Variations of Meteorological Parameters, Energy Fluxes and study of Ice Sheet Dynamics using Remote Sensing and In situ Measurements
datasets.abstract: The connection between snow albedo and climate has long been recognized as an important feedback mechanism. Snow albedo feedback mechanism has been shown significantly to amplify global warming. Thus, it is clearly important to monitor and calculate the variability of the albedo of snow and ice of the continent using satellite technology and ground based information. The reflection, absorption and transmission of solar radiation from any geological surface govern the radiative energy budget, and hence, the surface conditions. The radiation budget estimation of strongly reflecting surfaces of different snow and ice media in Antarctica (i.e. continental ice, shelf ice, natural snow, fast ice, pancake ice etc.) makes the study of their optical properties imperative in order to estimate the global energy balance and climate modeling. However, during summer, the melting process exposes the blue ice regions and causes wide variations in reflectance characteristics.
datasets.purpose: Study of spatial and temporal variation of energy fluxes in shelf and continental ice sheet. Study of ice sheet velocity using remote sensing and in situ measurements. Thickness mapping along the grounding line using GPR and remote sensing techniques Mapping of crevasse vulnerable zones and probable shelf ice break.
datasets.project_name: Temporal and Spatial Variations of Meteorological Parameters, Energy Fluxes and study of Ice Sheet Dynamics using Remote Sensing and In situ Measurements

datasets.title: Atmospheric Studies using Moveable Atmospheric Radar for Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Atmospheric radar is the only method available which can provide continuous monitoring of full height profiles of turbulence, waves, winds and static stability. This can be used to identify stable layers, turbulent layers and tropopause folds. This information can be used to test (and ultimately improve) modelling of the vertical transport and mixing processes which contribute to exchange of constituents between the stratosphere and the land/ice surface, and between the sea surface and higher-level land /ice. Further, radar observations of Polar Mesosphere Summer Echoes (PMSE) offer a number of advantages over satellite and ground-based optical observations for detecting and attributing eventual changes in conditions at the summer mesopause. Radars can operate all day round even during polar summer when the Sun does not set.
datasets.purpose: Use radar observations of atmospheric structure and turbulence, in the polar troposphere and lower stratosphere, to improve and validate models of air transport, particularly in relation to vertical transport and mixing, in different meteorological conditions. Extend possibilities to utilize radar measurements of ice-cloud layers in the polar summer mesosphere to improve understanding of middle atmosphere dynamics and composition on a global scale.
datasets.project_name: Atmospheric Studies using Moveable Atmospheric Radar for Antarctica
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Heart Rate Variability on Exposure to Severe Gold at Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: An attempt has been made to evaluate Heart Rate Variability (HRV) as a reliable index for sympathetic and parasympathetic components of the autonomic nervous system response during the course of acclimatization to severe cold at Antarctica. Two groups (10 each) of healthy men in the age group of 2344 years participated in the study. Group A consisted of fresh inductees to Antarctica for conducting scientific research during austral summer. Group B consisted of winter team members who had already completed 14 months of stay at Antarctica. The HRV experiments were conducted at New Delhi; and on 7th, 30th and 60th day of stay at Antarctica. The HRV was measured as spectral components of low frequency (LF) 0.04-0.05 Hz, related to sympathetic activity and high frequency (HF) 0.15-0.50 Hz due to vagal efferent activity and the sympathovagal balance as LEVHF ratio.

These instruments consist in all 32 spectral bands covering the spectral range from 400 to 2500-nm. Among the 32 bands, four spectral bands are identical to that of AWiFS sensor. These instruments were successfully operated under harsh and hostile environment of Antarctica, and they were used for collecting voluminous ground truth data during the period from December 2006 to March 2007.

datasets.title: Serum Immunoglobulins and Cortisol During Winter Stay in Antarctica Effects of Naltrexone Administration.
datasets.abstract: In six volunteers, who were members of the winter-over team of the 15th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica, serum IgG, IgM and Cortisol were measured before and after eight days of the opioid blocker Naltrexone (NLT) administration. The study was conducted in six phases. There were no significant changes in the IgG levels before and after NLT administration. However NLT administration reversed the decrease in IgM found during the early winter and in the summer phase at the end of the isolation period indicating a role for the opioid receptors. Results of the serum Cortisol values measured before and after NLT administration indicate that the central opioid receptor regulation may vary in humans during different seasons in Antarctica. This may indeed reflect an inherent mechanism involving opioids in providing adaptation to the stressful situation by taking anticipatory cues from the environmental factors.

datasets.title: Optimisation of Greenhouse Climate and PAR at Maitri.
datasets.abstract: The optimization of greenhouse climate at Maitri station in Antarctica is described. Strategies for controlling temperature, humidity, light and CO2 concentration are described. Heating load has been estimated. July was the coldest month and required most heating. Annual heating degree days at 25? C indoor temperature were 13277.3, while those for 20? C and 15? C indoor temperatures were 11452.3 and 9627.3 respectively. Annual heating loads at 25, 20 and 15? C indoor temperatures were 77038.56, 66449.04 and 55859.28 MJ respectively. Monthly heating loads varied between 4424.88 and 8993.52 MJ at 25? C indoor temperature. Annual heating loads varied in accordance with the greenhouse temperature as Hmj = 24166.57 +2114.04 *Tg Maximum PAR (Photosynthetically Active Radiation) level at the ice surface reaches upto 90000 lux. PAR levels inside the greenhouse varied between 100 and 45000 lux during polar day.
datasets.purpose: Antarctica, the most isolated continent, has only 2% of its area as free of ice. Apart from snow algae, lower species of plant kingdom viz. moss and lichens are found in these zones. Antarctic water and soil have a little amount of nutrients, so the growth of these species is poor. The severe Antarctic climate limits the number of land plants that are able to grow. Higher plants can not survive here because of extremely low temperatures; although two vascular plants: Colobanthus quitensis and Deschampsia antarctica have been reported to grow in Antarctic peninsula. In order to grow plants in Antarctica, protected cultivation is the only way as outlined by Joshi and Banerjee (1988) and Kononov and Kiran (1988). Intensive production of vegetables is possible in greenhouses under controlled environment. In order to study plant growth and yield of vegetable crops, a greenhouse was constructed at Maitri station during the IX Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.project_name: Optimisation of Greenhouse Climate and PAR at Maitri.

Some variation in the accumulation/ablation pattern over shelf ice is noticed during 1992 austral summer. A near steady state of recession of the snout of Dakshin Gangotri Glacier is indicated.

datasets.title: Study of ELF-VLF Emission and Tweek Atmospherics Observed at Maitri.
datasets.abstract: The study of the various geophysical phenomena during quiet and disturbed periods of solar activity gives us a deep insight into the detailed microstructure of microphysical processes taking place in ionosphere, magnetosphere and ionosphere magnetosphere coupling. Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) and Very Low Frequency (VLF) emissions are one of them and are believed to have origin in the ionosphere-magnetosphere coupled system and may be due to plasma instabilities or in-situ electromagnetic radiation from high-energy particles. The propagation of these emissions in the ionized regions (ionosphere and magnetosphere) provides invaluable information regarding the physical structure and characteristics of these regions. In this paper we have presented the observed hiss with periodic structures at Indian Base Station MAITRI, Antarctica during the XXIV Indian Antarctic Expedition.

For this purpose signals from Global Positioning System (GPS) satellites were monitored. Diurnal range in variation of TEC is found to be much less than that at low latitudes. datasets.title: Response of the Ionosphere During the Low Solar Activity Period 2008 Over Maitri, Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Present study, based on dual frequency GPS, derived preliminary results of the diurnal and seasonal variations of Total Electron Content (TEC), amplitude scintillation (S4-Index) and response of TEC during the minor geomagnetic disturbances over the Indian base Station Maitri (Latitude -70.65? N, Longitude 11.45?E) Antarctica, during the low solar activity period (Jan.-Dec. 2008). Monthwise TEC values are highest during the months of January and December, as compared to June month. As regarding seasonal variations, in winter months i.e. June, July and August 2008, TEC values were lowest because ionization process are very low, due to the absence of sunlight; whereas during southern summer season TEC values reaches its maximum, due to the presence of 24-hour sunlight and hence the ionization radiation from the sun.

datasets.title: Ground Penetrating Radar Survey for Detection of Shelf Ice Depth and Its Spatial Variation in Central Dronning Maud Land, East Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Ice shelves are a permanent feature of Antarctica; these not only bind but also shape the continental ice sheet. However, shelf ice is fluctuating in nature, due to direct contact with the sea. Changes in the extent of shelf ice with varying climatic conditions can be interpreted using various remote sensing satellites; but these satellites do not yet have the capability to retrieve depth information. Radio-echo sounding provides an efficient tool to measure ice depth.
datasets.purpose: The survey results show that the shelf ice thickness varies between 20 and 60 m. 3-D map of the surveyed area was prepared using the latitude and longitude information from the GPS and the depth information from the GPR. After combining various GPR profiles, it is observed that the shelf ice thickness decreases while moving towards the sea in the north direction and it increases away from the sea edge towards the south. Sharp reflections of radio waves from two different levels (depth) were observed at few locations in radargram, although these reflections are from very limited area but their interpretation is a further area of research.

datasets.title: Comparison of Cardiovascular Responses to Cold Stress of Summer and Winter Over Members in Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Nine subjects each from eleventh Summer and eighth Wintering teams were studied to compare the changes in the cardiovascular reactivity to cold exposure. Cold immersion test (CT) was carried out on these subjects on three occasions and simultaneous record of pain threshold time, blood pressure, heart rate (ECG) were obtained. The results show that the normal reactivity of cardiovascular system to cold exposure gets attenuated after acclimatization in Antarctic environment. The short summer exposure was sufficient to increase the cold induced pain threshold. However, it lasted only for three weeks whereas for winter groups the acclimatization was for a longer period. This indicates different mechanism of acclimatization for the two groups.

datasets.title: Monitoring of ozone, water vapour etc during the voyage to Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The monitoring of trace species such as water vapour, ozone etc. is of great significance for understanding the Physics, Chemistry and radiation budget of the atmosphere. The water vapour being highly variable constituent in the atmosphere with temperature, space and time, its measurement plays a great role in the study of many atmospheric processes, such as weather, climate, infrared astronomy, cloud physics communication, etc. A highly sophisticated and microprocessor based compact sun photometer consisting of five filter channels at 300, 305, 312, 940 and 1020 nm was used to measure water vapour and ozone in addition to various other parameters such as UV-B radiation, near IR radiation, aerosol optical depth etc. The measurements were made on the way from Goa, India (15?24' N, 73? 42'E) to Maitri, Antarctica (70 deg 46' S, 11 deg45' E)on Polar Bird (Norwegian ship) during December 1996- March 1997.

datasets.title: Energy budget model based on albedo and glacio-meteorological parameters of diffrent snow-ice media in Antarctica through ground based observations, 1997-98.
datasets.abstract: Measurements of the dependence of albedo in different snow and ice media on solar elevation angle, cloud cover, liquid water content, grain size etc. can be interpreted in terms of single scattering and multiple scattering radiative transfer theory. Detailed albedo measurements were carried out during summer and winter period in different snow and ice media in 1997-98 at different chosen sites in Antarctica. Average albedo values were found to be high in snow medium (max. 99%) moderate in shelf ice (max.90%) and very low values (max.58%) in the continental ice medium. The albedo was found to be a function of cloud amount, increasing with the amount and thickness. In white-out conditions during blizzards high albedo (Av. 83%) was found as compared to clear sky day (Av.76%) and after blizzard (Av. 78%). It showed dependency on the type of snow also. New snowfall over old snow displayed higher values (90%) than older snow (70%) and decreases with the age of snow.

datasets.title: UV Radiation and Primary Production in the Antarctic Waters.
datasets.abstract: A profiling underwater radiometer was used for the first time in the waters around Indian Antarctic Station (70?46'S & 1 l?44'E) in the summer of 1994. The profiles include natural fluorescence (upwelled radiance at 683 nm), scalar irradiance (photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), computed primary production (pp), diffuse attenuation coefficient, and UVB (308 and 320 nm) and UVA (340 and 380 nm) radiation and ocean temperature all measured as a function of depth from 21/1/94 to 673/94. Fifteen stations in the Antarctic waters (69?53' to 70?02'S) and 6 en route (64?53' to 30?01'S) were analysed. The average values for surface chlorophyll a and pp were higher for temperate than for Antarctic waters (1.68 mg/m3 and 216.56 mgC/m3 /d respectively). The values for column chlorophyll (22.48 mg/m2) and primary productivity (1023.79 mgC/m2 /d) in the Antarctic waters however, were 2.14 and 1.5 times higher than those in temperate waters.
datasets.purpose: A profiling underwater radiometer (Biospherical Instruments Inc. San Diego, CA, USA) was used to procure data on chlorophyll a (chl a) derived from natural fluorescence (upwelled radiance at 683 nm, scalar irradiance-PAR (photosynthetically available radiation), diffuse attenuation coefficient (K), computed primary production (pp), UVB and UVA radiation as function of depth from 15 stations in the Antarctic waters (69?53' to 70?02'S) and 6 stations from Temperate waters (64?53S to 30?01'S). The instrument enables to assess the effect of sub-surface transmission of UVR in aquatic environments.

datasets.abstract: It is a well-known fact that stress generates free radicals that may cause lipid peroxidation and affeact the antioxidant status of the body. The body has certain set mechanisms to exert scavenging action on free radicals that include some antioxidant enzyme systems like super oxide dismutase, catalase and glutathione peroxidase, glutathione-s-transferase and glutathione reductase which are involved in the detoxification of reactive oxygen species directly or indirectly Low levels of these antioxidant enzymes will cause accumulation of free radicals and may finally actively participate in the process of tissue injury (Mulden et al, 1991). According to another study free radicals damage tissue both at cellular and sub-cellular level by causing lipid peroxidation in the cell membranes and the inactivation of membrane bound enzymes (Florence, 1995).

datasets.title: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctic, Maitri
datasets.abstract: Antarctica has attracted the attention of scientific community all over the world since it is one of the most important climate regimes with a potential to influence long term global climatic patterns. In order to study these, IMDs meteorological programme is specifically aimed at preparing a data archive of meteorological parameters over Antarctica. This may also enable us to understand the global aspects of Indian weather in general and monsoon behavior in particular. World Meteorological Organization (WMO) strongly recommends that any research station established in Antarctica should run a complete meteorological observatory and deliver the obtained data through Global Telecommunication System (GTS).

To improve understanding of teleconnections between Antarctic and Indian Monsoon.To provide data for use in weather predictions and climate projections for India. To improve representation in numerical models of radiative, dynamical and chemical coupling processes throughout the atmosphere, focusing on energy and momentum transfer, chemical transport and links between Indian region and hemispheres.To understand the connections between ozone concentrations and characteristics of the polar vortex that will enable improved projections of the climate system response to ozone recovery, and particularly of changes to winds and storm frequencies at high southern latitudes. datasets.title: Changes in Leptin and Neuropeptide Y in Team Members of Indian Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.abstract: Antarctic expeditioners face different extremes of environmental conditions along with social isolation and sexual deprivation, which create a combination of physico-social factors that complicate normal human activity at a polar station. Adaptation in that new condition is always associated with some metabolic changes with alteration in nutritional requirements and utilisation. The present study was undertaken with the aim to assess the changes in appetite regulatory peptides i.e. leptin and neuropeptide Y and to know actual energy intake and expenditure of the Antarctic expeditioners. The study was conducted in three phases viz. Phase I at Goa (basal), Phase II 48h after reaching Antarctica and Phase III after one month of stay at Antarctica. Blood samples were collected in each phase for biochemical estimations. Energy and nutrient intake were analysed from the duplicate plate samples of the expeditioners.
datasets.purpose: The present study, was undertaken to see the changes in leptin and neuropeptide Y levels in human volunteers at Antarctica and their role in regulation of appetite, food intake and change in body weight and to know the actual energy intake and expenditure of the volunteers at Antarctica.

datasets.title: Meteorological & Climatological Studies at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Antarctica continent influences the general circulation pattern over the globe and is supposed to provide significant forcing to the future climate changes due to its huge ice shield covering most part of the continent. Weather over Antarctica is a real challenge to the meteorologist participating in the Indian Scientific Expedition. A permanently manned meteorological observatory equipped with the instruments to monitor weather system exist at the Indian Antarctic station MAITRI and continuous meteorological parameters were recorded during 17th Expedition from Jan.98 to Dec. 98. During the XVII Indian Scientific Expedition, installation of a snow gauge was done for measuring the snow collected during snowfall/bizzard days. In this report data pertaining to surface weather parameters i.e. the atmospheric pressure, temperature, wind direction, wind speed, cloud snowfall, global radiation, surface ozone and vertical distribution of ozone are presented and discussed.

datasets.title: Response of sub-Auroral Ionosphere to the space-weather events.
datasets.abstract: The proposal is an attempt to study various upper atmospheric stormy features over Indian Permanent scientific Base Maitri which comes under the sub-auroral region especially during the sub-storm events. It is considered that a sub-storm begins when a non-uniform solar wind stream approaches the boundaries of the magnetosphere. These processes are responsible to perturb the auroral region and cause to extend the auroral region more towards the mid-latitude region and along the evening and morning sides of the auroral oval in the form of two flows until they meet each other in the midnight sector (20 30 min after the disturbance onset in the noon sector). The effects of magnetospheric sub-storms in the ionosphere have been studied for several decades but far from completely. First, this is most probably caused by the fact that geophysicists try to better understand the processes in the magnetosphere and far from the Earth during sub-storms rather than in the ionosphere.
datasets.purpose: Study the response of sub-auroral ionospheric region to the geomagnetic sub-storm events. Investigation of solar wind thermospheric magnetospheric ionospheric coupling process over sub-auroral region during adverse space weather conditions.

datasets.abstract: Aerosol optical depth and solar infrared irradiance at 1020 nm using narrowband filter has been measured using a microprocessor based sun photometer during 1997,2002,2003 and 2004. The observations were taken on hourly basis on all clear days at Maitri, an Indian Antarctic Station, during seventeenth, twenty-first, twenty-second and twenty-third Indian Scientific Antarctic expedition. Very low AOD values and comparatively high solar infrared irradiance at 1020 nm have been observed during the entire period of observation at this clean and pristine environment of the continent. But found a clear variation in month-to-month values of AOD, which can be attributed to the local meteorological conditions.
datasets.purpose: Aerosol studies over the sites such as Antarctica will help in estimating the background level aerosol forcing over a pristine site. Factors like high surface albedo and unique solar insolation cycle over Antarctica also makes the study an interesting one.

During XVI expedition the wind monitoring station was installed and commissioned. Wind data has been collected in three levels. Further a study of terrain features, energy loading patterns and infrastructure available at Maitri was carried out.

datasets.title: Measurement of Total Ozone, D-UV Radiation, Sulphur Dioxide and Nitrogen Dioxide Through Brewer Spectrophotometer at Maitri, Antarctica During the Year 2000.
datasets.abstract: Brewer Spectrophotometer has been installed at Maitri, the permanent Indian Scientific Research Station, Antarctica in July 1999 to measure total ozone, damaging ultra-violet radiation (D-UV), Sulphur dioxide (S02) and nitrogen dioxide (N02). The depletion of ozone and its fluctuation could be monitored day to day during Antarctic spring season (August-October). The data collected during the year 2000 are analyzed in this paper. The instrument Brewer spectrophotometer, (here after called Brewer) and its functions are described briefly. The values of total ozone and D-UV are compared in each month. The sudden increase or decrease of D-UV confirms further depletion or recovery of ozone in the successive days during spring. The measurements confirm the existence of 'Ozone Hole' over Antarctica during 2000. The measurements of S02 and N02 at Maitri show very low values.

datasets.title: Quantifying and monitoring climate-induced changes in Antarctic waters
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic Ocean plays a major role in the development and maintenance of the Earth?s climate system. Rapid regional warming of air temperature on the Antarctic Ocean during the last few decades is exceptional and unprecedented change causing retreat of the ice fronts and increased melt water production particularly in summer. This in turn results in changes of terrestrial as well as marine ecosystems along the Peninsula. Locally increased import of fresh water from melting glaciers, increased sediment import from rock abrasion (by glacial melting and aerosol transport), and changes in constituents (nutrients, sediments, dissolved inorganic matter and contaminants) have the potential to fundamentally alter biogeochemical cycling and productivity in the coastal zone and in the Antarctic Ocean (continental shelves). Changes in the Antarctic coastal zone will not only affect regional biological (and perhaps human systems), but are also likely to influence the global climate and oceanic

datasets.abstract: Climate change impacts ocean biota in different ways and several ocean models have suggested that the Southern Ocean surface waters are going to become warmer and fresher with increased vertical stratification, reduced sea-ice, higher CO2 oceanic concentrations and ultimately increased up welling. Alteration of these ocean properties may affect the primary producers biomass and diversity. This is in turn could have a long lasting impact on oceanic birds and mammals, which are directly or indirectly linked to the availability of primary producers. In this connection, the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) had participated in the XIV, XV and XVI Indian Scientific Expeditions to Antarctica (1994-95 to 1996-97) and has implemented a Monitoring Programme entitled ?Developing a Long-term Monitoring Programme for Birds and Mammals in the Indian Ocean and Antarctica".

datasets.title: Micrometeorite Collection and Investigations from Pristine Environments of Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Brownlee (1985) estimated a total of about a million extraterrestrial particles from all collections worldwide, this number would of course be much larger today. If one considers the estimated annual micrometeorite flux of ~30,000 tons, the amounts collected on earth so far would be a few hundred milligrams or at best a few grams! This may not amount to be even the proverbial tip of the iceberg. Micrometeorites are an extremely valuable resource of solar system material. Cosmic dust, more so large collections, provide greater insights into the types of materials that asteroids or comets comprise of, and in turn have the potential to provide clues to the early solar system processes.

datasets.title: Isolation and Molecular Characterization of Sea Ice Microbial Communities of East Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: During the XXI Indian Antarctic Expedition bacterial samples have been collected from different habitats of Antarctica. A total of 150 pure isolates were obtained by streak plate method. Of these, 64 isolates are marine. Morphological, biochemical, physicochemical and molecular characterization of the all the strains have been completed. Studies on the salt and temperature tolerance of the marine isolates indicate that all the strains are halotolerant psychrotrophs. Studies on the pH tolerance revealed that they are neutrophils and tolerated a pH range of 4 to 11.8. PCR based RFLP analysis of various strains indicate that there are 13 genetically different marine species. Partial sequencing of 16 S rRNA of all the RFLP differentiated strains have been completed. Blasting and species identification will be possible only after sequencing the complete 1538 bp gene, which is in progress.

datasets.title: Pharmaceuticals and personal care products in the sewage effluents and adjacent sea waters in the Antarctic specially managed area (no. 6), Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) are a class of emerging micro pollutants that are now ubiquitously present in the aquatic and marine environments (Klosterhaus et al 2013, Luo et al 2014). PPCPs range from medicines consumed for various illnesses to stimulants like caffeine to personal care products like sun screen lotions, soaps, perfumes etc (Daughton and Ternes 1999). Their pathways into the aquatic environment are primarily from wastewaters originating from industries and domestic sources (Daughton and Ternes 1999; Ternes et al 2004). Studies have indicated that very low concentrations of triclosan, an antibacterial used in soaps, toothpaste and deodorants can induce cytotoxic, genotoxic and endocrine disruptor behaviour in aquatic organisms like fish, crustaceans and algae (Bedoux et al 2012).

datasets.title: Studies on Seismotectonics and Geo dynamical Processes between Antarctica and Southern Indian Peninsula: Continuous GPS monitoring between India and Antarctica (2012 -2013)
datasets.abstract: Global Positioning System (GPS) measurements at Maitri, Antarctica have been carried out since 1997 to study the seismotectonics and geodynamical processes of India and the plate motion between the Indian and Antarctica plates. The GPS velocity fields of Maitri and other IGS stations (Casey, Davis, Seychelles, COCO, Hartebeesthoek, Yaragadee, and Tidbinbilla) in different plates show consistency with the calculated plate motion. The estimated pole for the Antarctica plate is at 58.69?N, 128.29?W with rotation of 0.224?/Ma which gives a velocity of about 9 mm/year predominantly towards north at Maitri, Antarctica. The estimated velocity is consistent with this euler pole. Thus the velocities within uncertainties are in good agreement between geodetic and geologic model. Our estimated velocity vectors conform to those of SCAR GPS campaigns consistent with rigid plate rotation.

datasets.abstract: The Antarctica is known to be the coldest, stormiest, windiest and least known continent. It is almost completely covered by ice. Inspite of these inhospitable conditions, it is attracting world wide attention because of its strong influence on weather, the global heat balance and its hidden economic potential. In this an analysis of different weather systems encountered and experienced during the passage and stay at Antarctica of the XIII Antarctica expedition. The expedition team sailed from Marmagao onboard M V Stepan Krashanennikov on 08 Dec 93. The team included two Meteorological scientists from India Met Dept and one Meteorological and Oceanographic Officer from the Indian Navy. The summer of 1993 - 94 had one of the severest blizzards during Feb 94 which damaged the ship's rudder control system. This led to an unavoidable extended stay at Antarctica.

datasets.title: Baseline Data on Natural Radioactivity and Trace Metal Concentration in Natural Antarctic Samples.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic environment can be expected to provide a reference level for environmental and pollution studies due to its remoteness and restricted human activities. BARC participated in the Ninth Expedition mainly to collect background baseline data on natural radioactivity and trace heavy metal concentrations in air, water and rock samples and also to measure background gamma dose rate in air and tritium levels in the ocean as well as in Antarctic fresh waters. The observations made during this expedition and the results of the analyses on the samples collected are presented in this report.

datasets.title: Ice Sheet dynamics from Schirmacher Oasis to Wohlthat Mountains, cDML, East Antarctica and their stress pattern.
datasets.abstract: Recession of the snout of Dakshin Gangotri glacier in the western part of Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica has been recorded over two decades. However, the rate of retreat is not uniform and varies at different locations. The ice wall forming the western flank of the glacier has shown an average retreat of 17.07 m between 2001 and 2009 while the snout had gone back by 6.94 m (average) during the same period. Before 2001, the snout had shown a complete recession of 3.13 m (average). The snout occupies valley area receiving less amount of solar radiation as compared to the western wall, which is a vertical cliff receiving maximum amount of solar radiation. The notable difference in the rate of recession in different parts of the Dakshin Gangotri glacier overriding Schirmacher Oasis can be attributed to combined effect of natural factors, including meteorological parameters, ice sheet dynamics and geomorphology of that area.

datasets.title: Terrestrial exposure dating on Roche Moutonnees and glacial deposits of Schirmacher Oasis to understand the extent and timing of last glacial maxima in the Queen Maud Land, East Antarctic
datasets.abstract: Schirmacher Oasis is an ice free area in the Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica,which lies between continental ice sheet and ice shelf. In this area numerous pro-glacial lake, Roche Moutonnees and glacial deposits of different scale are present. These geomorphic features are indicative of glacier advances and retreat in the past. Based on the environmental magnetism and radiocarbon dating on lake sediment, Warrier et al. 2014 suggested that this area is evading full glaciations since 40,000 years. However, this area experienced many glacial-interglacial variation of different scale during the above period. Terrestrial exposure dating on Roche Moutonnees and boulders from glacial deposits will provided the information about the extent and timing of last glacial maxima of that area. For dating these geomorphic features cosmogenic radionuclides such as 10Be and 26Al are suitable geochronological proxies. The production rate of these radionuclides are more in the higher latitude.

datasets.title: Geophysical Studies in Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The geomagnetic storms and sub storms are the major mechanisms by which solar wind energy enters the Earth's upper atmosphere. The magnetic sub storm is a night-side phenomenon occurring in high latitudes through which charged particles are accelerated along the magnetic field lines from the magneto tail and pushed into the inner magnetosphere, whereas the geomagnetic storm is caused by the intensification of equatorial ring currents at a distance of few earth radii (inner magnetosphere) from the surface of the earth giving rise to a large reduction of the northward component of the geomagnetic field on the ground at low latitudes. Further, the location of Maitri being sub-auroral and moving in and out of auroral oval with increasing magnetic activity makes it an ideal location for any effort that leads to the prediction of space weather.

datasets.title: ICE CORE (IND-22/B4) DATA,CENTRAL DRONNING MAUD LAND, EAST ANTARCTICA
datasets.abstract: Ice core provide one of the most direct climatic proxy records. Ice core are cylinders of ice drilled out from ice sheet or glaciers. Ice cores contain an abundance of information about climate. Inclusions in the snow of each year remain in the ice, such as wind-blown dust, ash, bubbles of atmospheric gas and radioactive substances. An ice core from the right site can be used to reconstruct an uninterrupted and detailed climate record extending over hundreds of thousands of years, providing information on a wide variety of aspects of climate at each point in time. These recorded atmospheric signatures in the ice make the ice cores such a powerful tool in paleoclimate research. Ice core division of NCAOR has collected several ice cores from coastal Dronning Maud Land, East Antarctica. The details of the ice cores collected and the parameters analysed are presented here.

datasets.abstract: Lamprophyres occur in varied tectonic setting and are generally considered to represent primitive magmas and some are even thought to represent primary magmas (Rock, 1987). They are also considered closer to the inter telluric magma compositions with the ?combination of groundmass + phenocrysts + volatile H2O/CO2-rich mineral representing a complete magma system [melt + suspended crystals + volatile phase]? (Rock, 1990). Thus, they present an opportunity to study mantle reservoirs through petrological and geochemical tools.

datasets.title: Detection and characterization of viral RNA from Antarctic ice sheet
datasets.abstract: The Antarctica ice sheet may have trapped and preserved multiple airborne and waterborne viruses, many of them being pathogenic to humans, animals, and plants. Some of these viruses might have been trapped in the ice before human came into contact with them, hence upon re-emergence such viruses may potentially interact with human population that would not have any resistance or immunity against them, giving rise to major pandemics causing immense morality and morbidity among humans. Global warming might become a major cause for such re-emergence of pathogenic viruses, as the melting of polar and glacial ice may release and/or activate viruses preserved in the ice. Therefore, in the context of global warming, it is crucial to identify such viruses before they can emerge and gain epidemic proportions such that therapeutics or vaccines might be envisaged.

datasets.title: Atmospheric Studies using Moveable Atmospheric Radar for Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Atmospheric radar is the only method available which can provide continuous monitoring of full height profiles of turbulence, waves, winds and static stability. This can be used to identify stable layers, turbulent layers and tropopause folds. This information can be used to test (and ultimately improve) modelling of the vertical transport and mixing processes which contribute to exchange of constituents between the stratosphere and the land/ice surface, and between the sea surface and higher-level land /ice. Further, radar observations of Polar Mesosphere Summer Echoes (PMSE) offer a number of advantages over satellite and ground-based optical observations for detecting and attributing eventual changes in conditions at the summer mesopause. Radars can operate all day round even during polar summer when the Sun does not set. They are also much cheaper to run than satellites or ground-based lidars.

datasets.title: Response of high latitude ionosphere to the sub-storms and storms
datasets.abstract: The proposal is an attempt to study the response of high latitude ionosphere to changing space weather conditions especially the ionospheric consequences due to sub-storms events. The study can be performed by utilization of ionospheric data generated with the help of space (Global Ionospheric Scintillation and Total electron Content monitoring i.e. GISTM system) and ground (Canadian Advanced Digital Ionosonde i.e.CADI) based experiments which are already installed by CSIR-NPL, New Delhi during 28th ISEA at Maitri, Antarctica. The said systems are working properly and providing quality data since March 2008. Installed Ionosonde and GISTM systems at Maitri, Antarctica continuously provide a high quality data which is useful to know the real time status of different ionospheric parameters like peak density, TEC, day-to-day occurrences of spread-F & L-band scintillation during the changing space weather condition.

datasets.title: Observation of Meteorological Parameter and High wind speed recorder
datasets.abstract: Antarctica has attracted the attention of scientific community all over the world as it is one of the most important climate regimes with a potential to influence long term global climatic patterns. In order to study these, IMDS meteorological programme is specifically aimed at preparing a data archive of meteorological parameters over Antarctica. This may enable us to understand the global aspects of Indian weather in general and monsoon behavior in particular. The daily synoptic observations recorded at Maitri, Antarctica enter into the Global Telecommunication System (GTS) and contribute to the international efforts for weather forecasting. Continuation of surface weather observation at Maitri will provide necessary input for understanding the variation in the Antarctica atmospheric circulation patterns, which have influence over global climate.

datasets.title: Studies on Diversity of Bryophytes of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Larsemann Hills an area of about 50 sq lies at South Latitudes 69? 20? and 69? 30? and East Longitudes 75? 55? and 76? 30? ice-free coastal oasis with exposed rock and low rolling hills and contain hundreds of fresh water lakes. Bryophytes, because of their relative lack of cuticle, absorb water and nutrients through the general surface of their plant body, even in some mosses, where the conducting tissue is fairly evolved, and liverworts where rhizoids are abundantly present, they normally depend on surface absorption of water and nutrients. Therefore they are growing near the water bodies and thus the habitats of Larsemann Hills will support the growth of bryophytes. Because of their poikilohydric nature and alternative strategy of adaptation, the bryophytes are one of the important plant groups which grow in Antarctica

Comparison on the existing flora with the flora of other Antarctic and alpine regions of the Indian Himalayas.Carry out phytosociological studies to understand vegetation pattern and structure.

datasets.title: Glaciological Studies in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica for assessing the impact of climate change

It is proposed to identify the accumulation and ablation zones at selected places in the vicinity of Bharti Station as well as on the polar ice sheet for monitoring the glacier mass balance through quantitative field observations. Stake farms would be fixed in the above zones and repeated GPR surveys be carried out to observe the nature of bedrock at selected places and to characterize the subsurface layering in the snow / glacier ice. These surveys would also provide information on the thickness and structure of the fast ice around Bharti promontory

datasets.title: Constraining geodynamic evolution of the northern Prince Charles Mountain (NPCM) and the eastern Amery Ice Shelf (EAIS), East Antarctica in relation to the Eastern Ghats Belt (EGB), India using geological and geophysical
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic continent and surrounding oceans are key parts of the Earth's System and can provide vital information on the crustal evolutionary processes operating on the Earth's surface. The basement of Antarctica comprises a suite of crustal blocks that were part of various supercontinents (e.g. Rodinia, Gondwana) and preserves distinct high-grade assemblages. Previous studies suggest that parts of eastern Antarctica and Eastern Ghats Belt (EGB), India were once adjacent to each other in pre-Permian continental reconstructions. Therefore, the terranes of east Antarctica and EGB play a very crucial role in the Rodinia / East Gondwana debate.
datasets.purpose: Characterization of magmatic as well as late Mesoproterozoic-early Neoproterozoic and Pan-African metamorphic events associated with partial melting phenomena using an integrated petrological, geochemical and geochronological approach in the Northern Prince Charles Mountains (NPCM) and East Amery Ice Shelf (EAIS) ? Prydz Bay regions of East Antarctica and Eastern Ghats Belt (EGB), India.Determination of crustal structure and heat flow patterns in the studied terranes the NPCM and EAIS of east Antarctica and EGB of India. Decipher the correlation between East Antarctica and India based on integrated results of geological and geophysical dataset.
datasets.project_name: Constraining geodynamic evolution of the northern Prince Charles Mountain (NPCM) and the eastern Amery Ice Shelf (EAIS), East Antarctica in relation to the Eastern Ghats Belt (EGB), India using geological and geophysical approaches

datasets.title: Paleoenvironmental reconstruction from lake sediments of Larsemann Hills and marine sediments of Prydz Bay: a multi-proxy approach
datasets.abstract: Paleo environmental reconstructions of lake sediments (Larsemann Hills) and marine sediments (Prydz Bay) provide a comprehensive picture of past variations of the environmental conditions. The lake project of NCPOR is one of the main thrust in the 12th five year plan along with envisaging new horizons with Prydz Bay. To understand the past environments, it is very much necessary to understand not only the past variations in climate of Larsemann Hills but also the adjoining region i.e., the Prydz Bay. To date, there is very little multi-proxy high-resolution record of paleo climate variations in the East Antarctic peninsula. Hence, the need of the hour is to obtain such records which would be helpful in understanding the different processes of the climate system that have taken place during the geological past. The paleo climate data obtained would help researchers to model the future climatic scenario for the Antarctic Peninsula.
datasets.purpose: To understand the palelimnology of Larsemann Hill lakes by reconstructing long-term climatic variations. 2. To study the geomorphic evolution of lakes in the Larsemann Hills,3. To understand the paleo-environments of Prydz Bay. 4. To understand the link between the evolution of Antarctic lakes and the marine sediments in Prydz Bay

datasets.title: Environmental Impact Assessment of Anthropogenic Activities at Indian Polar Stations- A local and global perspective.
datasets.abstract: First-order changes in the environment are often most clearly recognized as a physical or chemical change. The addition of a chemical or the destruction of a physical feature is often the first indication that humans have had an impact on the surrounding environment. Physical and chemical perturbations are also often most directly measurable. Researchers recommended that sewage be adequately treated before discharge into the polar environment. The wastewater treatment and waste management are very critical aspects in Antarctica because of cold climatic conditions, energy availability and Environmental Protocol and since adhere to be stringent measures due to pristine continent. The challenges in the wastewater treatment always existed because of the problems in technical expertise, logistics and operation support available in Antarctica compared to the rest of the part of the world.
datasets.purpose: Assessment of wastewater effluent release plume Assessment of Persistent Organic Pollutants (POP?s) in Air and Lake Water

datasets.title: Effect of human intervention on Antarctic Microflora
datasets.abstract: Human activities on the Antarctic environment have resulted in environmental pollution due to the use of fossil fuels and construction materials, the production of wastes, and interactions with landscapes, flora and fauna. Since the microbial populations adapt relatively quickly to their environment, any anthropogenic effect should be easily discernable in terms of changes in the composition and activity of microbial populations. The anthropogenic effect on Antarctic microflora is under-studied. Additionally, it has been difficult to distinguish the occurrence of human-associated bacteria from the anthropogenic effect on indigenous bacteria. To establish a clear link, it would be important to compare the bacterial communities at multiple sites with varying degree of human intervention. Present study will attempt to achieve this goal with both culture-based and molecular methods. Bharati being a new station, there is a greater scope to carry out such study.
datasets.purpose: Isolation and characterization of bacteria in and around Bharati station.Determination of non-culturable bacterial diversity and Comparison of isolated populations to determine the spatio-temporal variation and risk of pathogenesis.

datasets.title: Role of long-range transported aerosols on earth
datasets.abstract: In this proposed project, the continuous real-time observation of aerosol optical and physical properties are going to be monitored during summer-time at Bharati in Antarctica because during this period, aerosols are transported from South America and Australia. The main aim of this project is to find out these long-range transported absorbing aerosols like BC and dust in Antarctica and their radiative effects over bright snow surface. Finally, the perturbation of Earth's radiation budget due to aerosols and their radiative heating rate over Antarctica and their cause will be investigated
datasets.purpose: Quantification of aerosol induced perturbation of Earth's radiation budget over Antarctica during summer using in-situ observation of optico-physical and chemical properties of aerosols.Estimation of vertical distribution of aerosol heating rate and its contribution towards air temperature in summer at Antarctica using optical properties of aerosols.Simulation of radiative heating caused by transported anthropogenic (BC) and natural (desert dust) aerosols and identification of source regions of dust aerosols from isotopic analysis (Sr and Nd)

datasets.title: Long-term monitoring of Wildlife and their habitats in Antarctica and Southern Indian Ocean
datasets.abstract: Climate change impacts ocean biota in different ways and several ocean models have suggested that the Southern Ocean surface waters are going to become warmer and fresher with increased vertical stratification, reduced sea-ice, higher CO2 oceanic concentrations and ultimately increased up welling. Alteration of these ocean properties may affect the primary producers biomass and diversity. This is in turn could have a long lasting impact on oceanic birds and mammals, which are directly or indirectly linked to the availability of primary producers. In this connection, the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) had participated in the 14th, 15th, 16th, 28th and 29th Indian Scientific Expeditions to Antarctica and has implemented a Monitoring Programme entitled ?Developing a Long-term Monitoring Programme for Birds and Mammals in the Indian Ocean and Antarctica?.
datasets.purpose: Investigate the distribution pattern and community structure of birds and mammals in the Southern Ocean and Antarctica. Evaluate and map the wildlife habitats, and to identify threats to wildlife and their habitats Monitor certain key pelagic organisms such as krill and long range movements of species such as penguins and seals using satellite tracking techniques.

datasets.title: Passive acoustic measurements in the shallow waters of Antarctic sea to study ice-flow dynamics
datasets.abstract: Thermal stresses and physical deformation of the iceberg due to wind, current and waves cause the iceberg to fracture and it generates the pressure waves, which propagate into the water column. The collision of iceberg with sea bed also produces prominent acoustic energies that are beneficial for analysing the geophysical events. The frequency range pertaining to the vocalizations of Blue and Fin whales falls at 90 Hz bands. Usually at high altitude areas, the ocean temperature profile is isothermal. With increasing pressure, the sound velocity profile increases linearly with depth. This acoustic phenomenon is well-known as Polar half channel in which the sound waves spread horizontally over a sequence of sea surface reflections.
datasets.purpose: To measure the underwater ambient noise in the shallow waters of Antarctic sea To study the ice flow dynamics such as iceberg quaking, thermal fracturing of sea ice, melting of glaciers and sweeping of ice pellets from the ambient noise measurements of the shallow waters of Antarctic sea. To characterize and classify the marine species such as Blue whales, Fin whales and Seals from the ambient noise measurements of the shallow waters of Antarctic sea.
datasets.project_name: Passive acoustic measurements in the shallow waters of Antarctic sea to study ice-flow dynamics

datasets.title: Relationship between the paragneiss and orthogneiss in the Larsemann Hills, Antarctica
datasets.abstract: (i) Using GSI's large scale maps (1:2,000) of some parts and further detailed observations, syntectonic granites associated with different deformation events would be identified and sampled. (ii) Metapelites that are least affected by later thermal events (for example, orthoquartzite, if available) would be sampled for provenance characterization. To remove the possibility of subsequently grown zircons getting into the original detrital population, a robust screening technique would be used for characterization of each zircon. This would include REE signature, Th/U ratios and selected Hf-isotope characterization. Similar characterization would also be done on known migmatitic melts present in the area. The aim of the screening procedure would be to know the truly detrital zircon population of the metapelites.
datasets.purpose: To determine the antiquity of the paragneiss vis-vis orthogneiss in the Larsemann Hills, Antarctica. To relate and date granite magmatism with major deformation events

datasets.title: Measurement of Radiation Level due to Cosmic Rays and Terrestrial Radiation at and around Bharati Station, Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Under this Project, dose rate measurement of different components of cosmic rays, such as gamma, neutrons and charged particle will be evaluated. Passive dosimeters such as thermoluminescence dosimeter based on CaSO4 Dy, LiF:Mg,Ti, CR-39 under different packing conditions are deployed in and around Bharati and Maitri stations at Antarctica. The dosimeters are deployed for a period of four months every year during the summer expedition of NCAOR and will be processed and analyzed at BARC for dose evaluation. In addition to this, CR-39 solid state detector will be used for purely for neutron dose measurement. In the forthcoming 35th INSEA, it is planned to deploy several on-line gamma and neutron monitoring systems in and around Bharati station for continuous measurement of gamma and neutron dose rate throughout the year. In addition, several portable dose measuring systems will be carried by BARC scientist to measure radiation level outside Bharati station during summer expedition.
datasets.purpose: Measurement of radiation level due to cosmic rays and terrestrial radiation at and around Bharati Station, Antarctica using on-line and passive dosimeters.

datasets.title: Long-term monitoring of Wildlife and its habitats in Antarctica and Southern Indian Ocean
datasets.abstract: Antarctica and its surrounding ocean are at the centre stage of rapid and extreme environmental events due to prevailing global climate change, which in turn necessitates long-term monitoring of wildlife and their habitats in this region. Wildlife Institute of India (WII) has standardised the methods for enumerating wildlife populations, mapping their distribution and studying behaviour of selected species through replicate sampling in the last few expeditions. Based on the results obtained, WII had proposed that such monitoring exercises to be continued for generating long-term ecological data at regular intervals. WII now proposes to continue the monitoring programme in the Southern Indian Ocean and in Antarctica with addition of intensive study of certain species using satellite tracking and genetic analysis. In the next three expeditions, WII will target globally identified indicator species groups in Antarctica for monitoring, habitat assessment along with environmental variables
datasets.purpose: Estimating abundance and distribution of pelagic seabirds in the southern Indian Ocean and Southern Ocean. Assessing distribution and populations parameters of seals and penguins in Larsemann hills (including adjoining Svenner and Bollingen islands). Tracking the movement patterns of Snow Petrels and South Polar Skua for identifying nearby foraging habitats.

datasets.title: Variability of remote sensing reflectance of the waters around Antarctic continent implications to retrieval of chlorophyll-a from an optical sensor for studying biogeochemical cycle in the high latitude waters
datasets.abstract: The study area along the coastal waters are sparsely sampled regions because of the adverse weather condition, navigational hazards, remote location, inhospitable environment, with high sea states driven by strong winds. The evidence from our analysis and earlier reports suggest that Aqua- MODIS derived chlorophyll-a concentration in the Antarctic waters is underestimated significantly, but the reasons for this have remained inconclusive. We propose the following reasons for the observed satellite based underestimation (i) inadequate atmospheric correction, and (ii) Error in the bio-optical algorithm. To make progress in this complex problem, we have hypothesised to consider long-range advection of aerosol into the Antarctic marine atmosphere that is not accounted in the standard atmospheric correction algorithm. The algorithm is thus sensitive to changes in the composition of water constituents particularly in the Antarctic waters which are optically complex due to influx of glacial

Modelling remote sensing reflectance on the basis of specific absorption coefficients of different optically active substances. Validation of modelled values with measured remote sensing reflectance on the basis of remote sensing reflectance derived from in-water radiometer. Development of in-water bio-optical site specific algorithm.

datasets.title: Biogeochemical studies of blue ice regions in coastal East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The largest Blue-ice area (BIA) is located on the Amery Ice Shelf, East Antarctica. A BIA is formed when the snow cover is removed or it sublimates from the surface of the ice. This is especially prevalent in the coastal margins of ice sheets due to the presence of strong katabatic winds. BIAs cover nearly 2% of the Antarctic ice sheet. As the ice surface is free of snow cover, it receives solar radiation which is able to penetrate through the clear blue ice. The rise in temperature creates melt water beneath the surface of blue ice. Presence of debris deposited by wind further increases the temperature and the melt rate of the ice. Therefore availability of sunlight and liquid water creates ?a greenhouse-type environment? which is conducive for microbial production. Microbes residing in the interior of blue ice are mixed with fresh inputs of nutrients and microbes from the melting of debris as well as deposition from the atmosphere. This leads to the creation of a distinct ecosystem.
datasets.purpose: To study the biogeochemical composition of blue ice and its ability to support life. To determine microbial abundance and diversity in blue ice ecosystems

datasets.title: Verify and validate the speculated provenance for the detrital sediments of Prydz Bay through direct geological field and laboratory investigations in the interior of the Princess Elizabeth Land terrain, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: In an ongoing research, the glaciomarine sediments deposited along offshore of PEL are used to reconstruct the geology of this area recovered from ODP (Oceanic Drilling Program) 119 and 188, which were drilled on the continental margins of the PEL. Preliminary results have shown the dominance of garnet at site 740 and 739 (drilled sites of 119). Aluminosilicates, amphibole, pyroxene, ilmenite and iron oxides are the other identified phases in site 740 while site 739 shows the presence of amphibole, chlorite, staurolite, epidote, sphene and feldspar (associated with garnet and amphibole) apart from garnet. A broad range of garnet compositions indicates either multiple provenance sourcing or presence of a polymetamorphic terrain in the source area. Pyrope and almandine are the most dominant varieties in which the population of pyrope is comparatively higher in site 740 sediments.

datasets.abstract: Long-term, multi-disciplinary, multi-institutional initiative to characterizing the radiative, chemical, dynamical and electrodynamical processes themselves and their coupling with the low and equatorial processes, being conceived as a collaborative effort between SPL, NCAOR and Goa University. The experiments would be added in a phased manner, as the infrastructure develops and research matures. The integrated experiment is proposed for a period of five years from 2012. The financial commitment as well as the manpower required for the smooth implementation of the program will be shared between SPL, NCAOR, Goa University and Tripura University.Realizing the potential problems of scientific interest in Polar Regions, this comprehensive proposal includes of studies in two broad areas namely Polar Atmosphere and Polar ionosphere.

datasets.title: Search for Star born, Primordial, and Anthropogenic Radionuclides in Antarctica (SPAR).
datasets.abstract: The aim of the project is to continue interdisciplinary approach to analyse scanty distribution of cosmogenic and supernova produced long-lived radionuclides in Antarctic area. These cosmogenic radionuclides like 7Be, 10Be, 53Mn and the supernova produced radionuclides like 60Fe, 182Hf, 146Sm, etc., are present in the Earth crust in minuscule amount, typically 1 in 1011 to 1 in 1014 level. The measurement of cosmogenic radionuclides 26Al will give relevant information on solar spot, on the solar flux and on recent nucleosynthesis. Measurement of 10Be, 53Mn will give us idea on surface expose dating, i.e., until the rocks were ice-free. The project may unravel some of the intricacies of nature, detection of Supernovae (SN) radionuclides, in realizing galactic drama that occurred millions years before. However, the naturally occurring stable isobars such as 182W, 146Nd are million times more abundant than the SN radionuclides 182Hf or 146Sm and are the main obstacle in such analysis.
datasets.purpose: Interpretation of the exposure of Earth to various stellar processes by tracing the long-lived radionuclides formed by the p-processes in supernova. Application of surface exposure dating (SED) technique to explain various geo-temporal phenomenon. Unfolding human interventions and analysing environmental risk by medium-lived radionuclides and biological proxies. Determination of isotopic anomalies if any in natural decay series. Simplifying the chemistry for the ?work-horse? nuclides 10Be and 26Al
datasets.project_name: Search for Star born, Primordial, and Anthropogenic Radionuclides in Antarctica (SPAR).

datasets.title: Quest for the Meteorites in Grove Mountains area, Prydz Bay, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Thousands of meteorites have been collected from Antarctica since the commencement of organized meteorite search programmes by the Japanese in 1974 and the Americans in 1976. The ANSMET (Antarctic Search for Meteorites) programme has been successful in collecting more than 15000 meteorites from the Trans-Antarctic Mountains. There are two important factors prevailing in Antarctica are responsible for the abundance of meteorites than any other part of the world. First is the extreme low temperature and absence of humidity that allows preservation of meteorites in a nearly unweathered state. Second is the concentration of glacial load along stranding surfaces that takes place when the flow of ice is obstructed by mountain barriers. At such surfaces katabatic winds sublimate the ice cover exposing the load containing meteorites.
datasets.purpose: Systematic search and study for meteorites in the Grove Mountains area, Prydz Bay.

datasets.title: Constraining the retreat and advancement history of East Antarctica Ice Sheet (EAIS) during Late Quaternary using OSL Surface Exposure dating technique in parts of Larsemann Hills area.
datasets.abstract: The Larsemann Hills includes ~50 Km2 of an ice free area of rocky peninsula and islands in Prydz Bay, East Antarctica which predominantly constituted of Proterozoic meta-pelitic cordierite and gneisses (Stuwe et al 1989). In this area, attempts have been made to infer the Late Quaternary Palaeoclimate using multi-proxy datasets from lake sediment cores (Hodgson et al. 2005) and insitu cosmogenic 10Be exposure dating, salt/sediment geochemistry, rock weathering (Kiernan et al. 2009). Nonetheless, interpretations are mainly based on indirect inferences drawn through lake sediment and 14C and OSL chronologies (Gillieson et al. 1990; Hodgson et al. 2001a, 2005 & 2006), radiometric (210Pb and I37Cs), radiocarbon (AMS 14C) and uranium series (238U) methods (Hodgson et al. 2001b). These methods were inconclusive beyond certain temporal resolution. Also, the OSL dating poses obvious restrictions to its application in Antarctic region owing to partially bleached signals.
datasets.purpose: To attempt building up of chronology of glacial advance and retreat through Late Quaternary To assess the credibility of technique in East Antarctica ice free areas. To develop protocols of surface exposure dating by OSL using lithology and depth to time dependent luminescence bleaching profile.
datasets.project_name: Constraining the retreat and advancement history of East Antarctica Ice Sheet (EAIS) during Late Quaternary using OSL Surface Exposure dating technique in parts of Larsemann Hills area.

datasets.title: Constraining geodynamic evolution of Princess Elizabeth Land (PEL), East Antarctica in relation to the Eastern Ghats Belt (EGB), India using geological and geophysical approaches.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic continent and surrounding oceans are key parts of the Earth?s System and can provide vital information on the crustal evolutionary processes operating on the Earth?s surface. The basement of Antarctica comprises a suite of crustal blocks that were part of various supercontinents (e.g., Rodinia, Gondwana) and preserves distinct high-grade assemblages. Previous studies suggest that parts of eastern Antarctica and Eastern Ghats Belt (EGB), India were once adjacent to each other in pre-Permian continental reconstructions. Therefore, the terranes of east Antarctica and EGB play a very crucial role in the Rodinia / East Gondwana correlation. An interdisciplinary approach utilising both igneous/metamorphic petrological studies with geophysical investigations can provide a window into the geodynamic evolution of the region in particular and of the Earth in general.
datasets.purpose: Characterization of magmatic as well as late Mesoproterozoic-early Neoproterozoic and Pan-African metamorphic events associated with partial melting phenomena using an integrated petrological, geochemical and geochronological approach in the Princess Elizabeth Land (PEL) of East Antarctica and Eastern Ghats Belt (EGB), India.
