datasets.title: Monitoring Hydrodynamics of the coastal water of Prydz Bay (Thala Fjord and Quilty Bay)
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic Bottom Water and Antarctic Intermediate Water obtain their fundamental characteristics in the coastal region. It is an important component of the active air-sea exchange in this area that leads to deep convection and production of deep ocean water masses. As compared with the Weddell sea and Ross sea, relatively little is known about the Prydz bay in terms of hydrodynamics.The present studies will try to understand if such physical processes exist in coastal waters Prydz bay namely Thala fjord having connectivity with glaciers and the Quilty bay which is landlocked with no glacier connectivity. The coastal dynamics in the Prydz bay has been poorly understood because of the lack of systematic collection of hydrographic data. Very few historical spatial hydrographic data scattered point and transects are available in this sector.
datasets.purpose: Long term monitoring hydrodynamics of the Prydz bay (Thala Fjord and Quilty Bay). Long term variability of thermohaline structure with special focus on polar front.identification of water mass and mixing characteristics upper-ocean heat and salt content. thickness of fresh water discharges during sea-ice melt and its influence on geostrophic circulation. document and model the evolution of upper ocean thermal structure and heat content changes on annual and inter-annual time scales.Generation of time series hydrographic data bank in coastal regions.

Larsemann Hills in East Antarctica has opened a new vista in glaciological studies with the commissioning of the third permanent research station of India, Bharati in 2012. The Polar ice sheet lying adjacent to the Larsemann Hills is scientifically important as it is bounded by two glaciers, i.e., the Polar?rboken glacier to its west and Dalk glacier to its east with different flow velocities. The Polararboken glacier flows towards west and drains into Publications shelf whereas the Dalk glacier flows towards north and drains directly into the southeast part of Prydz Bay.

datasets.abstract: BARC had participated during Xth Antarctic expedition and carried out measurement on natural radioactivity and gamma ray background. The gamma ray measurement was basically carried out with on line survey meter which measured instantaneous dose rate both due to cosmic rays and terrestrial radiation. During the 29th expedition, background radiation due to cosmic ray was separately carried out based on survey meter as well as passive dosimeter around Maitri. The results shows that the dose rate due to cosmic rays are several times more than that at equator. Besides cosmic ray intensity at poles varies due to solar cycle. In view of the above it is planned to carry out long term measurement of radiation level due to cosmic rays at Antarctica. To have comparison with respect to longitude, it is worth carrying out these measurements at Bharti and Maitri.

datasets.title: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctic Bharati
datasets.abstract: Coastal waters in the last decade is alarming and puzzling the scientific community. The observed sea ice decline is believed to be due to the changes in the polar ocean and atmosphere related to climate change. The modelling efforts to reproduce the polar ocean-ice/snow-atmosphere behavior remain far from realistic. The lack of proper representation of processes active in the air-sea-ice interface, vertical mixing processes is attributed to the weak performance of climate models. Therefore, understanding the physical processes at the Air-Ice-Sea interface in the Polar Regions is essential for understanding the climate changes and their effects in the polar areas and beyond. Furthermore, for better policy making and climate change mitigation plans, a proper monitoring system is required for the polar oceans.

datasets.title: Non-pharmacological intervention to improve the cognition and mood in Antarctic Environment
datasets.abstract: Antarctica is the coldest, windiest, and one of the most dry areas with the highest average altitude on the planet, where photoperiods last as long as six months per year. Long-term stay in this extreme environment may cause significant changes in the health and well-being of individuals. However, human beings are naturally resistant and adaptable to the most varied environmental conditions. Mullin (1960) reported that in Antarctic environment, the most important psychological stresses appear to be the problem of individual adjustment to the group, the more subtly acting, relative "sameness" of the milieu; and the absence of certain accustomed sources of emotional satisfaction. Antarctic environment poses hardship such as narrow spaces, exposure to dangerous situations, social isolation, limitations in communication with the outside world and limited possibilities of evacuation from the environment. This has significant detrimental effects on sleep function, cognitive impairment.
datasets.purpose: To evaluate sleep, cognitive function and mood profile in Antarctic environment. To improve cognitive function and mood by cognitive retraining in Antarctic environment.

The lake project of NCAOR is one of the main thrust in the 12th five year plan along with envisaging new horizons with Prydz Bay. To understand the past environments, it is very much necessary to understand not only the past variations in climate of Larsemann Hills but also the adjoining region i.e., the Prydz Bay.To date, there is very little multi-proxy high-resolution record of paleoclimate variations in the East Antarctic peninsula. Hence, the need of the hour is to obtain such records which would be helpful in understanding the different processes of the climate system that have taken place during the geological past. The paleoclimate data obtained would help researchers to model the future climatic scenario for the Antarctic Peninsula.

datasets.title: Benthic Studies of Kongsfjorden,west coast of Spitsbergen, Svalbard
datasets.abstract: During the course of the proposed study the following specific tasks shall be addressed. 1. Study the macrobenthic faunal composition at selected locations in the Kongsfjorden Fjord covering a length of ~15 Km from the oceanic end to the glacial end of the Fjord along with representative samples for MPB (microphytobenthos) and meiobenthos. 2. Demonstrate the climate change (environmental parameters) if any on species diversity and distribution patterns of benthos in particular the influence of west Spitsbergen current; high-productive Atlantic and ice-covered Arctic waters. 3. Address potential shifts in macrobenthic species composition likely to take place on the sea floor due to changes (e.g. melting of glaciers, siltation, reduction in salinity) and to integrate the short term objectives of the present proposal with the long term objectives of NCAOR relevant to Benthic life. 4. Find out the principal source of organic materials / food supply (e.g. episodic pulses of organic carbon).

datasets.title: Reactive halogen compounds in the Antarctic environment
datasets.abstract: This project aims at investigating the distribution and characterising the effect of reactive halogen species on the oxidative capacity and aerosol formation in the Antarctic and Arctic atmosphere, and through campaign based observations shed light on their fluxes and the process of new particle formation. The aim focus of this year?s observations would be to consolidate data to study the annual cycle at Bharati. Reactive halogen species are important trace gases, which affect the composition of the natural environment through catalytic processes and through new particle formation. In the past, efforts have been made to understand their role in the remote ocean and polar environments; although observations are still rare in the Southern Ocean and considerable uncertainty still exists at the process level. Halogens have been recognised to contribute to as much as 45% of the ozone loss in the remote ocean boundary layer, and cause large-scale ozone depletion events in the polar boundary
datasets.purpose: Ozone depletion by halogen compounds in the troposphere and stratosphere.The oxidising capacity in the Antarctic atmosphere, including HOx and NOx ratio changes. datasets.title: Matching continents: correlating India and Antarctica across the Indian Ocean
datasets.abstract: India and Antarctica were important components of three giant supercontinent configurations, namely Columbia, Rodinia and Gondwana. Several studies have postulated that in many supercontinent assemblies, India and Antarctica were juxtaposed over a geological time period spanning more than 1.5 billion years. The Eastern Ghats Belt bears testimony to the assembly and dispersal of both the Columbia and Rodinia supercontinents, and possibly the formation of East Gondwana. The northern and the southern part of Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt (EGMB) are thought to have been juxtaposed with the eastern coastline of East Antarctica, in particular the Rayner Province, the Rauer Islands and Vestfold Hills. A correlation between the Permo-Triassic Gondwana sediments in the Mahanadi Rift (in peninsular India) and Lambert Rift (East Antarctica) has been postulated but remains contentious.
datasets.purpose: The chief objective is to correlate different domains of the Eastern Ghats Belt with conjugate domains in East Antarctica on the basis of petrological and detailed structural analysis, along with geo-chronological information.
datasets.project_name: Matching continents: correlating India and Antarctica across the Indian Ocean

datasets.title: Paleoclimatic Studies from Antarctic Coastal Areas with special reference to Larsemann Hills based on terrestrial and marine records.
datasets.abstract: With the establishment of the third Indian Antarctic Research Base at Larsemann Hills, a new vista has opened for carrying out multi-proxy geological studies in the region, especially pertaining to Quaternary climatic fluctuations. In climate evolution, the immediate past of Quaternary time period has been documented with key interglacial-glacial variability. During this period, Antarctic region witnessed several environmental periods, viz. changing climatic condition from arid-warm to humid and hence the coastal areas have preserved the history in their sedimentological column. These climatic variations have to be studied from marine and lake-sediment cores by using several proxies to decipher the interference of air-sea-land, which influenced the past climate and have a bearing on the present climatic conditions.

datasets.title: Estimation of be in Polar regions-Paleooceanographic Implications
datasets.abstract: Polar Regions played a decisive role in earth?s climatic changes over the Late Quaternary period due to their fluctuated ice sheet volume. The spatial scale and temporal pattern of these fluctuations are subject to considerable debate. Understanding the response of large ice masses to climatic forcing is of vital importance because ice- of ice sheets and sea ice to act as major heat sinks/insulators. Paleoceanographic conditions inferred from paleoecology using climate proxies in ocean sediments have provided such evidences; however, a clearer picture of past climatic changes is yet to draw by integrating the proxy records with atmospheric data. Beryllium (10Be), a cosmogenic radionuclide can be used successfully to infer past climatic changes of the Polar Regions 1.due to its highest atmospheric production rates at high latitudes because of the weaker shielding of the cosmic ray flux by the Earth?s magnetic field as it imposes a rigidity cut off on cosmic rays.
datasets.purpose: To study spatial and temporal variations in 10Be concentration in marine sediments of higher latitudes (Northern & Southern Hemisphere). To study temporal variation in 10Be concentration in sediment core and comparison of temperature changes occurred during corresponding period as inferred from ice cores. Benthic foraminiferal Mg/Ca ratio to reconstruct Paleotemperature and to constrain the temperature effect contained in foraminiferal δ18O values. Sediment texture and Grain size analysis to study sea level fluctuations (Glacial and interglacial conditions). To study past oceanographic & climatic changes with the help of Trace elements of marine sediments
datasets.project_name: Estimation of be in Polar regions-Paleoceanographic Implications

datasets.title: Study of Long Path Radio Wave Propagation Characteristics and Theoretical Simulation of Ionospheric Perturbations from Indian Antarctic Station Bharati.
datasets.abstract: Antarctica is most certainly the perfect location during summer season (November to February) in southern hemisphere. Prolonged days or nights provide a test bed for verifying theoretical models of how ionization and recombination take place. The effects of lightning and its induced effects which generates natural VLF signal as radio atmospherics (Sferics) can be studied widely from Antarctica. The current project is to extend this observation into a different location (Bharati station, Larsemann hill region) in the Antarctic landmass with latest instruments for data recording. The new location has special properties of absence of Antarctic ice mass which plays is the most responsible agent for attenuation of radio signal ICSP has more than a decade-long experience of data recording and interpretation.

datasets.abstract: Lead has four stable isotopes: 204Pb, 206Pb, 207Pb, 208Pb. 204Pb is a primordial isotope and others viz., 206Pb, 207Pb, and 208Pb are the products of radioactive decomposition of 238U, 235U, and 232Th. The lead isotopic compositional ratio of any geological material is characteristic and is dependent on original lead incorporated during formation, U/Th ratio specific to the rock and geological age of the material. Coals normally contain much less lead (2-10 ppm) even though higher concentration up to 100 ppm have been reported occasionally. The main hosts of lead in coals are galena, Pb, Se, Ba minerals, where Pb replaces Ba (including sulfates, phosphates, and silicates), pyrite and occasional organic associations (Swaine, 1990). As coaly matter is normally devoid of radioactive elements like U

datasets.title: Tracing long-range transport of anthropogenic lead (Pb) to coastal East Antarctica using Pb isotopes and geochemical fingerprinting
datasets.abstract: A total of nine shallow snow cores (up to 1 m in length) were collected on 15 January 2020 during the 39th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (2019?2020) from cDML, East Antarctica. Four cores (S1-S4) were recovered from the Kupol Verbljud (69?52′27.2″ S, 15?55′35.8″ E) and three cores (S5-S7) from Kamelryggen (70?18′47.2″ S, 16?16′32.8″ E) ice rises located in the Lazarev Ice Shelf, while two additional cores (S8-S9) were collected from the Leningradkollen ice rise (70?07′14.84″ S, 12?57′38.8″ E) along the Nivlisen Ice Shelf (Fig. 1). Together, these three ice rises span a coastal transect of approximately 50?130 km across cDML (Fig. 1). Within each ice rise, individual cores were spaced ~10 km apart to capture local- to regional-scale variability in snow accumulation and atmospheric deposition. In addition, two closely spaced cores (S3 and S4; ~1 m apart) were collected to assess spatial reproducibility.
datasets.purpose: This study ensures the collection of 9 snow cores of the same age from three distinct ice rises, Kupol Verbljud, Kamelryggen and Leningradkollen ice rise along the Nivlisen Ice Shelf. This helps in understanding the contrasts in spatial variation of biogeochemical cycling of various chemical species as well as of the factors affecting various proxies brought about by the changes in the surrounding ocean. The coupling of isotope and chemical profiles from three regions will help in understanding various atmospheric and oceanic processes influencing the seasonality of snow chemistry.

datasets.title: Surface Ice Flow Velocity and Tide Retrieval of the Nivlisen Ice Shelf from GPS Observations.
datasets.abstract: Using a Global Positioning System (GPS) receiver, 19 days of continuous GPS data were collected from January 23 to February 10, during the austral summer of 2005, in the frontal zone of Nivlisen ice shelf (NIS) of central Dronning Maud Land (cDML), East Antarctica. GPS data were analyzed to estimate the diurnal and semi-diurnal variations. We constrained the shelf DG GPS site co-ordinates with the base station MAITRI set up at Schirmacher Oasis and nearby International GNNS Service (IGS) stations. The Ice shelf motion in both cases was caused by a combination of ocean tidal effect, wind stress and ocean currents. The estimated horizontal velocity at DG GPS site was 0.72 m/day towards north-north-east with an azimuth of 20.27o. Major constituents of the oceanic tide have been delineated subjecting the hourly time series data (for five days) to Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis. The amplitudes of the diurnal and semi diurnal were ~1.25 m and 0.5 m, respectively.
datasets.purpose: The result showed not only the expected vertical tidal displacement but also a significant variation in the horizontal velocity. The maximum forward velocity occurred about 3-4 hours after the maximum tidal height, a phase relationship that suggests the role of ocean currents also as one of the driving forces for the ice shelf movement. Furthermore, this type of precise observations of diurnal and semi-diurnal tidal constituents can be assimilated in tide models.
datasets.project_name: Surface Ice Flow Velocity and Tide Retrieval of the Nivlisen Ice Shelf from GPS Observations.

datasets.title: Automatic Weather Station at Dakshin Gangotri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Regular observations of the weather parameters are very important for the understanding of Antarctic meteorology. The main difficulty in the collection of continuous weather data over this ice-covered continent is the extremely adverse weather condition experienced. In order to collect continuous weather data, automatic weather stations are established by various countries with the help of satellites. The India Meteorological Department has set up an automatic weather station popularly known as Data Collection Platform (DCP) at Dakshin Gangotri, Antarctica, during the Fifth Indian Scientific Expedition. The weather parameters at each GMT hour are sensed by the system and transmitted to the Meteorological Data Utilization Centre at New Delhi on a real-time basis, through Indian National Satellite INSAT-1B. In this a detailed description of the data collection platform system, the sensors used in the system and the difficulties experienced during the installation of this system.
datasets.purpose: Current understanding of Antarctic atmospheric processes and dynamics suffers from a shortage of meteorological observations from the southern sea ice-belt and the continent itself. Automatic measurement of surface meteorological parameters is, therefore, of particular importance for increasing sparse data coverage in the vast desolate areas of Antarctica, where a well distributed network of manned meteorological stations does not appear practicable. In the last decade, attempts for automatic weather stations were aimed for on-site recording of the data, which could be retrieved from the station during the subsequent summer season. India made similar efforts in the First Expedition itself, when indigenously designed Automatic Recording Weather Station was installed at the Indian Station.
datasets.project_name: Automatic Weather Station at Dakshin Gangotri, Antarctica.

datasets.title: Meteorological Studies at Antarctica During The Period March, 1986 to February, 1987.
datasets.abstract: A permanently manned meteorological observatory was established at the Indian Research Station, Dakshin Gangotri, during the Third Indian Scientific expedition to Antarctica, for continuous recording of meteorological parameters. The observatory is equipped with instruments to monitor the weather systems approaching and affecting the Station. Valuable data has been collected so far and such studies were continued during the period of March, 86 to Feb., 87 also, the results of which are presented in this paper. An automatic weather station (DCP) was also installed during the Fifth Indian Expedition, through which hourly data is being recorded and transmitted on real time basis to New Delhi through Indian National satellite INSAT-1B." The meteorological data collected during the period of the report has also been compared with mean climatological values of some nearby stations.
datasets.purpose: The observatory at Dakshin Gangotri is equipped with autographic instruments for continuous recording of meteorological parameters e.g. surface wind direction and speed, pressure and temperature. It also has the facility for measurement of surface and global radiations, surface ozone and atmospheric electrical potential gradient. Periodic balloon ascents are also taken to obtain vertical profile of upper air temperature, humidity and radiation fluxes. It also has the equipment for the reception of weather charts broadcasts from forecasting offices in the region and the Automatic Picture Transmission (APT) equipment 260 T. V. P. Bhaskara Rao for reception of cloud imageries from the polar orbiting weather satellites.
datasets.project_name: Meteorological Studies at Antarctica During The Period March, 1986 to February, 1987.

datasets.title: The Antarctic Winter as Recorded at Dakshin Gangotri
datasets.abstract: he data tape of the Automatic Weather Recording Station set up by the first expedition was recovered by the second expedition. The station performed well and the entire tape shows valuable and consistent recorded data. The temperature records show progressive cooling with the advance of the Antarctic winter with a minimum recorded temperature of -29? deg C. The wind data is consistent with published results of long term experiments showing winds generally from the South and South East sectors. The maximum wind speed recorded in the 6 months of recording was 85 mph from a southerly direction. Some qualitative explanations are put forward for the observations and the paper concludes with a set of recommendations for future experiments.
datasets.purpose: On the 15th February 1983 a small team from the Second Indian Expedition Contingent landed at Dakshin Gangotri and surveyed the condition of the Automatic Weather Recording Station left behind by the first expedition. The team reported that one of the four guy wires holding the mast had worked loose, causing the mastto tilt considerably to one side. The bins containing the electronics, tape unit and the sealed batteries were undamaged, however, as also the underwater connectors, interconnecting cables and "O" ring seals. The mast was re installed vertically by the team
datasets.project_name: The Antarctic Winter as Recorded at Dakshin Gangotri

datasets.title: Meteorological Studies at Dakshin Gangotri (Antarctica) March 1984 to February 1985.
datasets.abstract: The Third Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica established a permanent meteorological station at Dakshin Gangotri to monitor both surface and upper air parameters. This report contains results of these observations continuously taken at this station for one year. The variations in temperature wind velocity and atmospheric pressure and their influence on different weather systems are discussed. The low pressure systems moving over and around Antarctica carry warm and moist air whereas ridges draw in cold air. Significant fluctuations in temperature pressure and wind speed have been noticed in moving weather systems.
datasets.purpose: The weather of Antarctica influences the global weather to a great extent. The study of meteorological parameters over Antarctica and their correlation with Indian weather will help in understanding important weather systems. The unique nature of the Antarctic atmosphere, the uniformity of physical structure of snow surface and frequent weather changes are important for the study of meteorological theories.

datasets.title: Mochou Lake Organic and Inorganic Data - 28,000 years
datasets.abstract: This dataset comprises multiproxy paleolimnological and sedimentological records obtained from Mochou Lake, a coastal freshwater lake located in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica. Sediment core samples were collected to reconstruct past environmental and climatic changes and to investigate the response of Antarctic lake ecosystems to Holocene deglaciation, meltwater dynamics, and regional climate variability. The dataset includes stratigraphic descriptions, chronological information, geochemical measurements, stable isotope compositions, and biological proxy records generated from sediment core samples. Analyses were conducted using standard laboratory procedures to determine variations in sediment composition, organic matter sources, lake productivity, and catchment processes through time. datasets.title: Atmospheric Impact of Long-Range Aerosol Transport over the Arctic (Alta)
datasets.abstract: The Arctic is a particularly sensitive region to global climate change. In this context, there is an increased need in understanding the role of atmospheric aerosols in changing the snow Albedo, phenomenon like ?Arctic haze? and ?thinning of Arctic Sea? and perturbation to the radiation balance in the Arctic region. A more realistic evaluation of these changes is possible when long term measurements are made available from remote Arctic locations. It is important to note that while air pollution in most heavily populated areas of the world comes predominantly from local and regional emissions, pollution in the remote Arctic is primarily a result of long-range transport from source regions outside the Arctic.The strong anthropogenic influence over the Arctic Region is primarily due to the position of the Arctic polar front and presence of human population in Europe, North America and North Asia located north of polar front. In addition, the feedback and coupling between the Arctic.

datasets.title: Monitoring of Icebergs in Antarctic Waters and A Note on the Secular Movement of Dakshin Gangotri Glacier.
datasets.abstract: Iceberg monitoring in the Antarctic waters, during onward and return cruise of Ninth Indian Antarctic Expedition, has revealed concentration of icebergs in two well defined zones separated by an iceberg free zone, in between. Distribution pattern and the analyses of size-shape parameters of these icebergs have shown that the majority of large sized (> 500m), tabular icebergs are concentrated in the area close to the Antarctic coastline as compared to the pinnacled and/or disintegrating icebergs (of < 500 m class) which show relative abundance between the S 51 ? and S 60? latitudes. A marked similarity in the distribution patterns of the icebergs during successive voyages has been noticed. Monitoring of the snout of Dakshin Gangotri glacier during austral summer of 1991 and its comparison with the results of earlier studies reveals minor oscillation of the frontal part of snout and the proglacial lake at the foot of this snout.
datasets.purpose: Large blocks of ice, calved from the ice shelf or derived from the glacier tongues are termed as icebergs. As per an estimate, nearly 5000 icebergs of varying dimensions are produced annually in Antarctica. Those of the icebergs which are not grounded, float in the southern ocean waters, governed by the circumpolar currents and the strong Antarctic wind patterns, causing navigational hazards. Monitoring of the icebergs visually and by satellite imagery has become an integral part of glaciological studies as this provides an important input to the overall mass balanee studies of Antarctic icesheet. Iceberg monitoring was carried out during the onward and return voyages of the Ninth Indian Antarctic Expedition as per the guidelines of Norsk Polar Institute (Norwegian Polar Research Institute). It included recording of location, dimensional aspects like size, shape, tilt etc. and the study of morphological characteristics of icebergs encountered along the cruise.

datasets.title: Epiphytic Algae On The Bryophytes Of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The epiphytic algae on the bryophytes of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica, are taxonomically investigated, and sixteen algal species are recognized including ten species of blue?green algae dominated by the species of Nostoc, three species of green algae, a xantho- phycean alga and two diatoms. The occurrence of algae on different bryophytes is dependent on water-holding capacity of the bryophytes and sometimes nutrient enrichment in nearby lands through the excretion of resting sea birds. Thus, the bryophyte colonies in Broknes Peninsula, Fisher and Solomon Islands have rich and diverse epiphytic algal populations among the 18 study sites. The present study not only widens our knowledge on polar algal distribution, but can also be preferred as ?model? environment for the further studies of plant-adaptive strategies
datasets.purpose: Bryophytes and lichens being the most adaptive plants in the extremely harsh climatic conditions of Antarctica play a pivotal role in the composition of polar ecosystem by providing a suitable ambiance for colonization of algae in both extra and intracellular regions for nitrogen fixation activity to the vegetation. This colonization also helps the microscopic organisms to thrive in extreme weathers. The wind is the main dispersing agent of algal spores from nearby aquatic or terrestrial habitats to the bryophyte colonies, and sometimes birds also help in spore dispersal. The colonization occurs mostly near the rhizoids and the axial area or sometimes on the leaf surfaces, but during unfavorable conditions, the heterocystous cyanobacteria thrive near the shoot spices. Sometimes, algae specifically cyanobacteria colonize within the hyaline leaf cells through pores which help them in withstanding unfavorable pH.
datasets.project_name: Epiphytic Algae On The Bryophytes Of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica

datasets.title: Pup Lagoon, Larsemann Hills: Grain Size Data
datasets.abstract: Grain size distribution data were generated from sediment core samples collected from Pup Lagoon in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica, during the Indian Antarctic Expedition. The dataset includes measurements of sediment particle size fractions that characterize sediment texture and depositional conditions within the lagoon basin. Grain size analysis provides insights into sediment transport processes, catchment dynamics, and variations in depositional energy. These data contribute to understanding sedimentary processes and environmental variability in Antarctic coastal lake systems and provide valuable information for paleoenvironmental reconstruction in the Larsemann Hills region.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of generating grain size data from the Pup Lagoon sediment core is to investigate past sedimentary processes and environmental changes in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica. Variations in grain size distribution help identify changes in sediment sources, transport mechanisms, and depositional energy through time. The dataset supports paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate research by providing sedimentological evidence to interpret past hydrological and climatic variability in Antarctic lagoon systems and contributes to broader studies of environmental change in polar coastal regions.

datasets.title: Spatial distribution and phylogenetic studies of selected ice-dwelling calanoid copepods in Larsemann Hills, Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Sea ice is a structurally heterogeneous habitat consisting of an ice-crystal matrix interspersed with a complex array of brine channel and pockets. The sea ice cover plays an important role in structuring marine habitats of polar oceans. It serves as a habitat for some flora and fauna. The sea ice community consists mainly of bacterial, algae, fungi, protozoans and metazoans, including sympagic (ice-dwelling) calanoid copepods.Calanoid copepods are very common in the sea ice layer of Eastern Antarctica. So far about 6 species of calanoid copepods have been reported from the whole Antarctica region and no detailed report are available from Larsemann Hills. Moreover, the detailed study on their life cycle stages and distribution pattern has not been done in Eastern Antarctica in general and Larsemann Hills in particular. Calanoid are in important connecting link in the complex food web existing in Antarctica.
datasets.purpose: 1. To investigate the distribution and life cycle stages of calanoid copepods within platelets ice layers, and thus to broaden knowledge on their biogeography.
datasets.project_name: Spatial distribution and phylogenetic studies of selected ice-dwelling calanoid copepods in Larsemann Hills, Antarctica

datasets.title: New distributional record of Obelia longissima (Pallas, 1766) from Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The benthic hydroid Obelia longissima (Pallas, 1766), earlier known from western peninsular region of Antarctica has been described for the first time from Easther Island of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica.
datasets.purpose: The Larsemann Hills is the second largest of the four major ice- free oases of Antarctica 1. It is spread across a 50 km 2 stretch located between the Vest fold Hills and the Amery Ice Shelf on the south-eastern coast of Princess Elizabeth land, East Antarctica in the Prydz Bay region. It is bordered from two sides by two peninsulas, Broknes and Stornes and several small islands. Hydrozoans are small, bushy, sessile, feather- like colonies, composed of numerous interconnected small polyps, sometimes confused with seaweeds due to their appearance. An estimate puts the species count to about 260 hydrozoan species that occur in Antarctica 2 , usually benthic adhering to various substrata like boulders, pebbles, sand, shells and algae. During the 35th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (INSEA), authors came across a specimen of genus Obelia intermingled with marine alga from Easther Island and a subsequent morphotaxonomic study and literature.
datasets.project_name: New distributional record of Obelia longissima (Pallas, 1766) from Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica

datasets.title: Chroococcidiopsis, A Cryptoendolithic Cyanobacterium From Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Cryptoendolithic microbial communities represent a significant micro ecosystem in Antarctica. Lichens, fungi and algae are the integral components of this bio me. In the present communication a cryptoendolithic cyanobacterium, Chroococcidiopsis is reported from the bed rock of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica.
datasets.purpose: Cyanobacteria are the extreme-tolerant microorganisms growing on every light-exposed niche in the harshest environment of Antarctica. They not only form slimy benthic bio-films in the aquatic habitats but also colonize on the soil and rock surfaces and sometimes refuge within the rocks, called as endoliths. This high degree of plasticity in the cyanobacteria life style is promoted by low amount of available substrata, extreme climatic conditions and the short period favorable for growth in Antarctica (Hawksworth, 2005). These microorganisms prefer the inside of rocks rather than their surfaces, because of the wide thermal fluctuation on the exposed surfaces leading to their sterility for microbes, while the stable nano-climatic conditions within the rock provide a much suitable ambience (Nienow & Friedmann, 1993; de los Rios & al., 2003). The endolithic colonization can be viewed as a stress avoidance strategy, where overlying mineral substrate provides efficient protection from letha.
datasets.project_name: Chroococcidiopsis, A Cryptoendolithic Cyanobacterium From Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica

datasets.title: Diversity Of Bryophytes Of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Nine taxa of Bryophytes belonging to seven genera and four families have been described from Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica. Of these Guembelia longirostris (Hook.) Ochrya & Zarnowiec is reported here for the first time from the East Antarctica and two species viz. Bryum argenetum Hedw. var. argenetum, B.argenetum Hedw. var. muticum Brid. are recorded for the first time from the Larsemann Hills. The same have been described and illustrated along with a key to species and their distribution, habitats and associates have been also provided.
datasets.purpose: The Larsemann Hills (69?20′?69?30′S and 76?55′?76?30′E), is an ice-free coastal oasis of 40 km 2 , located approximately halfway between the Vest fold Hill sand the Amery Ice Shelf on the South-eastern coast of Pry dz Bay, Princess Elizabeth land, East Antarctica, bordered by two main Peninsulas, Broknes and Stornes Peninsula and several islands with exposed rock and low rolling hills containing hundreds of fresh water lakes supports rich growth of Bryophytes as because of their relative lack of cuticle, absorb water and nutrients through the general surface of their plant body. The terrestrial habitats of Larsemann Hills is mostly colonized by the thallophytes and dominated by mosses. To thrive in the harshest environment they develop various biochemical, physiological and morphological mechanisms.

datasets.title: Chemical characteristics of cryoconite holes and snow in Larsemann Hills, Antarctica over the melt season
datasets.abstract: During the 36th ISEA, to understand how the biogeochemistry of cryoconite holes varies through a melt season in coastal Antarctica, cryoconite holes subjected to different light conditions were monitored during the melt period. Mesocosm experiments were also conducted with snow and cryoconite holes to understand the impact of photochemical and microbial activities on dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and ionic constituents in these environments. Chemical analysis (DOC, carboxylate ion and major ion concentration) was carried out on the samples retrieved at the beginning and at the end of both the experiments. Both photochemical and microbial processes resulted in changing the biogeochemical characteristics in these environments. Therefore, consequences of these combined processes would determine the cycling of DOC and nutrients in the Antarctic supraglacial environments.
datasets.purpose: The dataset generated provides an insight on how physical, geochemical and biological changes to glaciers as a result of rapid climate change in this region could influence the composition of the DOC pool and its susceptibility to photochemical and microbial transformation.

datasets.title: Heart Lake/Stepped Lake: Diatom Data
datasets.abstract: Diatom assemblage data were generated from sediment core samples collected from Stepped Lake in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica, during the Indian Antarctic Expedition. The dataset includes taxonomic identification and relative abundance of diatom species preserved in lake sediments. Diatoms are sensitive indicators of environmental conditions such as salinity, nutrient status, and hydrological changes. The data provide valuable information for reconstructing past limnological and climatic variability in Antarctic lake systems and contribute to paleoenvironmental studies aimed at understanding environmental change in the Larsemann Hills region.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of generating diatom data from the Stepped Lake sediment core is to reconstruct past environmental and hydrological conditions in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica. Changes in diatom assemblages help infer variations in lake water chemistry, salinity, and lake level through time. This dataset supports paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate research by providing biological indicators of environmental change and contributes to understanding long-term ecological responses of Antarctic lake ecosystems to climatic variability.

datasets.title: LH73 Environmental magnetism and Geochemistry data Larsemann Hills
datasets.abstract: Coastal ice-free oases in East Antarctica served as biological refugia during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM). However, the processes that sustained lake ecosystems under extreme cold and limited hydrological connectivity remain understudied. Here we show that a 29 kyr sediment record from Lake LH73, East Antarctica, reveals shifts in sediment transport pathways and ecological impacts, using grain-size end-member modelling, environmental magnetism, and geochemical proxies.

datasets.title: Guembelia longirostris (Grammiaceae, Bryophyta) an addition to the bryoflora of East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Guembelia longirostris (Hook.) Ochyra & Zamowiec earlier poorly known by a single collection from West Antarctic peninsular region has been described for the first time from Broknes Peninsula of Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica. The species is characterize by a small central strand of stem, ovate-lanceolate leaves, weakly keeled distally, margins recurved, with a long hyaline hair-point at apex and costa semi-elliptic to reniform in transverse section, U-shaped, bistratose at distal half and unistratose toward the costa and median as well as basal leaf cells with distinctly thickened, sinuate-nodulose longitudinal walls.

Brid., Sarconeurum glacial (M?ll. Hal.) datasets.title: LH73, Larsemann Hills: Diatom & Grain Size Data
datasets.abstract: Diatom assemblage, magnetic susceptibility, and grain size data were generated from sediment core samples collected from LH73 Lake in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica, during the Indian Antarctic Expedition. The dataset includes taxonomic identification and relative abundance of diatoms, measurements of magnetic susceptibility, and particle size distribution of sediments. These proxies provide complementary information on lake productivity, sediment sources, and depositional processes. The combined dataset offers insights into past limnological conditions and environmental variability in Antarctic lake systems and contributes to paleoenvironmental reconstruction in the Larsemann Hills region.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of generating diatom, magnetic susceptibility, and grain size data from the LH73 Lake sediment core is to reconstruct past environmental and hydrological changes in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica. Diatom assemblages provide information on ecological and water chemistry variations, magnetic susceptibility reflects changes in mineral input and sediment sources, and grain size data indicate shifts in sediment transport and depositional energy. Together, these datasets support multidisciplinary paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate studies aimed at understanding long-term environmental variability in Antarctic lake ecosystems.

datasets.abstract: The proposed project is submitted to investigate the water quality of freshwater habitats (Lake, pools and Streams) with reference to biodiversity in the various habitats, planktonic density, their assemblage and habitat preference vis-?-vis environmental change with the hypothesis that there will be high variation in water quality as compared to the previous records. It is also hypothesized that due to elevation in the environmental temperature and climatic change, variation would be observed in the biodiversity as well as in their assemblage or preference to a specific habitat.To achieve the objectives and to confirm the hypothesis abiotic and biotic samples will be collected from the aquatic habitats (Lake, pools and streams). For limnological studies some of the parameter such as temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, and total dissolved solids will be carried out in the field whereas for others parameters (alkalinity, Hardness, Chloride, nitrate, phosphate, etc.)

datasets.title: New Distributional Record Of Two Marine Macro-Algae From Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Macro-algae (Seaweeds) are important component of Antarctic marine sub tidal assemblages. They are not only the principal primary producers but also are nutrient source for aquatic and terrestrial herbivores of this extreme region. Two marine algal species Callophyllis variegata (Rhodophyta) and Durvillaea Antarctica (Phaeophyta) are recorded as new distributional records from Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica which have high economic value.
datasets.purpose: The Larsemann Hills is a 50 km 2 stretch ice-free coastal oasis, second largest of only four major ice-free oases of Antarctica, located between the Vest fold Hills and the Amery Ice Shelf on the South-eastern coast of Prydz Bay, Princess Elizabeth land, East Antarctica, bordered by two main Peninsula, Broknes and Stornes. Several Islands of varying dimensions and some unnamed promontories are present between these two peninsulas. Persistent katabatic winds blow from north-west direction during summer days which contribute to high rates of sea ice formation resulting in the formation of very dense Antarctic bottom water. This pushes the Southern Ocean?s nutrient rich water towards the surface, helping to create high primary productivity in Antarctic waters (Griffiths, 2010). Algae predominate in the bio me of Antarctica comprising of mostly cryptograms due to their ability of abiotic stress tolerance (Vincent, 1988).
datasets.project_name: New Distributional Record Of Two Marine Macro-Algae From Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica.

datasets.title: Long term environmental monitoring and impact assessment studies at Indian Scientific Base, Maitri & upcoming new Indian Scientific Base, Larsemann Hills over East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Antarctica is the coldest continent on the earth. The Indian Ocean, Pacific Ocean and Atlantic Ocean surround the continent. Antarctic continent covers 10% of the earth surface and has a surface area of nearly 14 million square kilometer. It also has 70% of the world?s fresh water resources in the form of ice sheets. The whole continent (almost) 98% is covered by thick ice sheets. As a result of the environmental conditions, the remaining (~ 2%) portion without ice cover is basically the barren soil and rocks.Antarctica continent is endowed with the harshest climate on earth. The coldest temperature recorded in the Antarctica was ?90?C at Vostok Station (in the year 1983). The mean temperature in Antarctica lies between ?20?C to ?30?C on the coast of Antarctica and ?40?C to ?90?C in the interior of Antarctica. The Antarctica environment in addition to extreme cold is also full of ultraviolet rays during the summer period.
datasets.purpose: The main aim of the proposed work is to carry out a detailed long term environmental monitoring and environmental impact assessment studies at the existing Indian Scientific Base, Maitri, and also at upcoming new Indian Scientific Base, Larsemann Hills in east Antarctic during 29th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica.

datasets.title: Study of Algal Diversity of Larsemann Hills, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Algae are ubiquitous, a multitude of species ranging from microscopic to gigantic kelp inhabit the world?s oceans, freshwater bodies, soils, rocks, trees, etc. and are responsible for most of the global production of organic matter by photosynthesis. Thus, they play a fundamental role in the world?s ecosystem and their kaleidoscopic diversity, systematic and phylogeny is indispensable. The Larsemann Hills is an ice-free area of about 50 Km 2 located approximately halfway between Vest fold Hills and Amery Ice shelf on South-eastern coast of Prydz Bay. Continuous human activity in Larsemann Hills is promoted by the coastal location, ice free landscape, the further scientific research, and the potential for tourist visits may affect the algal diversity. The Antarctic climate/environment is highly susceptible to the impact of human activities and has much less natural ability to recover from disturbance than the environment of other continent.

This study assesses climate change impacts on the Larsemann Hills region of East Antarctica through measurements of accumulation, ice velocity, and surface mass balance (SMB). An expanded stake network increased the monitored area from ~220 km? to 24,000 km?, enabling improved evaluation of ice-sheet dynamics.

datasets.title: Colonization Of Algae And Cyanobacteria On Calcareous Remains Of Dead Animals In Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The Larsemann Hills is an ice-free coastal oasis of 50 km 2 , located approximately halfway between the Vest fold Hills and the Amery Ice Shelf on the southeastern coast of Pry dz Bay, Princess Elizabeth land, East Antarctica, bordered by two main peninsulas, Broknes and Stornes and several islands. It is the second largest of only four major ice-free oases. A congenial micro climate along with ade-quate freshwater during summer provide a hospitable environment for the aquatic as well as terrestrial biota. The major temperature-regulating factor is the per-sistent katabatic winds blowing from the northwest direction during summer, which increase the air temperature to 8?10oC with mean monthly temperature slightly above 0oC, which plays a significant role in the distribution and diversity of various flora and fauna. Cyanobacteria and certain algae are primary components of aquatic and terrestrial bio mes of Antarctica 1 .

datasets.title: Study of Solar-Terrestrial Interaction Based on Magnetic Field Observations from Bharati Station, Larsemann Hills, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Various dynamic processes in the near-Earth space environment, driven by the transient solar activity, severely affect the high latitude regions. Magnetic field data collected at globally distributed observatories have been an important tool for the study of manifestations of solar-terrestrial interaction in different regions of the Earth. A newly commissioned Indian Antarctic station, Bharati located at corrected geomagnetic (CGM) coordinates 74.7? S and 97.2? E is well suited for the study of several polar region specific processes associated with solar-terrestrial interaction. Around 20 days magnetic field variations recorded at Bharati during the austral summer months of XXVI and XXVII Indian Scientific Expeditions to Antarctic (ISEA), form the basis for this study. Initial results of polar geomagnetic substorms and long period geomagnetic pulsation characteristics have been presented in this study.
datasets.purpose: In this study we carry out a detailed analysis of about 20 days geomagnetic disturbance data collected at Bharati station (geographic location 69.4? S, 76.2? E) during the summer season of XXVI (Mar 2006) and XXVII (Feb - March 2007) ISEA. A digital fluxgate magnetometer (DFM) was operated to record variations of three orthogonal components (H in magnetic north-south, D in east-west and Z vertically upward) of the geomagnetic field.
datasets.project_name: Study of Solar-Terrestrial Interaction Based on Magnetic Field Observations from Bharati Station, Larsemann Hills, Antarctica.

datasets.title: Investigating the India Antarctic connection through paleomagnetism and geochronology of the Vestfold Hills dykes
datasets.abstract: This proposal is aimed at addressing the specific problem of evaluating the possibility of the 2.37 and 1.9 Ga dykes in Dharwar craton as part of this large radiating dyke swarm. This hypothesis is intended to be addressed through field and laboratory studies. The field work will be carried out at Vestfold Hills region during the 34 ISEA to i) identify and understand geological relationship of different dyke swarms on the basis of trend and intersecting nature, ii) collect oriented hand samples suitable for paleomagnetic studies, iii) one representative sample from each dyke set for Ar- Ar age dating. The samples will be drilled into 1 diameter specimens for paleomagnetic measurements using spin magnetometers. The measurements will be made after each step of thermal heating till the samples are completely demagnetized. One representative sample each will also be subjected to thermomagnetic analysis and Curie temperature test. Magnetic Mineralogy will also be evaluated microscopically.
datasets.purpose: To understand India Antarctic linkage during Paleoproterozoic through correlation of radiating dyke swarms in the eastern Dharwar in India and Vestfold Hills in Larsemann Hills region.
datasets.project_name: Investigating the India Antarctic connection through paleomagnetism and geochronology of the Vestfold Hills dykes

datasets.title: Study of melt/freeze dynamics in Antarctica and sea-ice characterization using space based and ground based observations
datasets.abstract: Understanding the behaviour of ice sheet/ice shelf is necessary to know their response to climate change. Changes have been observed in the recent past which resulted in the breaking of ice shelves from the continent. There is an observed variation in the deposition of snow over sheet ice. Variations in density and wetness are observed with depth, which are functions of topography, distance from sea, climate conditions etc. Active and passive microwave data have been used by researchers to get the spatial distribution of melt over the continent. Satellite data is also being used to derive geophysical parameters of snow/ice. A different response from ice/snow to scatterometer was observed over the years and different places, which needs validation. Ground based information about different snow pack properties play a vital role in calibrating the satellite data over the continent.
datasets.purpose: Collection of snow density, wetness, temperature, melt freeze status at alternate day interval on the accessible polar ice near Bharati station from November onwards to understand spatio ? temporal variations in the snow properties over sheet ice. . Profiling over sea ice to measure thickness and correlating with satellite data.. To monitor the ice shelves for their melt/freeze status with detailed study of Amery shelf and shelf near Maitri.. To collect snow characteristics at Antarctica which include melt / freeze status, snow density, temperature, depth, liquid water content, etc., using GPR, snow fork at few accessible field locations in order to understand/verify the variations in backscatter response and to correlate with field conditions.

datasets.title: Hydrodynamics of the Indian Ocean sector of coastal Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The report addresses preliminary results from the temperature and salinity profiles recorded by using XCTD probes deployed along the ship track from Prydz bay (68.69S, 75.29E) to India bay (69.26S, 12.94E) during the 28th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica. In the Prydz bay region, cold Antarctic Surface Water sinks to deeper depth near 70E. This region is dominated by closed cyclonic gyre adjacent to the Amery Ice Shelf. Being a closed circulation, there is inflow of cold water from the east near the West Ice Shelf and outflow near Cape Darnley and due to its confined nature waters tend to be more salty in this region. In the India Bay region, high salinity is encountered with salinity range of 34.5 and above in regions where Circumpolar Deep Water is present.
datasets.purpose: The major objectives of this study are to (1) study interannual variability in thermohaline changes during the austral summer, (2) quantify the thickness of melt water associated with melting of ice, (3) identify the water masses to characterize mix-ing, and (4) quantify the heat and salt content of the ocean. We attempt to address these by deploying expendable temperature, conductivity and depth probes (XCTDs) along the ship route between Prydz bay and India bay.
datasets.project_name: Hydrodynamics of the Indian Ocean sector of coastal Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Geophysical Studies in Polar Regions
datasets.abstract: A magnetic substorm is a short duration disturbance for a period of one to few hours in the earth's magnetosphere mainly at high latitudes. It is characterized by an explosive energy released from the magnetotail in the form of energetic particles (~5-50 KeV) and strong plasma flows (~100-1000 km/s or so) in the nightside region (Lakhina et al., 2008).Measurements of total magnetic field at Maitri in campaigns and by IGRF model had indicated large decline in magnetic field (~ 110 nT/yr) at Maitri during the last few decades. This decline seems to reduce as one moves away from this station. Continuous monitoring of total magnetic field at Maitri has, however, revealed that the decline has been smaller during the last seven years (~65 nT/y). It is not known how the total field behaves at other places within Antarctica. It is therefore important to monitor the spatial dependence of declining magnetic field by operating the PPM at a few locations in the Antarctic.
datasets.purpose: To determine the substorm onset and location from Antarctic observations. Finding the time delay in substorm onset at Maitri and Bharati. Finding the extent of the substorm and the possible responsible parameters. Examine the auroral westward electrojet at Maitri and Bharati using Magnetometer data. To examine the consequence of interplanetary conditions on the Auroral Substorm Absorption (ASA) events over sub-auroral latitude.Study of substorm associated dayside CNA and simultaneous pc5 pulsations in geomagnetic field variations.To identify the global signatures in atmospheric electrical parameters and distinguish atmospheric, ionospheric and magnetospheric signatures in the surface electrical parameters with the goal of evaluating the electrical response of the atmosphere to magnetospheric influences.To monitor the declining strength of the total magnetic Field F observed over the last few decades in the Southern Hemisphere, especially over the Antarctic continent.
datasets.project_name: Geophysical Studies in Polar Regions
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Antarctic Biodiversity: Past and Present
datasets.abstract: Antarctica is characterized by its unique geographical and climatic isolation. The extreme climate has led to the evolution of novel biochemical adaptations. These adaptations in Antarctic microbes may provide useful compounds for use in the biotechnology industry such as cold-tolerant enzymes and antimicrobial compounds. Since only a small fraction of the true microbial diversity in natural environments has been observed and even less has been cultivated, therefore; there is need of assess the use of cultivation; versus molecular methods to describe the biodiversity, phylogeny and bioprospecting of Sediment cores and Ice cores for the different types of microorganisms present (e.g. Bacteria, cyanobacteria, fungi, etc).
datasets.purpose: Although much is known of the microbes that inhabit in surface soils of Schirmacher oasis, Larsemann Hills and other areas of Antarctica, but there is fragmentary of data about the microbes that inhabit sediment cores, and Ice cores. This offers a unique opportunity to analyze data on diversity of pristine biotopes, molecular phylogeny, and bioprospecting.
datasets.project_name: Microbial biodiversity, phylogeny and Bioprospecting of Sediment & Ice cores of East Antarctica.

datasets.title: Geophysical Studies in Polar Regions
datasets.abstract: A magnetic substorm is a short duration disturbance for a period of one to few hours in the earth?s magnetosphere mainly at high latitudes. It is characterized by an explosive energy released from the magnetotail in the form of energetic particles (~5-50 KeV) and strong plasma flows (~100- 1000 km/s or so) in the night side region (Lakhina et al., 2008). It could be visibly seen as sudden brightening and increased movement of auroral arcs in night side. Auroral zone is the region where most aurorae occur, which is typically 3? to 6? in latitudinal extent and typically 15? to 20? from the magnetic pole defined by the axis of the Earth's magnetic dipole. The study of the high latitude magnetospheric physics is incomplete without delineating the various characteristics of substorms. Extensive studies have been carried out to understand the onset timing and location of the substorm.
datasets.purpose: To determine the substorm onset and location from Antarctic observations. Finding the extent of the substorm and the possible responsible parameters

datasets.title: Provenance and depositional environment of lake sediments from Larsemann Hills area and Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica vis-a-vis geochemistry, heavy minerals and sedimentology
datasets.abstract: Enrichment of a given element in any sediment may be affected by a variety of environmental factors. One of the most important factors affecting the exchange of dissolved substances between sediment and water in lakes is the redox potential gradient in the system. The mobility of Fe and Mn is known to be redox driven and so it can be used to reflect general conditions for soil development. When soil development is weak, the soil redox remains at a relatively high level and Fe and Mn are present in the form of insoluble oxides (Fe3+ and Mn4+). When soil development improves, the soil redox is gradually lowered and they are reduced to soluble Fe2+ and Mn2+ entering the lake via soil water. Fe and Mn can also be used to indicate the redox condition of the lake water. When the lake is well oxygenated, Fe and Mn are present in the form of insoluble oxides and hence are readily incorporated into the sediment.

datasets.title: Satellite-based DEM for monitoring Antarctic ice topography, with a special focus on glaciers
datasets.abstract: The cryosphere plays a central role in the Earth's radiation due to the presence of ice and snow. Its glossy surface reflects much of the incoming solar radiation, which regulates the air-sea heat budget. Increasingly sophisticated satellite technology in the last several decades has enabled researchers to monitor the cryosphere on a routine basis. The recent findings in elevation changes at Antarctic evidently show the crucial need for more cryospheric data and research. This project will focus on the generation of accurate DEMs and velocity maps of glaciers nearby Schirmacher Oasis near Maitri station and Larsemann Hills near Bharati station region using Cartosat, ICES at, INSAR and ground GPS values.

datasets.title: Antarctica Glacier/ Sea Ice Motion tracking by using soft computing techniques
datasets.abstract: The primary objective of this project is to go for vital study on the tracking of Antarctica glacier/ sea-ice motion using image analysis techniques. This study may be useful in maintaining the ice sheet mass balance and changes in ice dynamics. This also can be used for measuring the ice motion, tidal flexure, glacier / sea-ice acceleration, surface drawdown, etc. The proposed project?s work flow follows some major steps including, pre-processing, mosaicking and error estimation. The pre-processing step includes the correction of radiometric and geometric correction of SAR images captured in different days. Radiometric correction is to avoid radiometric errors or distortions, while geometric correction is to remove geometric distortion. In the proposed scheme some image analysis scheme with edge preserving spatio-contextual image enhancement and restoration techniques will be followed to make it viable for mosaicking step.
datasets.purpose: The primary objective of this proposal is to investigate and analyse, both theoretically and experimentally to devise some interfacing tools to provide a vital study on the tracking of Antarctica glacier / sea-ice motion using soft computing techniques.

datasets.title: Assessment of Polar Ice Dynamics Using Remote Sensing Data and In-situ Observations.
datasets.abstract: Global climate change remains a topic of concern over last few decades. Most of the global climate models predict the increase in Earth?s surface temperature with much larger increase over the polar regions. This is also supported by the evidence that the polar ice cover is thinning as well as shrinking. The polar regions, through their sea ice cover, ice sheets, and deep-water formation/ventilation sites, have the potential to influence global atmospheric and oceanic circulations. This demands constant monitoring and modeling of polar ice dynamics and thermodynamics. The only way of the continuous monitoring of these icy regions having harsh and remote conditions is the use of remote sensing. The present study is a part of our long term programme which is oriented towards the monitoring and assessment of ice dynamics in the parts of East Antarctica, covering Indian Antarctic Stations Maitri and Bharati including area nearby Amery Ice Shelf-Lambert Glacier system.
datasets.purpose: The major objective of the polar ice dynamics and mass balance study can be sub-divided suitably into following components, encompassing in-situ data collection of the polar regions by participating in the Antarctic expeditions Ice sheet/ice-shelf energy and mass balance studies (i) Define changes in the ice margin and surface characteristics and (ii) Measure the changes in energy and mass balance components. Sea Ice dynamics and thermodynamics studies (i) Estimation and assessment of sea-ice concentration and thickness distribution (ii) sea-ice motion vector using synergistic use of Optical (AWIFS, OCM) and Microwave (SAR, Scatterometer, Altimeter, SSMI) data. Validation & Signature studies (i) Validation of Microwave/Optical remote sensing products (ii) Polar ice signature database generation using Space-borne sensors.Assessment and monitoring of vulnerable areas to changes, using space-borne data.

It is an important component of the very active air-sea exchange in this area that leads to deep convection and production of deep ocean water masses. Antarctic Coastal Current is barotropic, banded at many points with countercurrents, which is mainly driven mainly by east winds south of 66?S. The eastern part of the Weddell Sea form the left wing of our study area and the Prydz Bay eddy forms the western limb of the study area. The heat transport into the southern Weddell Sea is estimated to be 3.48?1013 W. This implies an equivalent heat loss through the sea surface of 19 W m−2. The Antarctic Bottom Water and Antarctic Intermediate Water obtain their fundamental characteristics in the coastal. The coastal hydrodynamics in the vicinity of Antarctica is also as a result of freezing in austral winter and melting of sea ice in austral summer. In the Indian Ocean.

datasets.title: Environmental Impact Assessment of Anthropogenic Activities at Indian Polar Stations- A local and global perspective
datasets.abstract: Atmospheric emissions from fossil fuel burning (power and heat generation, aircraft, vehicles, etc.), emissions from incineration and other general activities can alter local environments. These activities can result in the introduction of particles as well as specific contaminants to the atmosphere (e.g., polycyclic hydrocarbons probably from exhaust). On a larger scale, they may jeopardize the scientific value of Antarctica for monitoring low-level global changes in atmospheric aerosols. It was considered that particle emission levels on the larger scale were too low for monitoring by conventional means away from stations. This, by itself, will allow first order estimates of mass emissions of particles and of SO2, NOx and subsequent modeling of dust and particle plumes. Collection of air samples provides confirmation of estimates. Samples of snow can be used as integrated samples of contaminant deposition.

datasets.title: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Antarctica has attracted the attention of scientific community all over the world since it is one of the most important climate regimes with a potential to influence long term global climatic patterns. In order to study these, IMD?s meteorological programme is specifically aimed at preparing a data archive of meteorological parameters over Antarctica. This may also enable us to understand the global aspects of Indian weather in general and monsoon behavior in particular. World Meteorological Organization (WMO) strongly recommends that any research station established in Antarctica should run a complete meteorological observatory and deliver the obtained data through Global Telecommunication System (GTS). The daily synoptic observations recorded at Bharati, Antarctica will enter into the Global Telecommunication System (GTS) and contribute to the international efforts for weather forecasting.
datasets.purpose: To improve understanding of variability and change in Antarctic climate. Monitoring of surface climate across East Antarctica. To improve understanding of teleconnections (where weather changes at one location are linked to changes elsewhere) between Antarctic and Indian Monsoon, To provide data for use in weather predictions and climate projections for India. To improve representation in numerical models of radiative, dynamical and chemical coupling processes throughout the atmosphere, focusing on energy and momentum transfer, chemical transport and links between Indian region and hemispheres.

datasets.title: Geophysical Studies at Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Induction coil magnetometer for monitoring geomagnetic field variations in 0-32 Hz frequency range was installed at Maitri. The data is used to study geomagnetic pulsations at this latitude. Schumann Resonance frequencies estimated from the data set provide information about the global temperature and global change in temperature when the instrument is operated on long-term basis. Measurements of total magnetic field at Maitri in campaigns and by IGRF model had indicated large decline in magnetic field (110 nT /yr) at Maitri during the last few decades. This decline seems to reduce as one moves away from this station. Continuous monitoring of total magnetic field at Maitri has, however revealed that the decline has been smaller during the last seven years (65 nT/y). It is not known how the total field behaves at other places within Antarctica. It is therefore important to monitor the spatial dependence of declining magnetic field by operating the PPM at a few locations in the Antarctic

datasets.title: Mass balance, dynamics, and climate of the central Dronning Maud Land coast,East Antarctica (MADICE) & Bio-geochemical processes associated with supraglacial ecosystems of coastal Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Mass balance of ice shelves is the key knowledge to better understand ongoing and future Antarctic contributions to the global sea-level rise. Thinning rates of ice shelves vary widely around Antarctica, and ice shelves in Dronning Maud Land (DML) are poorly understood in particular. DML is characterized with loosely-connected ice shelves along its 2000-km-long coast. Individual ice shelves are relatively small but extend close to or even beyond the continental-shelf break. Most of such ice shelves are punctuated by numerous grounded features (ice rises and rumples); ice rises are locations where ice-shelf flow is diverted around the grounded ice. Such grounded features are known to play vital roles in ice-shelf and ice-sheet dynamics over various timescales. The ice rises and rumples interact with adjacent ice shelves, ocean, and atmosphere, so these elements are inter-connected and need to be understood together.
datasets.purpose: To understand the current status and dynamics of ice shelves and evolution of ice rises in the coastal Dronning Maud Land. To understand the role of ice rises in the evolution and future of the Antarctic Ice Sheet and to reconstruct the palaeoenvironmental variables like temperature, precipitation, aerosols, and sea ice conditions during the past using ice core records from ice rises. To study photochemical and microbial processes associated with selected supraglacial ecosystems and their significance in coastal Antarctica.

datasets.abstract: It is quite important to study the ionospheric and propagation characteristics of Very Low frequency signal over a long path during usual and unusual solar flux variation. For this, Antarctica is most certainly the perfect location during summer season (November to February) and winter (June to August) in southern hemisphere. Prolonged days or nights provide a test bed for verifying theoretical models of how ionization and recombination take place. As the receiver is close to the pole, charged particles from solar coronal mass ejections can interact with the geomagnetic field and our recorded signal should also carry the information of this strong interaction. The effects of lightning and its induced effects which generates natural VLF signal as radio atmospherics (Sferics) can be studied widely from Antarctica.
datasets.purpose: The objective of this project project is to understand the propagation characteristics of Very Low Frequency (frequency 3-30kHz) signals over very long path for a long term basis simultaneously for both Bharati and Maitri region. For both the stations, High accurate instruments will be installed permanently. Secondly ground and near space based Cosmic ray detection will be executed using balloon experiments. The observational time for balloon-borne studies will be in summer.

datasets.title: Characterization of Atmospheric aerosols over Indian Antarctic station during the Southern Hemispheric summer of 2008-2009.
datasets.abstract: Aerosol optical depth (AOD), Aerosol black carbon (BC) mass concentrations (MB) and total mass concentration (MT) were measured over two Antarctic locations Maitri (70 45'52" S & 11 44'03" E, 123 m MSL) and Bharati (69 24.41' S, 76 11.72' E approximately at 35 m above sea level.) as a part of the 28th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica during the southern hemispheric summer of 2008-2009. Our study showed relatively high values of MB and mass mixing ratio (FBC) over Maitri (~ 75 ng m-3 and 2 %) compared to that over Bharati (~ 13 ng m-3 and 0.2 %). At both locations, MB fall abruptly after the blizzard where the values reduce to as low as half of the pre-blizzard values. This BC scavenging by snow can lead to change in snow albedo and will have strong climate implications. The Angstrom exponent estimated from the spectral values of absorption coefficients are found to vary from 0.5 to 1 indicating that the BC over Antarctic region is mainly originating from fossil fuel burning
datasets.purpose: Temporal variations of physical and optical properties of aerosol were investigated from Indian stations Bharati and Maitri in the eastern coastal Antarctica during the 28th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (28 ISEA). Our results indicated that the temporal variations of aerosols are large at Maitri, and differed significantly from those of Bharati where the human interference is very less.

datasets.abstract: Antarctic sea ice algal communities play a very significant role in primary production during the summer essentially due to the long daylight hours. The Antarctic Ocean absorbs large amount of atmospheric carbon dioxide which is a greenhouse gas due to the uptake of carbon dioxide by phytoplankton. Some of the microalga found in snow and ice during summer accumulates in sufficient numbers to colour the snow banks red, green, orange and even grey. Snow algae are generally single-celled organisms. Snow algae grow in semi-permanent to permanent snow or ice in the alpine or polar regions of the world.NIOT has isolated more than 200 marine micro algal strains from the coastal and oceanic waters of Indian main land, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep Islands and has screened more than 150 microalgal strain for biomass, lipid and other biochemical production.

datasets.title: To study the Aerosol radiation forcing over the Antarctic region by measuring Aerosol properties and Radiation
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic atmosphere and its constituents, particularly the aerosols and the Black Carbon in the atmosphere is currently gaining interest among the scientific community. The present knowledge and the data sets both are limited as far as the aerosol-radiation interaction of the region is concerned. Aerosols (including BC) are known to affect the radiation balance of any region. Although polar regions are not the source of anthropogenic aerosols the presence of aerosols including the Black carbon (BC) has already been reported over the polar regions. These aerosol particles from anthropogenic and bio-mass burning sources transported to polar regions may cause direct warming of the lower troposphere by absorption of radiation and IR emission. The shoot particles of the aerosol deposited over the snow increases the surface albedo and may contribute to an increase in snow melting.

datasets.abstract: Antarctic is a land of extremes and larger than Europe, nearly twice the size of Australia, it is almost entirely buried beneath an ice sheet which covers around 99 percent of the land surface. The Antarctic ice sheet contains 90 percent of the world?s ice and around 70 percent of its freshwater. Due to the Antarctic?s position at the South Pole, the long Antarctic winter is spent in continuous darkness, while in mid-summer parts of the continent experience 24 hours of sunlight. The most iconic of bird species of Antarctic is the penguins. All penguin species are restricted to the southern hemisphere, but only two species namely, the Emperor Penguin Aptenodytes forsteri and Ad?lie Penguin Pygoscelis adeliae are considered to be truly Antarctic, breeding on the Antarctic continent.Fifty three species of birds have been reported from Antarctica, of which one species is endemic and five species are listed under threatened category of IUCN. datasets.abstract: Pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) are a class of emerging micro pollutants that are now ubiquitously present in the aquatic and marine environments (Klosterhaus et al 2013, Luo et al 2014). PPCPs range from medicines consumed for various illnesses to stimulants like caffeine to personal care products like sun screen lotions, soaps, perfumes etc (Daughton and Ternes 1999). Their pathways into the aquatic environment are primarily from wastewaters originating from industries and domestic sources (Daughton and Ternes 1999; Ternes et al 2004). Studies have indicated that very low concentrations of triclosan, an antibacterial used in soaps, toothpaste and deodorants can induce cytotoxic, genotoxic and endocrine disruptor behaviour in aquatic organisms like fish, crustaceans and algae (Bedoux et al 2012). Calculation of hazard quotients (HQ) is an indirect technique, that is proposed in this work, where the ecotoxicological risk to the aquatic organisms can be assessed.
