datasets.abstract: The change in lightning show good correlation with global temperature change. Williams (1992) has proposed that the ionospheric potential can be used as global thermometer. However, this relationship is highly non-linear and need further research. Further, the study by Carslaw Et al., 2002 and Harrison, 2000 have shown that the electric fields caused by the global circuit could can affect aerosol charging by modifying the ion environment on the boundaries of clouds where ion concentrations are profoundly asymmetric and the electric fields are enhanced. The global circuit could therefore act to communicate cosmic ray changes throughout the atmosphere, by changes in the conduction current.

datasets.title: Melt Pond Data - 44ISEA
datasets.abstract: Surface melt-induced melt ponds and supraglacial lakes (SGLs) are key indicators of ice-sheet response to atmospheric warming in Antarctica. When firn saturation limits meltwater infiltration, water accumulates in surface depressions, forming ponds and lakes that may refreeze, drain, or enhance melting through albedo feedbacks. These processes can influence ice-shelf stability and ice dynamics. This study investigates the seasonal variability, formation, and evolution of melt ponds and SGLs in and around the Maitri Research Station, Schirmacher Oasis, to better understand surface melt processes and their implications for Antarctic ice stability.
datasets.purpose: To investigate the seasonal variability and evolution of surface melt by analysing the formation, persistence, and dynamics of melt ponds and supraglacial lakes in and around the Maitri Research Station, Schirmacher Oasis. datasets.title: Biogeochemical gradients drive phylogenetic?functional decoupling in native microbial communities of Schirmacher Hills lacustrine systems, East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Antarctic lacustrine ecosystems host distinctive native microbial communities shaped by extreme environmental gradients and their intrinsic ecological value is potentially at risk from the introduction of non-native species associated with increased human activity in the antarctic pristine natural ecosystems. Here, we examined the biogeochemical characteristics and microbial community structure across seven lacustrine systems in the Schirmacher Hills, East Antarctica, experiencing varying degrees of human activity, revealing pronounced spatial differentiation between near-station lacustrine systems (NSL) and far-station lacustrine systems (FSL). FSL exhibited elevated total organic carbon (0.24 vs. 0.14 mg L⁻?) and depleted δ??C signatures, indicating the accumulation of allochthonous organic matter, whereas NSL showed higher monosaccharide concentrations, suggesting enhanced microbial processing of labile carbon.
datasets.purpose: In this study, we integrate high-resolution organic geochemical proxies-including total nitrogen (TN), total organic carbon (TOC), stable carbon and nitrogen isotopes (δ??C and δ?⁵N), C/N ratios, total carbohydrates (TCHO), and monosaccharide concentrations-with 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to assess microbial community structure across lacustrine systems in the Schirmacher Hills.

datasets.title: Delineation of Land-Ice-Sea (LIS) interface (Hinge-line), around Schirmacher Oasis, central Dronning Maud Land (cDML), East Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The Ice Shelf, mother of all icebergs in Antarctic sea is a continuation of polar ice sheet moving away from the continent and floating over the Antarctic seas. The ice shelves are dynamic, may be confined or unconfined; either made up entirely of glacier-ice or partly of sea-ice or composite ice; each with its own set of individual characteristics, governed by factors such as mass balance, climatic conditions, velocity of movement, thickness of the ice and saturation of sea water. The ice shelf varies in size and shape depending on the thickness of polar ice-cap in a particular region, the ocean currents and outreach support of the sub-Antarctic islands giving it an additional support as pillars (sea mounts) rising from the sea bottom. The ice shelf is cantilevered on one end, at the triple junction of Land-Ice-Sea and floats freely over the sea on the other end. It may or may not be grounded over the sub-Antarctic islands.

datasets.title: Sandy Lake, Schirmacher Oasis: Rock magnetics, Grain size, C, N elemental & isotopes
datasets.abstract: Rock magnetic parameters, grain size distribution, and carbon and nitrogen elemental and isotopic data were generated from sediment core samples collected from Sandy Lake in the Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica, during the Indian Antarctic Expedition. The dataset includes measurements of magnetic properties, sediment particle size fractions, and C?N concentrations and isotopic compositions. These proxies provide complementary information on sediment provenance, depositional processes, and organic matter sources. The integrated dataset supports reconstruction of past environmental and climatic variability and improves understanding of sedimentary and biogeochemical processes in Antarctic lake systems.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of generating rock magnetic, grain size, and carbon and nitrogen elemental and isotopic data from the Sandy Lake sediment core is to investigate past environmental, sedimentary, and biogeochemical changes in the Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica. Rock magnetic parameters help identify variations in mineral input and sediment sources, grain size reflects changes in depositional energy and transport processes, and C?N elemental and isotopic data provide insights into organic matter sources and productivity. Together, these datasets support paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate reconstruction of Antarctic lake ecosystems.

datasets.title: Melt Pond Data
datasets.abstract: Surface melt-induced melt ponds and supraglacial lakes (SGLs) are key indicators of ice-sheet response to atmospheric warming in Antarctica. When firn saturation limits meltwater infiltration, water accumulates in surface depressions, forming ponds and lakes that may refreeze, drain, or enhance melting through albedo feedbacks. These processes can influence ice-shelf stability and ice dynamics. This study investigates the seasonal variability, formation, and evolution of melt ponds and SGLs in and around the Maitri Research Station, Schirmacher Oasis, to better understand surface melt processes and their implications for Antarctic ice stability.
datasets.purpose: To investigate the seasonal variability and evolution of surface melt by analysing the formation, persistence, and dynamics of melt ponds and supraglacial lakes in and around the Maitri Research Station, Schirmacher Oasis.
datasets.project_name: Vulnerability of East Coastal Antarctic to surface melt and Ponding

datasets.title: Long Lake. Schirmacher Oasis: Grain Size Data
datasets.abstract: Grain size distribution data were generated from sediment core samples collected from Long Lake in the Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica, during the Indian Antarctic Expedition. The dataset includes measurements of sediment particle size fractions that characterize sediment texture and depositional conditions within the lake basin. Grain size analysis provides insights into sediment transport processes, catchment dynamics, and variations in depositional energy. These data contribute to understanding sedimentary processes and environmental variability in Antarctic lake systems and provide important information for paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate reconstruction in the Schirmacher Oasis region.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of generating grain size data from the Long Lake sediment core is to investigate sediment depositional patterns and infer past environmental and hydrological changes in the Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica. Variations in grain size distribution help identify shifts in sediment sources, transport energy, and catchment processes through time. The dataset supports paleoenvironmental studies by providing sedimentological evidence for interpreting past lake dynamics and contributes to broader research on climate variability and landscape evolution in Antarctic oasis environments.

datasets.abstract: Break up pf Rodinia assembly and birth of Gondwanaland took place during Neoproterzoic era which represents one of its most dynamic periods of the earth evolution. Understanding the Neoproterozoic tectonic on the location and time from Neoproterozic geography will help to understand the successive phanerozoic tectonic and present tectonic belts as they are being controlled by the past plate configuration (Collins and Pisaversky, 2005). Early existence of a single super continent known as palaeopangea (Pipera, 1976; 1982; 2000) with the southern part known as Gondwana was formed by the amalgamation of south America, south Africa , Madagascar, India, Australia, Antarctica and Sri Lanka. Later Mc. Williams (1981) proposed that there was two separated part of land i.e. East Gondwana (India, Australia, and Antarctica) west Gondwana (South America and South Africa).
datasets.purpose: Dating of the Lamprophyre and dolerite dykes and sills, finding palaeo-geography position of these rocks using palaeomagnetic study, extending the correlation of dolerite and lamprophyre dykes from the Eastern Ghat Mobile Belt of India to Ryaner Complex and Dronning Maud land of East Antarctica.

datasets.title: Geomagnetic and Atmospheric Electrical Parameter Variations observed at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Surface measurements of the atmospheric electrical parameters, viz. ionosphere to ground currents, electric field and geomagnetic field were carried out at the Indian station, Maitri, Antarctica. The averaged pattern of diurnal variations in the electric field and Maxwell current density averaged over selected fair weather days nearly follows the Carnegie curve, with a minimum around 0300 UT and a maximum around 1900 UT. However, during magnetically disturbed days, there is a departure from universal diurnal variation in both the electric field and vertical conduction current, which is attributed to the influence of solar wind-magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling. Examining the cause in detail will require further investigation. The correlation coefficient between the current and electric field had a high value (more than 0.75) for all these days. The measured atmospheric electric field and geomagnetic field variations were compared. geomagnetic conditions.
datasets.purpose: This study will help us to examine the impact of upper atmospheric contribution to the geoelectrical parameters during different geomagnetic conditions.

datasets.title: Hydrodynamics along Meridional Transects in the Southwest Indian Ocean Sector of the Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: Preliminary analysis of expendable CTD profiles collected during the 26th Indian Antarctic Expedition along the ship route from Durban to India Bay, Antarctica (Track-1) and Prydz Bay to Mauritius (Track-2) during February to March 2007 are discussed. Vertical thermohaline structure reveal that the northern and southern branches of Subantarctic Front on both Tracks merge; likewise, the Agulhas Retroflection Front (AF) and South Subtropical Front (SSTF) merge between 43? and 44?S on Track-2. The southern branch of the Polar Front (PF2) meanders by 550 km southward towards east. The Subtropical Surface Water, Central Water and Mode Water are located north of 43.5?S, while the Subantarctic Surface Water, Antarctic Surface Water, Antarctic Intermediate Water and Circumpolar Deep Water are encountered in the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC) region.
datasets.purpose: Repeated hydrographic observations are required to compare and quantify changes in the hydrodynamics over a period of many years; however, such observations are impractical because of the high costs of chartering research vessel. To overcome this problem, I have initiated a project to collect hydrographic data in the southwestern IO sector of the SO by using expendable CTD (XCTD) probes which can be launched from a moving ship.
datasets.project_name: Hydrodynamics along Meridional Transects in the Southwest Indian Ocean Sector of the Southern Ocean during Austral Summer 2007.

datasets.title: Probiotics maintain the gut microbiome homeostasis during Indian Antarctic expedition by ship
datasets.abstract: Ship voyage to Antarctica is a stressful journey for expedition members. The response of human gut microbiota to ship voyage and a feasible approach to maintain gut health, is still unexplored. The present findings describe a 24-day long longitudinal study involving 19 members from 38th Indian Antarctic Expedition, to investigate the impact of ship voyage and effect of probiotic intervention on gut microbiota. Fecal samples collected on day 0 as baseline and at the end of ship voyage (day 24), were analyzed using whole genome shotgun sequencing. Probiotic intervention reduced the sea sickness by 10% compared to 44% in placebo group. The gut microbiome in placebo group members on day 0 and day 24, indicated significant alteration compared to a marginal change in the microbial composition in probiotic group. Functional analysis revealed significant alterations in carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism.
datasets.purpose: The present study is first of its kind, providing a feasible approach for protecting gut health during Antarctic expedition involving ship voyage.
datasets.project_name: Probiotics maintain the gut microbiome homeostasis during Indian Antarctic expedition by ship

datasets.title: Urine metabolite profiling of Indian Antarctic Expedition members: NMR spectroscopy-based metabolomic investigation
datasets.abstract: The southernmost region of earth, Antarctica, has world's most challenging environments. Those who live for long time and work in Antarctic stations are subjected to environmental stresses such as cold weather, photoperiod variations leading to disrupted sleep cycles, constrained living spaces, dry air, non-availability of fresh food items, and high electromagnetic radiations, psychological factors, such as geographical and social isolation, etc. All these factors have a significant impact on the human body.
datasets.purpose: The present study investigated the impact of Antarctica harsh environment on human physiology and its metabolic processes by evaluating urine metabolome, using 1H NMR spectroscopy and analyzing certain physiological and clinical parameters for correlation with physiological expression data and metabolite results. Two study groups - before Antarctic exposure (B) and after Antarctic exposure (E), consisting of 11 subjects, exposed to one-month summer expedition, were compared. 35 metabolites in urine samples were identified from the 700 MHz 1 H NMR spectra from where integral intensity of 22 important metabolites was determined.
datasets.project_name: Urine metabolite profiling of Indian Antarctic Expedition members: NMR spectroscopy-based metabolomic investigation

datasets.title: Validation of Air-Sea Interface Parameters in the Southwest Indian Ocean Sector of the Southern Ocean.
datasets.abstract: As a part of the International Polar Year project, meteorological data from NCEP-NCAR and ECMWF numerical weather forecasts (NWFs), QuikSCAT winds and AMSR-E sea surface temperature (SST) in the surface atmospheric boundary layer have been validated by using ship-based data collected in the southwest Indian Ocean sector of the Southern Ocean during the 26th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica. The NWFs overestimate mean sea level pressure by ?5 to ?12 mb. The root-mean-square difference (rmsd) ranges from 1.7 to 2.3 mb and the regression yields a high correlation coefficient (r) exceeding 0.9, significant at 1% level. Validation of NWF air temperature yields a rmsd of 0.8 ?C and r exceeding 0.9. Relative humidity from NWFs is underestimated by 3%, and the data fail to capture sporadic events in the midlatitudes. The QuikSCAT winds are underestimates by 1.3 m s?1 and show a large bias south of 50?S.
datasets.purpose: This paper addresses the analysis of meteorological data collected during the 26th ISEA on board MV Emerald Sea from Durban to India Bay, Antarctica during 9?14 February 2007 (Track?1) and from Prydz Bay, Antarctica to Mauritius during 19?26 March 2007 (Track-2). In particular, we elucidate large-scale meteorological features identified along the two tracks, and validate the satellite and numerical weather forecasts (NWF). Though the data points are few, it is hoped that this work would help in understanding the extremes in the ABL conditions in the SO and the validation would serve as one of the point of reference India?s OCEANSAT?II mission scheduled to be launched in 2009 with a Scatterometer for measuring ocean-surface wind and Ocean Color Monitor for biophysical studies.
datasets.project_name: Validation of Air-Sea Interface Parameters in the Southwest Indian Ocean Sector of the Southern Ocean.

datasets.title: Exploring the Potential of Arctic Microbes for Bio-hydrogen Production
datasets.abstract: This study investigates Arctic microbes to uncover novel hydrogen-producing strains. Sampling will occur at various sites around Ny-Alseund, Svalbard, with different sample types. Key objectives include isolating biohydrogen-producing microbes, quantifying and optimising hydrogen production and evaluating different organic substrates for hydrogen yield. In-situ measurement of field parameters will be conducted, and samples will be transported to BITS Pilani, Goa Campus, for further analysis. Microbes will be isolated from samples under anaerobic conditions, tested for dark fermentation and quantified for hydrogen production via gas chromatography. Promising isolates will undergo sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Later, selected cultures would utilise organic wastes as carbon sources, and hydrogen production would be optimised for pH, temperature and other relevant parameters. The maximum hydrogen yield can be used to demonstrate the application of hydrogen fuel cells.
datasets.purpose: Evaluating the biohydrogen production potential from microbes in Arctic samples is crucial for advancing sustainable energy solutions. With its unique and extreme environment, the Arctic region harbours diverse microbial communities that have adapted to frosting conditions. These microbes possess metabolic pathways that can be harnessed for biohydrogen production, a clean and renewable energy source. By analysing the metagenomics of these microbes, we can identify novel hydrogen-producing strains and optimise conditions for maximum yield. This research contributes to the global effort to reduce reliance on fossil fuels and mitigate climate change. Additionally, understanding the biohydrogen potential of Arctic microbes can lead to innovative biotechnological applications, enhancing energy security and promoting environmental sustainability.
datasets.project_name: Exploring the Potential of Arctic Microbes for Bio-hydrogen Production
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Impact of the harsh Antarctic environment on mucosal immunity
datasets.abstract: Mucosal immunity of Indian Antarctic personnel was analysed during the 34th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (ISEA) by ship voyage. Serum and salivary IgA, IgA1 and IgA2 levels along with salivary cortisol and TGF-β were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Samples were collected at three different time points (T1, T2 and T3) during the expedition. Serum and salivary IgA, IgA1 and IgA2 concentrations incrementally increased towards the end of the expedition as compared to the beginning of the expedition. Salivary IgA and TGF-β levels were significantly altered during the expedition. Levels of IgA1 (P = 0.0007) and IgA2 (P = 0.0135) increased significantly at T3 as compared to T1. Additionally, significant changes in serum IgA were observed, with peak levels at T3 (P = 0.0015) and T2 (P < 0.001). However, the level of serum IgA2 was also significantly altered at T3 (P < 0.05) and T2 (P = 0.0006) in comparison with T1.
datasets.purpose: The aim of the present study is to explore the impact of Antarctic environmental stress on the humoral and mucosal components, primarily IgA, IgA1 and IgA2 and salivary TGF-β, the first such study of its kind.
datasets.project_name: Impact of the harsh Antarctic environment on mucosal immunity

datasets.title: Community analysis of Meiobenthos and Genetic diversity of major functional groups in Arctic Kongsfjorden
datasets.abstract: This proposal aims to evaluate the meiobenthic organisms for its community function and dynamics, genetic variability of the major meiofaunal functional groups like Harpacticoids, Ostracods, Polychaetes, Oligochaetes,, Kinorhyncha, Gastrotrichs, Nematodes, Foraminiferans etc. and its role in trophic processes specific to organic production-mineralization and carbon turnover rate . A suitable community structure based model of meiobenthic community would be evolved that would give an insight on the benthic processes in relation to the functional groups in Kongsfjord. Meiofauna in general, are the dominant taxon, affect detrital decomposition and carbon transformation. Even though preliminary studies suggests the abundance and diversity of macrobenthic fauna and meiobenthic nematodes in Kongsfjorden system (Bijoy Nandan et al., 2013 & Krishna Priya et al 2013), a comprehensive and in depth scientific information is greatly lacking on the meiobenthic component, specific to the community.

datasets.title: Health in Antarctica: Indian Perspective
datasets.abstract: Antarctica is the only continent with no permanent human habitation. The continent is currently inhabited by scientific teams at various national Antarctic research bases around the continent, who live in the continent temporarily for a few months. The strength of each base is highly variable. At the Indian Antarctic research base, Maitri, the population is about 70-80 in summer and around 25 in winter. The Chinese station, Zhongshan, houses 60 members during summer and 25 during winter, whereas the Australian station, Davis houses 120 members during summer and 18 during winter. The Russian Antarctic station, ovolazarevskaya is the only station accessible during the winter and it is 10 kilometers from Maitri. Due to this sparse and temporary population, exhaustive data on health disorders expected in Antarctica is not readily available. Moreover, the expedition team members are deputed after detailed medical and psychological assessment and are provided modern facilities in Antarctica.
datasets.purpose: Oversee and plan the health care facilities at Maitri.
datasets.project_name: Health in Antarctica: Indian Perspective

datasets.title: Biogeochemistry and Paleoenvironmental studies of Larsemann Hills, Prydz Bay and SchirmacherOasis (Reconstruction of relative sea level from lacustrine sediments of Ongul Island)
datasets.abstract: akes from the coastal oasis of Larsemann Hills respond to changes in regional climate. They are mainly influenced by the ice-sheet dynamics and regional eustatic variation based on their proximity to either of them or both. The sedimentary sequences of the ice-free regions of Antarctica offer unique climate records (lake sediment deposits). The lake sedimentary sequences in the ice-free coastal oasis doting the Antarctic continental margin are excellent paleo-archives, which are well studied to understand the interplay of regional climate and Antarctic climate dynamics. These lakes act as ?sentinels of change? (Williamson et al., 2009) and ?early warning systems? (Hodgson and Smol, 2008) as their ecosystem?s response to climate change is instantaneous and provide critical insights into the effects (Moss, 2012) and mechanisms of climate change.
datasets.purpose: Reconstruction of the ice sheet variabilityat the Larsemann Hills and Schirmacher Oasis to examine East Antarctic Ice Sheet sensitivity and response to glacial-interglacial cycles Approach: To reconstruct the past-sedimentary proxy variations over glacial/interglacial cycles to decipher the response of the lakes to the Antarctic climate and regional ice-sheet dynamicsTo trace lacustrine biogenic productivity, redox conditions and mobility of trace elements in the sedimentary column of lakesApproach: Antarctic lakes are known to be oligotrophic; the preexisting lake sediments may be an important source of nutrients and carbon to the present lake ecosystems and may provide clues to subsistence of life in subglacial lake systems.This will also provide information on past marine incursions in the lake, changes in terrestrialweathering with changing climate.

datasets.title: Apportioning nurdles and microplastics on the way to Antarctica using foldscope
datasets.abstract: Nurdles are small plastic pellets measuring less than 5 mm and thus represents microplastics. Nurdles along with other forms of microplastics are considered as major concern with respect to marine pollution. They are marine debris originating from plastic particles utilized in manufacturing large-scale plastics. Marine life is severely threatened by these small pieces of plastic; the creatures that make up the base of the marine food chain, such as krill, are prematurely dying by choking on nurdles. A variety of marine life, from insect larvae, small fish, amphibians and turtles to birds and larger mammals, mistake microbeads for their food source. This ingestion of plastics introduces the potential for toxicity not only to these animals but to other species higher in the food chain. Harmful chemicals thus transferred can include hydrophobic pollutants that collect on the surface of the water such as polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)

datasets.title: Hydrodynamics of the Indian Ocean sector of chokepoint between Africa and Antarctica and coastal Antarctica, as a part of validation of satellite data.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic Coastal Current is the southernmost current in the world. It is an important component of the very active air-sea exchange in this area that leads to deep convection and production of deep ocean water masses. Antarctic Coastal Current is barotropic, banded at many points with counter currents, which is mainly driven mainly by east winds south of 66?S. The eastern part of the Weddell Sea form the left wing of our study area and the Prydz Bay eddy forms the western limb of the study area. The heat transport into the southern Weddell Sea is estimated to be 3.48?1013 W. This implies an equivalent heat loss through the sea surface of 19 W m−2. The Antarctic Bottom Water and Antarctic Intermediate Water obtain their fundamental characteristics in the coastal. The coastal hydrodynamics in the vicinity of Antarctica is also as a result of freezing in austral winter and melting of sea ice in austral summer.

datasets.title: Neuro-cognitive performance and Emotional Regulation among Antarctic Expedition Group: Convergence Evidence from Electrophysiological Behavioural Investigation
datasets.abstract: It is now well established that Antarctica environment has huge impact on human functioning. Human beings are highly adaptive to extreme environmental condition. Individual can resist and have normal functioning in extreme environment. However, it poses a constant challenge to the health and welling being of individual (Mullin, 1960). Lugg (2000) in his study identified five most frequent physiological condition experienced during Antarctica stay.e., injuries and poisoning, respiratory complaints, damage and irritation of skin and subcutaneous tissue, disruption in the nervous system and sensory organ functioning and finally gastrointestinal problems. datasets.title: Microbiome in the Permafrost of Canadian High Arctic
datasets.abstract: NCPOR implemented the project on Evaluation of microbiome and multi drug resistant bacteria in the tundra, Active soil layer and Permafrost regions of Canadian high Arctic?. The project objective to study the microorganism in the thawing of permafrost of Arctic regions. Arctic warming impacts the thawing of permafrost- ?which could potentially reactivate many of the dormant microorganisms that are preserved in the permafrost soils for centuries. Some of these microorganisms may be pathogenic and/or drug-resistant bacteria that can lead to the resurgence of zoonotic diseases. In this project, we intend to perform a comprehensive survey of the microbiome in the tundra soil, active layer, and permafrost and evaluate the presence of potential pathogenic and drug resistant using a culture-dependent and independent approach but also to delineate potential sources- anthropogenic and/or ancient origins in the Canadian high Arctic regions.
datasets.purpose: The emergence of new pathogens under the current climate change scenario, especially multidrug-resistant bacteria is a matter of public health concern globally. The permafrost is a natural reservoir for diverse microbial taxa, and its thawing can reactivate ancient microbes into an active state. Thus, it is important to understand the role of these emerging microorganisms, especially their possible human health significance. Therefore, the studies on the health-significant bacteria are necessary for understanding the emergence of antibiotic-resistant genes and multidrug-resistant bacteria in the Canadian Arctic. Also, we can contribute to understanding the possible spread of virulence genes and ARGs via horizontal gene transfer to other bacteria, animals, humans, and environments. Our efforts will enable the policymakers and local population to take precautionary measures against the spread of antimicrobial resistance.

datasets.title: Microbiome in the Permafrost of Canadian High Arctic 2024
datasets.abstract: One of the most noticeable impacts of Arctic warming is the thawing of permafrost ?which could potentially reactivate many of the dormant microorganisms that are preserved in the permafrost soils for centuries. Some of these microorganisms may be pathogenic and/or antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) that can leadlead to the resurgence of zoonotic diseases. Besides, antibiotic resistance genes (ARG) can be transported to the Arctic environment through the migration and movement of humans and birds (Arcilla et al., 2017, Zhang et al., 2017). Since ARGs are now widespread among microbial communities, whether the extensive diversity of ARG and pathogenic bacteria in environmental reservoirs is the result of anthropogenic influence is controversial. Thus, in this proposal, we intend to perform a comprehensive survey of the tundra soil, active layer, and permafrost not only to evaluate the presence of potential ARG and ARB using a culture-dependent and independent approach.

datasets.title: Arctic expedition August 2024
datasets.abstract: Hydrography and plankton samples were collected on board MS Teisten in the Kongsfjorden and Krossfjorden during august 2024. The water samples and plankton samples were collected from various depths in both the fjords using Niskin sampler and plankton net respectively. Considering the knowledge gap, the present research proposal hypothesizes that (i) the sea ice decline and on-going Arctic amplification will significantly impact the fjords' biogeochemical processes and ecosystem function. (ii) Understanding the diversity of plankton and their adaption/shifting would be the contribution of biomass and feedback to climate change. (iii) Understanding the present and future ecosystem function and climate change of the region using satellite and model estimation for long-term observation in the Arctic fjords.

datasets.title: Ecological quality assessment of Kongsfjorden Fjord in the arctic environment: integrating macrobenthic communities and benthic indices
datasets.abstract: The analysis of benthic faunal composition in Kongsfjorden revealed that polychaetes were the dominant group, followed by other groups. Species diversity indices ranged from 3.656 to 4.219, with the highest diversity recorded at Station 10 (St-10) and the lowest at Station 3 (St-3). A total of 46 were classified into five ecological groups following the AZTI classification, while six species could not be assigned. Among the classified taxa, 17 species (36%) belonged to EG-I, 15 species (32%) to EG-II, 8 species (17%) to EG-III, 6 species (13%) to EG-IV, and one species (2%) to EG-V. The AMBI values derived from the macrobenthic community ranged from 1.07 to 3.10, indicating that the sampled stations varied from normal to unbalanced benthic ecosystem conditions. Likewise, the M-AMBI values ranged between 0.63 and 0.77, corresponding to ecological quality statuses classified as ?good? to ?high.?

datasets.title: Reconstruction of Organic Matter and Isotopic Variability in Kongsfjorden Sediment Core Over the Past Two Centuries
datasets.abstract: This dataset comprises geochemical and isotopic analyses of a 21 cm sediment core retrieved from Kongsfjorden, an Arctic fjord in western Spitsbergen. The data include sedimentary organic matter concentration and its isotopic composition over the past two centuries. The dataset reveals temporal changes in organic matter sources and isotopic signatures, capturing the interplay between glacial melting, marine productivity, and environmental variability. These proxies provide valuable insights into past climate change and productivity shifts influenced by Arctic warming.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of this dataset is to reconstruct the historical variability of sedimentary organic matter concentration and isotopic composition in Kongsfjorden over the past two centuries. By linking these records to glacial melt dynamics and climate variability, the dataset facilitates the study of past environmental changes, including the impacts of Arctic warming on marine productivity and sedimentation processes.

datasets.title: High-Resolution Sedimentary Geochemical Record of Arctic Climate Variability in Kongsfjorden Over the Last Millennium
datasets.abstract: This dataset features a high-resolution sediment core geochemical record spanning the last millennium from Kongsfjorden, an Arctic fjord in western Spitsbergen. It includes measurements of sedimentary organic matter concentrations (TOC, TN) and their isotopic compositions (δ13C, δ15N) obtained from core NP14-FM. The dataset captures multidecadal to centennial variability, offering insights into climatic transitions between warm and cold Arctic intervals. These geochemical proxies provide evidence of the interplay between marine and terrestrial organic matter sources and their links to Arctic climate dynamics and teleconnections with the Indian monsoon system.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of this dataset is to investigate Arctic climate variability over the last millennium using sedimentary organic matter concentrations and isotopic compositions from Kongsfjorden. By examining shifts in organic matter sources and isotopic signatures, the dataset facilitates the study of long-term climate transitions and teleconnections, particularly the Arctic-Indian monsoon link, aiding in reconstructing past environmental changes.

datasets.abstract: Bio-optical studies are essential in polar regions due to their role in understanding the interactions between light, water, and biological processes, particularly in the context of climate change. These studies help reveal how phytoplankton, a key component of polar ecosystems, respond to changes in light availability, water quality, and nutrient levels?factors highly influenced by glacial melt and seasonal ice dynamics. By examining parameters like light absorption, scattering, and fluorescence, bio-optical research can track shifts in primary productivity, carbon cycling, and the overall health of polar marine ecosystems. This information is vital for predicting the impact of warming temperatures on polar food webs and global carbon sequestration.
datasets.purpose: To study the (1) effect of prevailing environmental conditions on phytoplankton light absorption and physiology, (ii) bio-optical characterization of the fjord waters using hyperspectral radiometer and spectrophotometry, (iii) assess the phytoplankton biomass (productivity) variability of the ecosystems (iv) model the underwater bio-optical properties, which have implications for satellite ocean color remote sensing.

datasets.title: Diazotrophs in the Arctic fjords
datasets.abstract: Nitrogen-fixing or diazotrophic microbes fix atmospheric nitrogen (N2) to ammonia (NH3+) using nitrogenase enzyme and play a crucial role in regulating marine primary productivity and carbon dioxide sequestration. However, there is a lack of information about the diversity, structure, and environmental regulations of the diazotrophic communities in the high Arctic fjords, such as Kongsfjorden. Here, we employed nifH gene sequencing to clarify variations in composition, community structure, and assembly mechanism among the diazotrophs of the salinity-driven stratified waters of Kongsfjorden. The majority of the nifH gene sequences obtained in the present study belonged to cluster I and cluster III nifH phylotypes, accounting for 65% and 25% of the total nifH gene sequences. The nifH gene diversity and composition of particle attached and freeliving bacterial communities were encountered through this study

datasets.abstract: Kongsfjorden receives inputs from Atlantic and Arctic waters, as well as glacier runoff, and is an ideal site to study the impact of environmental variability on ecosystem dynamics relevant across the Arctic. Kongsfjorden experiences significant interannual variations in water mass characteristics, which impact the seasonality and magnitude of phytoplankton blooms. Additionally, strong interannual variations in meltwater and the amount of terrigenous inputs to the fjord are also reported. This suggests that Kongsfjorden not only experiences strong seasonality but also interannual variability in water mass characteristics, primary production, macroalgal, and terrigenous inputs. Despite extensive microbiological research in Kongsfjorden, multi-year, seasonally resolved data on microbial community dynamics are not available. Thus, high-resolution monitoring over many annual cycles is required to resolve the variations of microbial populations against the backdrop of climate change.

datasets.title: Functional diversity of Heterotrophic Bacteria in the water column and surficial sediments of Kongsfjord with special reference to those involved in carbon cycle.
datasets.abstract: Heterotrophic bacteria play major role in the mineralisation of diverse organic substances available in the marine environment and contribute to productivity in a significant manner. Heterotrophic bacterial consortiums play key role in the breakdown of large molecular weight substances to smaller entities which will be further taken inside by the bacteria and utilized for metabolism. This way they covert lot of dissolved organic matter (DOM) to particulate organic matter (POM). The metabolism also leads to release of DOM by bacteria which in turn utilised by other members of the community. While the organic matter being transported from the surface to the bottom, the easy to digest fractions are being used up in the water column and hard to digest structural materials are likely to reach the bottom where they will be used up by the heterotrophic bacterial community in the surficial sediments as well as those residing within certain depth of the sediment.

datasets.title: Exploring Bacterial Pigments from the Arctic: Potential for Biotechnological and Environmental Applications
datasets.abstract: The main objective of the present study is to extract and characterize pigments produced by diverse bacterial species isolated from Arctic sediment samples. Pigments were extracted from previously collected Arctic sediment-derived bacterial isolates, followed by preliminary physicochemical and functional characterization. The extracted pigments were subjected to wavelength scanning to determine their spectral properties, along with evaluation of their antioxidant potential and UV absorption capacity, highlighting their possible protective and bioactive roles. Concurrently, genomic DNA was extracted from the respective pigment-producing bacterial cultures, and molecular identification was initiated using PCR-based amplification of target genes; sequencing and taxonomic analysis are currently in progress. It was observed that pigment production was comparatively reduced under laboratory culture conditions, likely due to the absence of native Arctic environmental factors
datasets.purpose: The main purpose of this study is to elucidate the chemical structure of the extracted bacterial pigments and accurately identify the nature of the bioactive compounds. In addition, the study aims to evaluate the stability of these pigments and, where instability is observed, to enhance their shelf life and functional performance through nanoemulsion-based stabilization strategies. Such formulation approaches are intended to improve pigment stability against environmental stressors and facilitate their potential commercialization. The stabilized pigments will be explored for diverse applications, particularly in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations, owing to their antioxidant and UV-protective properties.

datasets.title: Organic carbon and metal concentrations shape surficial benthic microbial communities in Arctic Fjords
datasets.abstract: Ocean warming and Arctic climate change have a significant impact on the biogeochemistry and ecology of Svalbard fjords. Glacier melt and permafrost thaw introduce terrigenous material from the rivers and glacial runoff into these fjords. This study focused on benthic bacterial community structure and the influence of environmental factors in three climate-sensitive Arctic fjords located in the northern and western regions of Svalbard. Our findings revealed significant differences in bacterial community structure between the surface sediments of the northern and western Svalbard fjords (PERMANOVA, R? = 0.215, p-value = 0.001). Notably, the western fjord exhibited higher bacterial diversity compared to the northern fjord. In the northern fjord, the dominant bacterial phyla were Bacteroidetes (41%), Proteobacteria (37%), and Firmicutes (18%). In contrast, the western fjord was characterised by a prevalence of Proteobacteria (46%), Firmicutes (25%), Bacteroidota (8%), and Actinobacteriota
datasets.purpose: This study is to answer the following questions: (1) Do bacterial diversity and composition vary between the northern and western fjord surface sediments? (2) What major environmental parameters influence bacterial community structure along the northern and western Svalbard fjords? (3) Are there differences in the functional profiling of bacterial communities between these fjords?

Field activities addressed organic matter characterization of different organic carbon sources in and around Kongsfjorden to study their nature and fate in the fjord in view of the intensifying terrestrial thawing and runoff in the Arctic. Hydrological (CTD casts) and biogeochemical (Niskin bottle sampling) data were collected during oceanographic surveys in Kongsfjorden onboard MS Teisten. An extensive terrestrial sampling was also carried out on the southern coast of Kongsfjorden to both East and West side of the town Ny-Alesund, to characterize all terrestrial sources of organic matter. The dataset includes hydrological data (T, sal, density), total organic carbon and total nitrogen data (POC and PN), C and N stable isotopic data (d13C and d15N), total carbohydrates data (CHO), total proteins data (PRT), monosaccharides

The growing oxygen-deficient ocean habitats brought about by climate and associated environmental changes negatively impact the marine life. Since oxygen is the most essential component needed for life, forecasts on the amount of dissolved oxygen in marine environments are vital for biodiversity (a healthy environment) and for economic issues. Benthic foraminifera are unicellular protists which have served as indicators of paleoceanographic and -climatic changes in polar regions. Examining the foraminifera?s microstructure can reveal information about the local environmental circumstances, particularly the levels of nitrate and oxygen, given the shifting conditions in the Arctic Ocean.

datasets.title: Time scale changes in the spatiotemporal variations in the community structure of meiofauna in the Arctic Kongsfjord.
datasets.abstract: Time-series studies on benthic meiofauna provide insights into the variability of meiobenthic communities across spatial and temporal scales. Sediment-inhabiting meiofauna, especially in the deep sea, are abundant and play critical roles in benthic food webs and ecosystem functioning. Their activities influence sediment properties, impacting services like stabilization, biochemical cycling, waste removal, and food web dynamics (Rose and Hauquier, 2012). Meiofaunal abundance, diversity, and community structure vary across time and spatial scales, often interactively. Regionally, variations are linked to surface productivity and the settling of organic matter, the primary energy source for benthic organisms (Thiel, 1983). Bathymetric gradients reflect organic material degradation en route to the seafloor. Factors like food and oxygen availability, sediment traits, seafloor topography, habitat heterogeneity, and bioturbation by larger fauna shape meiofaunal communities at smaller scales.
datasets.purpose: Marine biodiversity has grown in knowledge but remains less documented than terrestrial biodiversity due to the difficulty of accessing the marine biosphere. Exploring beyond surface waters requires specialized, costly, and time-intensive equipment, limiting precision and understanding. Biomonitoring is essential to address environmental changes caused by various pressures on marine ecosystems. Meiofauna, small benthic organisms, respond quickly to natural and human-induced changes, making them valuable for benthic monitoring. Kongsfjorden, influenced by Atlantic and Arctic water masses, has steep environmental gradients due to glacial inputs, reducing benthic biomass and diversity in the inner fjord. Light microscopy, traditionally used to study meiofauna, is time-consuming and requires taxonomic expertise. DNA-based methods like metabarcoding offer rapid, cost-effective biodiversity evaluations using molecular barcodes, such as COI and 18S genes.

This element will focus on the rate of vertical migration of zooplankton through time series studies (24 hrs) at selected locations of the fjord in various stations at various seasons and its contribution to the biogeochemical cycle of the ecosystem. Diel and ontogenic migration of zooplankton is proposed to be one of the important mechanisms in transporting carbon from the euphotic zone to the deep water and the amount of respiratory carbon transported from the euphotic zone by diel migrant mesozooplankton can be, at times, of the same order of magnitude as that of the gravitational particle sinking.

datasets.abstract: The specific objectives are as follows: A. Characterizing Ecosystem Scale Dynamics of Permafrost Thaw: i. Identify thermokarst areas in Svalbard and Ny-Alusend areas by long-term satellite data and reconnaissance surveys. ii. Develop a database of physical characteristics of these areas on an on-going basis. iii. Develop intra and inter-seasonal characteristics of thermokarst landscape areas using a range of measurements such as atmospheric GHGs (CO2 and CH4), optical surface reflectance, narrowband and broadband albedo and net energy fluxes at the surface level and various meteorological parameters. iv. Quantify aerosol transport and impacts on snow spectral albedo. B. Identifying Permafrost degradation through Geochemical Signatures: i. Establish an isotope mixing model that will quantify the variability of downstream water from glacial melt, permafrost/active layer thaw and rain over the field campaign of 2018.

datasets.abstract: The cryosphere, comprising polar ice sheets, sea ice, and permanently frozen high-latitude terrains, plays a critical role in regulating the global climate system. Arctic glaciers are particularly sensitive to climate change, and the Svalbard archipelago represents a unique transition zone between maritime and continental climatic regimes. Continuous glacier monitoring in this region is therefore essential to quantify climate-driven cryospheric changes. Following the establishment of the Indian Arctic Station at Ny-?lesund in 2008, the MoES, Government of India, through NCPOR, India was assigned the Vestre Broggerbreen glacier, where the Geological Survey of India has conducted mass balance, ablation, glacier dynamics, snout monitoring, geomorphological mapping, and GPR-based ice-thickness studies since 2010. Long-term observations indicate a predominantly negative mass balance.

datasets.title: Integrated monitoring of Vestre Broggerbreen glacier , Ny-Alesund, Svalbard, Arctic
datasets.abstract: Integrated Glaciological Monitoring of Vestre Broggerbreen, Ny-Alesund, Svalbard. SCIENTIFIC AIMS & OBJECTIVES: Glaciers are using as instrument in moderating, modifying and modulating the weather and climate. The monitored glacier network provides a highly useful tool for monitoring spatial and temporal climate and climate change for reconstructing and modelling past and future climatic scenario. However, the rate of snow accumulation and annual balance of the glacier is important factor for sustaining their health. Glaciers also store information about past climates in the ice as enclosed gas bubbles, layers of dust and ice chemistry. Change in climate scenario has very profound impact in precipitation pattern along and across the Svalbard. The observed global sea level rise is a matter of international concern. The calculated contributions to sea-level rise in 100 year up to 2100 vary from almost zero to about 6 cm by Arctic glaciers (Oerlemans, 2005).

datasets.title: Late quaternary palaeoclimatic interpretation of clay minerals in sediments of Ny-lesund area, Svalbard, Arctic.
datasets.abstract: The Ny-?lesund area on the eastern Br?gger Peninsula, Svalbard exhibits both maritime and continental glacial settings, along moderate climatic changes. Climate change is more prominent in the Arctic due to sea-ice interactions. The region has experienced glacial and interglacial phases during the Late Quaternary. This study reconstructs paleoclimate history using terrestrial diamictons, analyzed through multi-proxy sedimentological methods and dated by Optically Stimulated Luminescence (OSL). Results indicate the sediments are chemically unaltered, immature, and derived from low-grade metamorphic sources. SEM reveals dominant mechanical and physical weathering with glacial to glaciofluvial imprints. Clay minerals like illite, kaolinite, and chlorite vary by geomorphic setting. OSL ages (e.g., 16?1 ka, 62?4 ka, 87?6 ka, 113?7 ka) reflect multiple climatic fluctuations linked to glacial cycles during the Weichselian stage, marking significant glacial advances and retreats in the region.
datasets.purpose: 1. Understanding the sedimentation history including possible cycle of repetition/fluctuation. 2. datasets.abstract: This proposal aims to evaluate the meiobenthic organisms for its community function and dynamics, genetic variability of the major meiofaunal functional groups like Harpacticoids, Ostracods, Polychaetes, Oligochaetes,, Kinorhyncha, Gastrotrichs, Nematodes, Foraminiferans etc. and its role in trophic processes specific to organic production-mineralization and carbon turnover rate . A suitable community structure based model of meiobenthic community would be evolved that would give an insight on the benthic processes in relation to the functional groups in Kongsfjord. Meiofauna in general, are the dominant taxon, affect detrital decomposition and carbon transformation. Even though preliminary studies suggests the abundance and diversity of macrobenthic fauna and meiobenthic nematodes in Kongsfjorden system (Bijoy Nandan et al., 2013 & Krishna Priya et al 2013), a comprehensive and in depth scientific information is greatly lacking on the meiobenthic component, specific to the community.

datasets.title: Snow and glacier studies observations
datasets.abstract: Arctic region interacts with atmosphere and ocean, and respond to global warming showing visible signal of change in cryospheric elements. Ice sheet elevation and sea ice area monitoring have been carried out and is a continuing activity to better understand sea level rise and albedo feedback mechanisms. Svalbard provides an opportunity to collect in-situ data for cryospheric elements and meteorological parameters in arctic environment. It is crucial to develop and validate remote sensing based approach to understand the long-term spatio-temporal trend. Advance instrumentation will help us to retrieve snow and glacier sub-surface layer properties and to correlate them with remote sensing observations. It is also important to carry out a comparative study between high latitude and high altitude snow and glacier resources to understand climate change response on polar and H-K cryosphere regions.
datasets.purpose: Present study aim to carry out space based investigation using multi ?sensor, -frequency and temporal remote sensing observations to improve our understanding of glaciers, snow, ice sheet/caps, sea ice & permafrost dynamics in Arctic region. Ground studies are crucial to develop and validate remote sensing derived geophysical products over Arctic region which will be carried out over Svalbard region. We also plan for carrying out a comparative analysis of the response of cryospheric elements over high latitude (Svalbard) and high altitude (Himalaya) regions.

datasets.title: Microplastic pollution in Arctic environment: extents and dynamics within fjord ecosystems
datasets.abstract: The study investigates the presence and characteristics of microplastics and associated contaminants, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and heavy metals, in Ny-?lesund during winter. Snow and ice samples were collected from 15 geolocated sites. The results revealed an average microplastic concentration of 20 particles/L in snow, with fibers predominating. Polyester (PET), polyethylene (PE), and polypropylene (PP) were the most common polymers, highlighting both local and long-range contributions to Arctic microplastic contamination. Airborne microplastics, though detected in low quantities (four particles over 24 hours), emphasize the significance of atmospheric transport in introducing these pollutants to the region.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of this study is to investigate the presence, distribution, and characteristics of microplastics and associated contaminants, such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and heavy metals, in the Arctic environment during winter. Specifically, this research aims to understand the role of atmospheric deposition in introducing microplastics to remote regions like Ny-?lesund and their persistence in snow and ice. By analyzing snow, ice, and airborne particulate samples collected from 14 geolocated sites, this study seeks to identify the primary sources of microplastics in the Arctic and their potential environmental impacts. The study also aims to explore the interactions between microplastics and toxic contaminants, assessing how microplastics may act as vectors for pollutants like PAHs and heavy metals, which are adsorbed onto their surfaces.

In this context, there is an increased need in understanding the role of atmospheric aerosols in changing the snow Albedo, phenomenon like ?Arctic haze? and ?thinning of Arctic Sea? and perturbation to the radiation balance in the Arctic region. A more realistic evaluation of these changes is possible when long term measurements are made available from remote Arctic locations. It is important to note that while air pollution in most heavily populated areas of the world comes predominantly from local and regional emissions, pollution in the remote Arctic is primarily a result of long-range transport from source regions outside the Arctic.The strong anthropogenic influence over the Arctic Region is primarily due to the position of the Arctic polar front and presence of human population in Europe, North America and North Asia located north of polar front. In addition, the feedback and coupling between the Arctic.

datasets.title: Monitoring of Arctic precipitation
datasets.abstract: The growth and shrinkage of polar ice sheets (mass balance) is one of the crucial points for the calculation of global sea level rise. One of the important parameters controlling the mass balance of ice sheets is the precipitation. Rising global temperatures over the next few decades are likely to increase evaporation and accelerate the global hydrological cycle which may cause drying of subtropical areas and increase precipitation at higher latitudes. Precipitation in Polar Regions has been forecast to increase with potential increases in global temperature. Much of the precipitation occurring in polar regions are in the form of snowfall. Strong winds prevailing in many parts of the polar regions cause snow drift from the ground and contaminate the measurements by conventional precipitation gauges. Thus, our confidence in measurements of polar precipitation is low due to the lack of data and the difficulty in separating real precipitation from drifting snow.

datasets.title: Impact of glacial runoff and associated Arctic freshening on Microbial community Structure:A case study in Kongsfjorden
datasets.abstract: The Arctic atmosphere is warming three times faster than global rates causing increased ice melt which led to the loss of 1/4 of the multi-year ice in the Arctic Ocean during the summer of 2007. As a result the Arctic ocean is receiving increasing amounts of ice melt water, causing a rapid freshening of the ocean. Arctic freshening is a complex process involving multilevel impacts in the ecosystem, affecting key physical and biogeochemical properties, bringing considerable impacts to biodata whose cumulative impacts are difficult to predict. Increased satisfaction of the upper water column due to surface freshening could have a profound effect on nutrient transport into the euphotic zone and decrease the overall productivity of the Arctic Ocean. There is a little data on how these drastic physical changes affect the microbial food webs that support the higher tropic levels. The current proposal envisages studying the temporal changes in the community structure of culturable total.

However, the rate of snow accumulation and annual balance of the glacier is important factor for sustaining their health. Glaciers also store information about past climates in the ice as enclosed gas bubbles, layers of dust and ice chemistry. Change in climate scenario has very profound impact in precipitation pattern along and across the Svalbard. The observed global sea level rise is a matter of international concern. The calculated contributions to sea-level rise in 100 year up to 2100 vary from almost zero to about 6 cm by Arctic glaciers (Oerlemans, 2005). Svalbard glaciers are at the northern extremity of a zone of rapid transfer of heat through the Norwegian Sea, this whole area of Svalbard

datasets.title: Brown carbon and HULIS in the Arctic
datasets.abstract: The Arctic is a particularly sensitive region to global climate change. In this context, there is an increased need in understanding the role of atmospheric aerosols in changing the snow Albedo, phenomenon like ?Arctic haze? and ?thinning of Arctic Sea? and perturbation to the radiation balance in the Arctic region. A more realistic evaluation of these changes is possible when long term measurements are made available from remote Arctic locations. It is important to note that while air pollution in most heavily populated areas of the world comes predominantly from local and regional emissions, pollution in the remote Arctic is primarily a result of long-range transport from source regions outside the Arctic.The strong anthropogenic influence over the Arctic Region is primarily due to the position of the Arctic polar front and presence of human population in Europe, North America and North Asia located north of polar front. In addition, the feedback and coupling between the Arctic.

datasets.title: Characterizing Permafrost Degradation in Svalbard and its Impacts on Terrestrial Ecosystems
datasets.abstract: The specific objectives are as follows: A. Characterizing Ecosystem Scale Dynamics of Permafrost Thaw: i. Identify thermokarst areas in Svalbard and Ny-Alusend areas by long-term satellite data and reconnaissance surveys. ii. Develop a database of physical characteristics of these areas on an on-going basis. iii. Develop intra and inter-seasonal characteristics of thermokarst landscape areas using a range of measurements such as atmospheric GHGs (CO2 and CH4), optical surface reflectance, narrowband and broadband albedo and net energy fluxes at the surface level and various meteorological parameters. iv. Quantify aerosol transport and impacts on snow spectral albedo. B. Identifying Permafrost degradation through Geochemical Signatures: i. Establish an isotope mixing model that will quantify the variability of downstream water from glacial melt, permafrost/active layer thaw and rain over the field campaign of 2018.

datasets.title: Arctic Viral Communities
datasets.abstract: Viruses are the most abundant biological entities on the planet and are the reservoir of most of the genetic diversity in the sea. Every second, approximately 1023 viral infections occur in the ocean and these infections are a major source of mortality of marine organisms. In marine systems, virus-mediated processes have significant impacts on marine communities and are a major force behind biogeochemical cycles. However, the viral genetic diversity remains poorly characterized. Virus affect mortality and thereby influence the diversity of autotrophic and heterotrophic marine microbial communities; in turn this affects global geochemical cycles (Fuhrman,1999; Wommack and Colwell, 2000; Weinbauer, 2004;Suttle, 2005, 2007). Approximately 50% of bacterial production and up to 26% of the total organic carbon fixed by photosynthesis is lost through viral lysis each day (Fuhrman, 1999; Wilhelm and Suttle 1999).

datasets.title: Survival of mesophilic health significant bacteria in the fjord sediment, water and nearby tundra and role of mesophilic intruders in the disemination of antibiotic resistant genes in the Arctic environment
datasets.abstract: With prevailing warming trends in the Arctic it is anticipated that warm water currents will further extend their tongue into the arctic fjords along with their indigenous microflora, which will be allochthonous to the Arctic environment. Similarly fast retreating ice cover over tundra will provide ideal feeding ground for foraging species, especially the migrant birds from distant tropical places. The most important ones in the Svalbard are Barnacle goose (Branta leucopsis, Svalbard population) and Arctic Tern (Sterna paradisaea). Highly productive seas in the polar region during spring and summer seasons also attract several marine birds into the fjords. These invasions of microbial community especially the bacteria will have implications on diversity, nutrient cycles and introduction of health significant mesophiles and antibiotic resistant genes (ARG?s) in the arctic environment. Our studies on diversity of heterotrophic bacteria in the Kongsfjorden has clearly revealed entry.

datasets.title: Role of aerosols and precursor gases in direct radiative forcing over Arctic region at Ny-lesund.
datasets.abstract: Arctic is the remote polar region characterized by the highest surface albedo and one of the less illuminated by solar radiation for a major time period during the year. The Arctic continent can be expected to provide reference levels for all environmental and pollution studies due to its remoteness and restricted human activities. Thus, in this region, while the total mass of the aerosol particles suspended in the vertical atmospheric column of unit cross section yields smaller values, the lower aerosol optical depth at all the visible and near-infrared wavelengths is of great concern for Earth?s radiation budget studies. The attenuation of solar irradiance and the processes of scattering and absorption by the aerosol particles may cause appreciable effects on the radiative exchange mechanisms occurring in the Arctic atmosphere. Hence the aerosol properties and their effects on other weather and climate of this region are certainly different from other continental areas.

datasets.title: Role of atmospheric transport in alteration of wintertime airborne pathogenic microbial communities over Arctic: A study over Ny-Alesund
datasets.abstract: Present dataset comprises raw FASTQ files generated from V3-V4 16S rRNA gene and ITS region sequencing of air and precipitation samples collected during polar dark winter nights at Ny-Alesund, Svalbard (78.5?N, 11.8?E), as part of the first Indian winter-time Arctic expedition in 2024. Sampling was conducted at 48-hour intervals between 19th January and 10th February 2024.
datasets.purpose: The raw FASTQ files are provided to enable transparency, reproducibility, and reuse of the sequencing data. These files allow independent verification of sequence quality, taxonomic assignment, and downstream bioinformatic analyses, including quality filtering, denoising, amplicon sequence variant (ASV) inference, taxonomic classification, diversity analyses, functional prediction, and comparative microbiome studies. Public availability of the FASTQ data also facilitates meta-analyses, methodological benchmarking, and integration with future datasets to advance understanding of atmospheric microbial communities in polar environments.

datasets.title: Biomimetic approaches to decipher the decadal changes in meiobenthic community structure of the Arctic Kongsfjorden
datasets.abstract: The Arctic Kongsfjorden has emanated limited studies on the benthic fauna especially on the meiofauna and its ecosystem structure in the above cited context. So the P.I and his research group as part of the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR) program in the Arctic Kongsfjorden initiated field and laboratory analysis of the benthos specific to meiobenthos and its community structure in 2011, then later in 2015 to 2018 periods. Long term decadal meiofaunal data sets are rare, but of those available it appears are the years of primary recurring cycles of the meiofaunal assemblage. So, the need for decadal observations on the meiofauna is a prerequisite for our understanding on the community pattern and its functionality in the context of the sedimentary and pore water characteristics in highly unpredictable environment of the Arctic.

datasets.title: Ecology and functional diversity of Meiofauna in selected Arctic fjords.
datasets.abstract: This proposal aims to evaluate the meiobenthic organisms for its community function and dynamics, genetic variability of the major meiofaunal functional groups like Harpacticoids, Ostracods, Polychaetes, Oligochaetes,, Kinorhyncha, Gastrotrichs, Nematodes, Foraminiferans etc. and its role in trophic processes specific to organic production-mineralization and carbon turnover rate . A suitable community structure based model of meiobenthic community would be evolved that would give an insight on the benthic processes in relation to the functional groups in Kongsfjord. Meiofauna in general, are the dominant taxon, affect detrital decomposition and carbon transformation. Even though preliminary studies suggests the abundance and diversity of macrobenthic fauna and meiobenthic nematodes in Kongsfjorden system (Bijoy Nandan. 2013 & Krishna Priya et al 2013), a comprehensive and in depth scientific information is greatly lacking on the meiobenthic component, specific to the community.

datasets.abstract: The ill effects of climate change has caused a poleward shift in the distribution of species due to the rapidly rising water temperatures. This calls for an immediate need to assess and document the extent of climate change-driven animal migrations occurring in the Arctic waters. However, the extreme climatic conditions and the remoteness of the region makes biomonitoring tedious in the Arctic ecosystem. The present study puts forward a deep learning-based analysis of a large underwater video dataset that was captured from the Arctic region. The dataset was acquired by underwater cameras mounted on custom-made stainless-steel frames. The videos footages were collected over a period of 26 days from the Kongsfjorden- Krossfjorden twin Arctic fjords in Svalbard, Norway.

datasets.title: Black Carbon Mass Concentration
datasets.abstract: Arctic amplification is the faster increase in the mean surface temperature of the Arctic region than the global mean valu e. Atmospheric aerosols are tiny particles suspended in air in the size range of 0.001 μm to 100 μm. Aerosols have a signi ficant impact on the amplification of the Arctic. It could be due to the complex feedback mechanism, such as the decreas e in sea ice extent, which can influence the global radiation balance by reducing the surface albedo. datasets.title: Distribution of Surface-layer Prokaryotes in the Western Arctic Ocean: Responses to Pacific Water Inflow and Sea Ice Melting
datasets.abstract: The digital database holds 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequence data from surface waters of the western Arctic Ocean, covering four oceanic sectors: the Bering Sea (63?N?66?N), southern Chukchi Sea (66?N?71?N), northern Chukchi Sea (71?N?76?N), and the Central Arctic Ocean (76?N?79.5?N). This analysis aimed to understand how microbial community composition and functions shift along the Pacific water?s inflow path, which begins in the Bering Sea, passes through the Chukchi Sea, and extends into the central Arctic Ocean. Results indicate that Pacific water inflow and sea ice melt have a significant impact on the environmental characteristics of the region, leading to diverse prokaryotic community structures. Heterotrophic populations reliant on phytoplankton dominate in the Bering Sea and southern Chukchi Sea, while in the Central Arctic Ocean, chemoautotrophic bacteria and archaea are present alongside heterotrophs adapted to nutrient-poor (oligotrophic) conditions. Although no single group
datasets.purpose: To test the hypothesis, ?the inflow of warmer and nutrient-rich Pacific water would alter prokaryotic community structure and functions in the WAO regions, not only in the sea-ice-free coastal regions but also in the sea ice-covered central Arctic Ocean during the summer sea ice melt. This may lead to the habitat range expansion of prokaryotic clades that taxonomically and functionally resemble those of Pacific origin to the Arctic Ocean.? We examined the 16S rRNA gene amplicon data, along with a metagenome-based functional analysis, to study the prokaryotic communities in the upper epipelagic waters down to a depth of 100 meters. Our study provides essential insights into the impact of changing environmental conditions on prokaryotic distribution and biogeochemical cycles of the Arctic Ocean in the climate change scenario.

datasets.title: Monitoring of Arctic precipitation.
datasets.abstract: The growth and shrinkage of polar ice sheets (mass balance) is one of the crucial points for the calculation of global sea level rise. One of the important parameters controlling the mass balance of ice sheets is the precipitation. Rising global temperatures over the next few decades are likely to increase evaporation and accelerate the global hydrological cycle which may cause drying of subtropical areas and increase precipitation at higher latitudes. Precipitation in Polar Regions has been forecast to increase with potential increases in global temperature. Much of the precipitation occurring in polar regions are in the form of snowfall. Strong winds prevailing in many parts of the polar regions cause snow drift from the ground and contaminate the measurements by conventional precipitation gauges. Thus, our confidence in measurements of polar precipitation is low due to the lack of data and the difficulty in separating real precipitation from drifting snow.

datasets.title: Investigations of atmospheric aerosols and there characterization over the Arctic during summer season
datasets.abstract: Polar regions hold an important place while answering the key questions about the global climate change. The role of atmospheric aerosols in producing the ?Arctic haze? and associated phenomenon is well recognized. In view of reports on thinning of Arctic sea ice and phenomenon like Arctic haze due to increase in the industrialization in northern hemisphere, there is an increased need for a better understanding of aerosol properties as well as aerosol interaction with radiation in the Arctic regions. Arctic atmosphere is impacted by long range transport of dust and also from the emissions from mid latitude regions. Characterization of absorbing aerosols over high reflecting surfaces of snow and ice in Arctic are important, as they can reduce the surface albedo, thereby perturbing the radiation balance of Earth atmosphere system.

datasets.title: Functional diversity of Heterotrophic Bacteria in the water column and suracial sediments of Kongsfjord with special reference to those involved in carbon cycle
datasets.abstract: Heterotrophic bacteria play major role in the mineralisation of diverse organic substances available in the marine environment and contribute to productivity in a significant manner. Heterotrophic bacterial consortiums play key role in the breakdown of large molecular weight substances to smaller entities which will be further taken inside by the bacteria and utilized for metabolism. This way they covert lot of dissolved organic matter (DOM) to particulate organic matter (POM). The metabolism also leads to release of DOM by bacteria which in turn utilised by other members of the community. While the organic matter being transported from the surface to the bottom, the easy to digest fractions are being used up in the water column and hard to digest structural materials are likely to reach the bottom where they will be used up by the heterotrophic bacterial community in the surficial sediments as well as those residing within certain depth of the sediment.

datasets.abstract: The digital database contains 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequence data retrieved from the seawater column and melt pond of the western Arctic Ocean. The environmental variations and their interactions with the biosphere are vital in the Arctic Ocean during the summer sea-ice melting period in the current scenario of climate change. Hence, we analyzed the vertical distribution of bacterial and archaeal communities in the western Arctic Ocean from sea surface melt-ponds to deep water up to a 3040 m depth. Prokaryotic communities were analyzed using NGS (amplicon sequencing ) technology. The distribution of microbial communities showed a clear stratification with significant differences among different water depths, and the water masses in the Arctic Ocean; appeared as the major factor explaining their distribution in the water column. A total of 34 bacterial phyla were detected in the seawater and 10 bacterial phyla in melt-ponds.

datasets.title: Bulk detrital Nd and Pb isotope composition of sediments from International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) Expedition 379, core site U1532
datasets.abstract: This dataset presents neodymium (Nd) and lead (Pb) isotope compositions of bulk detrital sediments recovered from International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) Expedition 379, Site U1532, located in the Amundsen Sea, West Antarctica (2019). The data were generated to reconstruct the history of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet during the Pliocene?Pleistocene period. Nd isotope ratios were measured using a Multi-Collector Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer (MC-ICP-MS; Thermo Fisher Scientific Neptune Plus) at the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, India. Pb isotopic measurements were conducted using a Thermo Scientific Neptune Plus MC-ICP-MS at GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research, Kiel, Germany. This research was supported by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Government of India, and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, Germany.
datasets.purpose: This dataset presents neodymium (Nd) and lead (Pb) isotope compositions from detrital sediments at IODP Site U1532 in the Amundsen Sea, West Antarctica. It aims to reconstruct West Antarctic Ice Sheet (WAIS) dynamics during the Pliocene?Pleistocene transition?an interval critical for understanding ice sheet sensitivity to climate change. The isotopic data trace sediment provenance and glacial activity, offering direct evidence from a region experiencing current rapid ice loss. These records help identify past WAIS extent and constrain tipping points, supporting improved ice sheet modeling and projections of future sea-level rise under warming climate scenarios.

datasets.abstract: The variability of the Indian Summer Monsoon is of great interest to the inhabitants of the South Asian countries due to its direct relationship with the food security of the region. Monsoon manifests itself as a northward migration of the ITCZ from equator to upto 25?N. Although there are a number of meteorological features associated with the ISM, such as the North-South surface pressure and temperature gradient, low level south-westerly jet, upper level easterly flow and the monsoon trough to name a few, the North-South gradient of tropospheric temperature (TTG) is now widely accepted as a primary driver of the ISM (Xavier et al., 2007). Tropospheric heating helps maintain upper level divergence which leads to augmented convergence and uplift of moisture at the lower level.

datasets.abstract: The atmospheric aerosols are particles of solid or liquid phase dispersed in the atmosphere, produced either by the mechanical disintegration processes occurring over land (e.g. lift up of dust) and ocean (eg. sea spray) or by chemical reactions occurring in the atmosphere. The varied concentrations and composition of these aerosols have strong influence in altering the local climate and to some extent regional as well. Owing to their long-range continental origin and associated transport mechanisms, they can have potential impacts even on a global scale. Recent investigations, through both national and international campaigns reveal that aerosols have significant impact on radiation budget and act as cloud condensation nuclei, increase cloud albedo and reduce precipitation by decreasing the effective cloud droplet size. Knowledge of aerosol properties is essential in atmospheric correction procedures in satellite remote sensing of Earth's surface.

On the other hand, the ACC system connects all the major global ocean basins, acting as an important link to heat, salt, and momentum fluxes.
