datasets.title: Microbiology and Carbon Biogeochemistry
datasets.abstract: The coastal waters around Antarctica and adjoining Southern Ocean (SO) account for 13% of global primary productivity and play a major role in global biogeochemical cycle of 34carbon and nutrients (Longhurst et al., 1995, Sarmeinto and Le Qu?r?, 1996). Although SO is known to be major sink for atmospheric carbon dioxide, recent studies in the Indian Ocean sector of SO do show large-scale variability in fluxes of carbon across the air-sea boundary and its influence on organic matter (Prasanna et al., 2015, Soares et al., 2015). Primary production (PP) in these waters is highly heterogenous- coastal and shelf waters, oceanic fronts experiencing upwelling and Marginal Ice Zones (MIZ) are more productive than the open southern ocean waters (Moore and Abbott, 2000, Fitch and Moore, 2007) which are identified as High-Nutrient Low Chlorophyll (HNLC) waters. In these HNLC waters, availability of iron is an important limiting factor that influences PP.
datasets.purpose: 1.To study (a) bacterial diversity- Total, culturable forms and Siderophore producing bacteria, (b) bacterial characterization- identification of culturable and Siderophore producing bacteria. 2.To estimate carbon uptake rates and respiration rates in the euphotic layer. 3.To establish organic carbon inventory-source and molecular characterization in the water column. 4.To estimate the total flux and various components of particulate matter at one location.

datasets.title: Study of Metrology and Atmospheric Aerosols
datasets.abstract: The variations in concentrations and composition of the most important natural aerosol systems at the global level, the marine aerosols, strongly influencesthe local climate and to some extent regional climate as well. The aerosols can be classified into in-situ produced and the long-range transported aerosols. Studying the associated transport mechanisms, it?s known that the long range transported aerosols have potential impacts even on a global scale. Aerosols have significant impact on radiation budget, act as cloud condensation nuclei, increase cloud albedo and reduce precipitation by decreasing the effective cloud droplet size. Knowledge of aerosol properties is essential in atmospheric correction procedures in satellite remote sensing of earth?s surface.

To achieve novel antimicrobial compounds and the opportunity to access geographically diverse sampling areas and different ecological niches are of fundamentals importance. Southern Ocean, which harbors rich microbial diversity, seems to have a promising future in the development of novel biologically active substances.

datasets.title: carbon flux Over the Southern Ocean During VI SOE.
datasets.abstract: The Southern Ocean covers nearly 20% of the global ocean area. It is well known that the presence of circum-global current is responsible for mixing of water masses and most of the ventilation of deep-sea water masses, including CO2, takes place in the Southern Ocean. During summer SO acts as important sink of atmospheric carbon dioxide. The mechanism which demonstrates the sinking of carbon is through regional productivity. The factors responsible for enhancing the productivity of SO are nutrient supply, availability of sunlight, favorable wind condition etc. Because of its important role in carbon cycle, the Southern Ocean will continue to receive ample attention, despite the extraordinary challenges of working in as hostile an environment as the Antarctic region. Clear signs of warming is seen in both Antarctic Bottom Water and Antarctic Circumpolar Current.
datasets.purpose: 1. To understand the role of the Southern Ocean in the global carbon cycle.

Southern Ocean is an ecosystem where nutrient concentrations do not limit annual primary production; instead light acts as major factor limiting the phytoplankton population in the region (Campbell & Aarup, 1989; Nelson & Smith, 1991). Phytoplankton are the major absorbers of incoming solar radiations in the oceans.
datasets.purpose: The objective of the proposal was to study the phytoplankton absorption based on size fraction and effect of optically active substances on it, Phytoplankton size spectral algorithm validation for the determination of phytoplankton species in Southern Ocean waters, improvement of phytoplankton size spectral algorithms suitable for Southern Ocean waters and to make an in-situ bio-optical data base for ocean colour applications in Southern Ocean.

After the study of Silas (1968) no detailed studies have been undertaken for examing biodiversity of cephalopods from SIO and ISSO. The present status of cephalopodsdiversity and abundunce in the ISSOis largely unknown. Hence the studies on Cephalopodsdistribution, abundance in relation to oceanographic parameters are proposed.

datasets.title: Bio Optical Properties Of Southern Ocean During V Southern Ocean Expedition
datasets.abstract: All water bodies, from clear-water oceans covering large areas to small, form an important part of natural environment. Oceans have the greatest influence on the climatic and synoptic conditions. They also influence the economy of nations and the quality of human life. This influence is essentially determined by dynamic, thermal, chemical, biological, geological and optical properties of the ocean. The water properties of different water bodies show great variability, connected with their limnological/optical type, season, cyclic change of biological activity and human impact. Optical properties are determined by optically active water constituents (in addition of water itself) that are called ?water components?. The consequences of the human impact and the respective changes in the water environment of the SO and the correlation of productivity with respect to the satellite data can be studied by insitu water colour component analysis of the SO.
datasets.purpose: 1. To derive quantitative information on the types of substances present in the water and on their concentrations from variations in the spectral forms. 2. To derive algorithm to assess the productivity of the SO using the water colour components.

datasets.abstract: Actinomycetes were initially considered as one of the major groups of soil microbes. However, they have been increasingly isolated from various marine samples, deep sea sediments and near hydrothermal vents. In fact, distribution of actinomycetes in the sea water remains largely undescribed. it is now widely accepted that culture-based techniques are inadequate for studying actinomycetes diversity and application of molecular phylogenetic techniques would result in the discovery of many novel actinomycetes. Since no report is available on the diversity of marine actinomycetes from Indian sector of Southern Ocean, an attempt has been made to study the diversity of this important group during this expedition

datasets.title: Biology and Biochemistry of Southern Ocean Squids During VI Southern Ocean Expedition
datasets.abstract: Cephalopods are exclusively marine predators and voracious carnivores with high metabolic and conversion rates. They feed on live prey throughout their life. Cephalopod resources of the Southern Ocean are considered as distinct with other oceans with high level of endemism in squids. Cephalopods pay an important role in the ecology of SO and acts as a linkage between abundant mesopelagic fishes, crustaceans, sea birds and whales. Our knowledge on the food and feeding ecology of cephalopods in the SO is limited to the commercial species. More work is needed on the biology of cephalopods for better understanding of their role in marine ecosystems of the SO. Oceanic squids are a comparatively less exploited group and the information is scanty. Hence, during the SO expedition it is proposed to investigate the biochemical composition of oceanic squids and characterize protein and bioactive peptides. It also aims at the pharmacological evaluation of protein and bioactive peptides.
datasets.purpose: To study the biological and biochemical characteristics of oceanic squids

However, POM studies in the ISSO are very limited thus makes it important to study the biochemical characterization of POM and its variability across the different fronts and within the water column for a better understanding of the biological pump and the ocean carbon cycle.

datasets.title: Primary Production And Associated Biological Process And The Variation Of Biological And Physicochemical Components With Time During 5th Southern Ocean Expedition
datasets.abstract: SO is characterised by perennially high macronutrient levels yet low and constant levels of phytoplankton stocks. Fronts and water masses of the SO greatly influence the regulation of biological production at the global scale. At the low temperatures experienced in the Antarctica, a large temporal lag often exists between phytoplankton and mesozooplankton production, which has been suggested to cause the phytoplankton biomass to increase substantially. Microzooplankton is ubiquitous and since many are similar in size to their phytoplankton prey, it may be possible that they exert some control on certain phytoplankton functional groups, at least during the growing season. In the present expedition the main biological components of water column intended to be studied are: Chlorophyll a, primary production, phytoplankton, mesozooplankton and microzooplankton.
datasets.purpose: 1. To understand the primary production and associated biological process of the water column in the fronts and zones of SO. 2. Time-series observation to understand the role of physicochemical components on the biological productivity at selected fronts.
datasets.project_name: Primary Production And Associated Biological Process And The Variation Of Biological And Physicochemical Components With Time During 5th Southern Ocean Expedition

datasets.title: Physical processes During VI Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The subtropical front of the southern Hemisphere represents the northward limit of the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC) and is characterised by a strong thermal gradient. Climatic implications of STF include the opening and closing of ?Indian Gate way? in to the Atlantic resulting in ?Aghulhas leakage? that influence the Atlantic meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) (Biostach, etal., 2008). Agulhas leakage is a result of north-south excursion of the STF in association with the north-south movement of the westerly wind belt. The SST gradient with in the front also results in strengthening/weakening the storm tracks and the annular modes that in turn controls the north-south movement of the westerly wind belt. This region is also characterised by high chlorophyll values which in turn may have an important role in determining the SST gradients across the front.
datasets.purpose: 1. Understanding the diurnal variations of physical properties as well as the chlorophyll concentrations.
datasets.project_name: Physical processes During VI Southern Ocean Expedition.

datasets.title: Micro and Mesozooplankton Biomass and Diversity During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The spatio-temporal changes in the plankton community structure will have profound influence on the food web of the region. Zooplankton forms an integral part of the pelagic food web as the marine ecosystem functioning is strongly dependant on its structure and succession (Dur et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2009; Hafferssas & Seridji, 2010). Studies conducted in the Indian sector of Southern Ocean (SO) have observed significant variation in the distribution pattern of micro and mesozooplankton groups (Jasmine et al., 2009). The community structure with special emphasis on amphipods showed significant variation between the subtropical region and the polar region. A total of twenty species of amphipods were recorded from the SO, however only two species Themisto gaudichaudi and Primno macropa, were found exclusively in the Polar region (Elizabeth et al., 2014 Personal communication).
datasets.purpose: 1. Understand the microzooplankton diversity in different sectors (PF1, PF2, SAF and STF) of SO. 2. Identify the spatial zooplankton diversity gradients in different fronts. 3. Understand the variability in food web structure. 60 4. To study the inter relationship between physical, chemical and other biological elements with secondary standing stock and diversity pattern.

datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Physical oceanography During V Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: Due to its physical geography, the SO is a major pathway for exchange of water properties between ocean basins, and between the surface ocean and the deep. The Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC) system driven by mid-latitude surface westerly winds accounts for this large fluxes of heat, nutrients, and carbon in the climate system. At the same time, it effectively isolates the polar ocean from lower latitudes, giving rise to the coldest temperatures in the World?s ocean, deep surface mixed layers, and a large area of seasonal sea ice. These physical characteristics have profound impacts on SO biogeochemical cycles and ecosystems. The strong north-south tilt of density surfaces associated with the eastward flow of the ACC exposes the deep layers of the ocean to the atmosphere at high southern latitudes.
datasets.purpose: 1. Understand the diurnal variations of physical properties as well as the chlorophyll concentrations in the major frontal regions.
datasets.project_name: Physical oceanography During V Southern Ocean Expedition.

The focus of our study was to explore the diversity of Actinobacteria in different depths of water and sediment samples from SO. Culture dependent and independent studies were performed to determine the diversity of actinobacterial genera. Rare actinobacteria such as Chryseoglobus indicus, Micrococcus luteus, Rhodococcus erythropolis, Brachybacterium sp.,
datasets.purpose: This research work is primarily designed to create a baseline report on unculturable Actinobacteria from the ISO and the outcome of the study will help to isolate culturable forms of actinobacteria and also to understand the ecology of Actinobacteria in the ISO.

datasets.title: Investigation Of Mass Concentration Of Suspended Particulate Matter During 5th Southern Ocean Expedition
datasets.abstract: The mass concentration of suspended particulate matter (SPM) in the ocean varies in different regions and at different depths due to various biotic and abiotic factors and is also influenced by geographical location, productivity and the dynamics of its water masses. Various processes such as biological activity, lithogenic inputs mostly clay and rock detritus through the melting of ice, submarine volcanic activity, hydrothermal and extra-terrestrial inputs determine the composition of SPM. Also, as a result of re-suspension of sediments, a large volume of lithogenic particles are transferred within the interior of the ocean.
datasets.purpose: The knowledge of the distribution of SPM is an important prerequisite for the description and prediction of the ecological conditions. The fundamental physical and chemical properties of water may vary depending on the type and origin of SPM. The SPM in the water column regulates the penetration depth of light and therefore it is an important parameter influencing primary productivity. Elemental chemistry of SPM will help in understanding source of matter.
datasets.project_name: Investigation Of Mass Concentration Of Suspended Particulate Matter During 5th Southern Ocean Expedition

datasets.title: Routine monitoring of the upper ocean thermal fields in the seas around India.
datasets.abstract: For getting a better understanding of the sea surface salinity distribution and atmospheric conditions in the Indian sector of Southern Ocean (SO), the present expedition carried out meta-data as well as surface water sample collection (for salinity observation) at every three hourly interval from 12o 59.7'N and 81o 17.5'E onwards from 12-01-2013 to 26-02-2013. The collected salinity samples (-I50 nos) were analyzed using onboard Auto-SAL. In addition to this, XBT operations were carried out at twenty stations to understand the vertical distribution of temperature in the different fronts and zones of the SO. Among the 20 XBT operations, 5 were carried out simultaneously with CTD stations to validate XBT fall rate equation for the SO and also to calculate temperature bias with respect to CTD data. Also, 6 stations were done along the zonal transect in the polar front (PF) to understand the zonal variability in this region.

datasets.title: Phytoplankton Biomass, Productivity, Absorption and Suspended Matter.
datasets.abstract: Every drop of water in the upper layer (top 200 meters) of the ocean contains thousands of free-floating, microscopic flora called phytoplankton. Arguably one of the most consequential activities of marine phytoplankton is their influence on global carbon cycle and climate (Falkowski, 2002). The phytoplankton photosystem contains chlorophyll-a, which traps the incident sunlight, fix the carbon dioxide, release oxygen (photosynthetic production) and produce organic matter which serves as source of food for virtually all other marine life forms. Thus, they play a vital role in sustenance of almost all life forms in the marine ecosystem
datasets.purpose: 1.To understand the physical forcings responsible for controlling phytoplankton biomass/chlorophyll-a and PP in the study area. 2.To measure in situ phytoplankton absorption, CDOM (from satellite) and total suspended matter to understand their role in attenuating underwater light, and linking it to PP variability.

datasets.title: Phytoplankton taxonomy, physiology and biogeochemical studies
datasets.abstract: Phytoplankton the vital component of the ocean?s ecological and biogeochemical system are the key drivers in the cycling of the elements and plays role in the regulation of atmosphere carbon dioxide. The cycling of the carbon in particular is modulated by the phytoplankton through the mechanism of photosynthesis and respiration (Aiken et al 1992). The variation of phytoplankton biomass, production and groups leads ecosystem of varying trophic status, characterizes the oceans and hence need to quantify on basin wide and global scale (Maranon et al. 2000). Knowledge on the qualitative and quantitative distribution of phytoplankton will be of fundamental importance in any attempt to understand the biological response to climate variability.
datasets.purpose: 1) To study the phytoplankton community structure by using different techniques (Light microscopy, High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), Fluorometer and Flowcytometery). 2) Study of phytoplankton physiology and their role in Biogeochemical cycle 3) Collection of sediment core to study the temporal distribution of diatoms and dinoflagellate cyst.

datasets.title: Southern Ocean Carbon and Climate observations and Modeling
datasets.abstract: The Southern Ocean Carbon and Climate Observations and Modeling (SOCCOM) is increasing the spatial and temporal coverage of physical and biogeochemical parameters in the Southern Ocean, by deploying a fleet of autonomous profiling floats equipped with temperature, salinity, depth, pH, nitrate, oxygen, fluorescence and backscatter sensors. With a predicted lifetime of 5 to 7 years, the floats are informing about seasonal cycles of biogeochemical parameters, their interannual variability, wintertime and under ice processes, as most of the SOCCOM floats are also enabled to profile under sea ice, store the data and surface to report profiles after ice melts.
datasets.purpose: In order to increase the spatial and temporal coverage of biogeochemical and physical measurements in the Southern Ocean, it is imperative to understand the gaps in observations, in order to select regions where to deploy the floats. The south Indian Ocean is one of the regions of the Southern Ocean where biogeochemical observations are lacking most. The objective of SOCCOM on the SOE-10, 2017-18 expedition was therefore to deploy a series of profiling floats, in order to cover the different regimes in the Indian Ocean: Subtropical, Subantarctic, Polar, and Antarctic frontal zones. Seven profiling floats were planned to be deployed: Figure 7 shows the initial plan for the location of their deployment.

datasets.abstract: Southern Ocean is the ocean bordering Antarctica. It?s unique in many ways as compared to other oceans. It is the only region where water flows all around the globe unhindered and all the 57ocean merge here. Hence, it acts as a link between all the oceans. Most of deep and intermediate water formation takes place here. Southern Ocean is one of the major driver of global climate. So, studies from Southern Ocean has great implication on climate change and paleoclimate reconstructions.

datasets.title: Biogeochemistry of CO2 system, Oxygen and Nutrients in Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: The effect of ocean acidification is more pronounced in the cold polar waters, and acidification of the Southern Ocean is likely to impact on several key biogeochemical processes including plankton community structures, and nutrient and alkalinity cycles, formation of calcium carbonate particles, and ballasting of organic carbon in the sinking particulate fluxes. Carbon and nutrient cycling in the Southern Ocean are regulated by a complex interplay of physical, biological and biogeochemical processes, most of which are not well understood. The 23present study, integrating biogeochemical cycling of Carbon-di-oxide, Dissolved Gases, Macro nutrients and SPOM, was designed and implemented to improve our scientific understanding and predictive capability of the Southern Ocean ecosystem.
datasets.purpose: 1. Investigate the cycling and fate of carbon dioxide in the shallow coastal Antarctica: Prydz bay and along different frontal systems.2. To understand the nutrient dynamics ? processes governing its distribution. 3. Identify the sources and processes that determine the biogeochemical cycling of suspended organic matter. 4. Effect of ocean acidification on coastal Antarctic phytoplankton and micro zooplankton communities and associated biogeochemistry.

datasets.title: Role Of Antarctic Krill Euphausia Superba In The Biogeochemical Cycle In The Indian Ocean Sector Of Southern Ocean.
datasets.abstract: Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) is a large euphausiid, widely distributed within the Southern Ocean and is a key species in the Antarctic ecosystem, being a major food item for a large number of top predators such as whales, seals, and sea birds. Krills are very successful in the extreme environment of the Southern Ocean because they are capable of exploiting a food supply that is both patchy and seasonal. The importance of krill in the Southern Ocean has implications for food web dynamics, biogeochemistry, and a major potential for commercial exploitation. Knowledge on the growth patterns, feeding and energy transformation are vital in understanding their population dynamics. A variety of approaches have been used to investigate krill growth such as by using length frequency of natural populations as well as direct measurements with the Instantaneous Growth Rate method and recently biochemical indicators of growth are identified as a possible alternative method.
datasets.purpose: Resource survey and ecology of Krill dwelling in southern ocean surface waters.

datasets.title: Biogeochemical studies with special reference to Polar Fronts During VII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The Southern Ocean is recognized as a region of major significance .in the biogeochemical cycle of carbon and nutrients. lt is the largest high-nutrient low-chlorophyll (HLNC) zone of theglobal ocean, The SO is the source and sink for several intermediate and deep water masses of the world oceans. In the SO, there exist various frontal waters, like the Subtropical Front (STF), Subantarctic Front (SAF), the Polar Front (PF) and Antarctic coastal waters. Frontal waters are highly complex systems formed at the mixing .of distinctly different water masses, and hence are physic-chemically 'dynamie regions. Certain areas in the SO can act as a sink for C02 by absorbing carbon from the atmosphere by various physical and biochemical processes which help in export of carbon from the surface layer to the deep ocean and finally to the sediments.
datasets.purpose: 1. Investigate the fate ofcarbon dioxide in the PF waters.

Nevertheless, the exponential increase of CO2 concentration in response to an array of anthropogenic perturbations congregated a momentum to the realization of its vital role in climate change (Keeling, 1958). In regulating the atmospheric CO2, the Southern Ocean play a major role (Broecker & Henderson, 1998) by acting as a sink particularly during the summer at southern hemisphere (Takahashi et al., 1993). In order understand the CO2 variability across various fronts of the SO; atmospheric air and surface sea water were collected from 14?53.011'S 76?19.514'E to 42?24.663'S 57?31.454'E.

datasets.title: Studies of Delta 13C and Delta18O of Atmospheric CO2 to Understand the Temporal Variation in the CO2 Sinking
datasets.abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is the primary greenhouse gas responsible for the global warming. The concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere is increasing since the pre-industrial times. Emissions of CO2 from fossil fuel combustion and industrial processes contributed about 78% of the total GHG emissions increase from 1970 to 2010, (IPCC, 2014). The CO2 concentration has been increased from 280 ppm to 407 ppm between mid-1800 to 2016. Though this concentration is very small which is ~0.04%, this could increase the global temperature significantly [Roy et al., 2007]. In carbon cycle the carbon is exchanged between different parts of earth system. Photosynthesis, respiration, volcanic emission, weathering are some of the important process in carbon exchanges. The ocean and photosynthesis are major sink for this atmospheric CO2.

So, in the recent past, isolation of actinobacteria has been mainly done as part of drug discovery programs, focusing on terrestrial sources; but recent efforts have been directed towards the marine environments because of the increasing discovery rate of new actinobacterial isolates from here and their promising bioactive compounds (Bull et al., 2000).

datasets.title: Biochemistry and hydrodynamics of the Indian Ocean sector of Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: The Southern Ocean plays a prominent role in controlling the global ocean?atmospheric climate system. The Southern Ocean water, spanning a wide range of density is directly forced by exchange of momentum, heat and fresh water with the overlying atmosphere and sea ice. The air? sea?ice interactions strongly modify the physical and chemical properties of outcropping layers and transform water from one density class to another. The water masses formed in this way ventilate a substantial fraction of the world ocean volume and are a key link in the global overturning circulation. Several water masses that ventilate the abyssal and intermediate depths of the world oceans have their origin in the Southern Ocean. These water masses play an important role in the global climate system as reservoirs of heat, freshwater and dissolved gases and act as a damping mechanism on variations in the global climate.
datasets.purpose: 1. To describe the thermohaline structure and water mass transformations.

datasets.title: Phytoplankton Productivity and Radiometric Measurements During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: Every drop of water in the upper layer (top 200 meters) of the ocean contains thousands of free-floating, microscopic flora called phytoplankton. Arguably one of the most consequential activities of marine phytoplankton is their influence on global carbon cycle and climate (Falkowski, 2002). In presence of light, the phytoplankton are able to fix carbon dioxide, release oxygen (photosynthetic production) and produce organic matter which serves as source of food for virtually all other marine life forms. Thus, they play a vital role in sustenance of almost all life forms in the marine ecosystem. The physiological responses of phytoplankton vary as a function of light regime, temperature, and nutritional status. A major goal in understanding how ocean dynamics affect phytoplankton production and carbon cycles is to determine how photosynthetic processes respond to geochemical and physical phenomena.
datasets.purpose: 1. To validate stable carbon isotope (13C) method by calibration exercise between radioactive ( 14C) and dissolved oxygen methods in the study area. 2. datasets.title: Isotopic Characterization of the Hydrological Cycle over the Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: There are various the naturally occurring stable isotopes of hydrogen and oxygen. In nature there are three stable isotopes of Oxygen (16O, 17O, and 18O) and two stable isotopes of Hydrogen (1H and 2H or D). The combinations of two hydrogen isotopes and one oxygen isotope are called stable water isotopes or stable water isotopologues. Out of a nine possible isotopologues only three are found in measurable concentrations i.e.: H2O16, H2O18 and HDO. Although normal or light water, which includes only light isotopes (i.e., H2O16), is much more common, heavy water containing heavy stable isotopes (i.e., H2O18, H2O17, and HDO) occurs in regular proportions on Earth.
datasets.purpose: 1. validate the theoretical values predicted using simple and atmospheric general circulation models. 2. validate the satellite based remote sensing measurements of isotopes in the atmosphere. 3. study the role of relative humidity, sea surface temperature and wind speed in governing the deuterium excess in vapor.

datasets.title: Synoptic Observations of the Trace Metal-Nutrient Distributions and Interactions in the Surface Waters of Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: There are three main ocean regions where high concentrations of macronutrients persist throughout the algal growth season, the North Pacific, equatorial Pacific and Southern Ocean. Of the three regions, the Southern Ocean is thought to have a disproportionate effect on global climate (Sarmiento et al., 1998; Sarmiento and Hughes, 1999). There are certain biogeochemical features of the Southern Ocean that are unique or unusual, particularly south of the Polar Front, where high concentrations of macronutrients nitrate, silicic acid and phosphate persist throughout the year. The surface waters of the Southern Ocean are also characterised by their high concentrations of bioutilised trace-metals such as Ni, Cu and Zn (Martin et al., 1990; Nolting and de Baar, 1994). The extremely low levels of Fe in the Southern Ocean are well documented (Martin et al., 1990; de Baar et al., 1999), and the role of Fe in limiting phytoplankton growth in this region has been suggested (de Baar et al., 1995).
datasets.purpose: To study the distributions of the trace metals and their coupling with the major nutrients in the surface waters of Southern Ocean

datasets.title: Impacts of Iodine Volatilisation from the Sea Surface
datasets.abstract: Recent research has identified that the reaction of iodide with ozone (O3) at the sea surface plays a critical role in controlling the chemical composition of the troposphere. This process directly controls the rate of O3 deposition to the oceans and is the dominant source of reactive iodine to the atmosphere, which also leads to significant chemical loss of tropospheric O3.In addition to direct loss of O3, iodine processes also influence other atmospheric oxidants leading to indirect effects on methane and aerosols with ramifications on climate, air quality and food security. This O3-iodide interaction is likely a negative biogeochemical feedback on tropospheric O3 and oxidants. Its dependence on O3 itself suggests that significant changes in its magnitude will have occurred from the turn of the 20th century, and its dependence on ocean iodide suggests changes over longer timescales; hence iodine.
datasets.purpose: Measuring the parameters necessary; mainly iodide surface concentration and IO emissions, to improve our understanding of the air-sea fluxes of iodine inorganic species, in a region where observations are notably lacking. -First simultaneous observations of IO and [I-] in real world observations. -Validate or improve the existing parameterisation for the prediction of iodide surface concentration and IO and HOI fluxes, through correlations of in-situ measured biogeochemical parameters such as SST, MLD, nutrients, wind speed and chlorophyll a. -Completing the mapping of iodine concentration in the surface seawater and through the water column, particularly in the Indian Ocean where this data is lacking and quantify the impacts of ocean mixing on iodine speciation; understanding and prediction of how iodide fields may change in the future (and past) ocean.
datasets.project_name: Impacts of Iodine Volatilisation from the Sea Surface

datasets.title: Physical Oceanographic Processes
datasets.abstract: The 9th expedition planned to conduct intense high resolution hydrography measurements in the Prydz Bay (PB). The PB, in East Antarctica, in the IOSO is a triangular-shaped embayment covering an area of about 80,000 km2. This region plays a crucial role in SO circulation, bottom and deep water formation, carbon sequestration and biological productivity. Compared to the Antarctic Peninsula, the Weddell and Ross Seas, relatively little attention has been paid to understand the complex physical processes occurring in the PB. To have a better understanding of PB hydrodynamics as well as its role on circulation and bottom and deep water formation in the IOSO high frequency observations needs to be carried out. The hydrography measurements are planned along the shallow (~500 m depth) and continental slope regions.

datasets.abstract: The Southern Ocean provides a critical link in the large‐scale ocean circulation and makes significant contributions to global budgets of heat, carbon, freshwater and nutrients. Southern Ocean covers about 20% of the global ocean surface area, yet accounts for approximately 40% of the global anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO2) uptake (Sabine et al., 2004). A major characteristic of large portions of the Southern Ocean is that the surface macronutrients are utilized inefficiently due to poorly understood interactions among iron, macronutrient, and light limitation, and physical mixing processes. The absorption of anthropogenic carbon dioxide into the ocean causes seawater to become more acidic.
datasets.purpose: 1. Investigate the cycling and fate of carbon dioxide in the Indian sector of Southern Ocean. 2. Investigate the biogeochemical cycling of dissolved oxygen, nitrous oxide and methane in southern ocean water. 3. To understand the nutrient dynamics ? processes governing its distribution along different frontal systems. 4. Identify the sources and processes that determine the biogeochemical cycling of suspended organic matter.
datasets.project_name: Carbon-di-oxide, Dissolved Gasses and Macro Nutrients
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Nitrification Experiment During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: Sequential ammonium (NH4 + ) oxidation to nitrite (NO2 - ) and eventually nitrate (NO3 - ) is collectively known as ?Nitrification? in pelagic ocean, which is a significant pathway that fuels new production in the euphotic zone and also provides oxidized electron acceptor to support anoxic respiration (Ward, 2011). The microbial communities that perform ammonia oxidations or the ammonia oxidizers, named as per their functioning, are potential contenders for the community involved in regenerated production below the euphotic layer. This autotrophic process consumes O2 and also produces N2O as a by-product which is potential green house gas. Another ill effect of this process is that it acidifies the ambient environment by producing free H+ . Rate of this nitrogen transformation process is dependent on different environmental condition. Among them, pH is one of the important variable possesses with direct positive impact.
datasets.purpose: 1. To investigate spatial distribution and magnitude of nitrifying activities along the different frontal zones of Southern Ocean. 2. To study the distribution and quantify the abundance of Ammonia oxidizing and nitrite oxidizing bacteria along Indian sector of Southern Ocean. 3. To evaluate the controls of environmental conditions on the rates nitrification.
datasets.project_name: Nitrification Experiment During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Micro and Mesozooplankton Biomass and Diversity During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The spatio-temporal changes in the plankton community structure will have profound influence on the food web of the region. Zooplankton forms an integral part of the pelagic food web as the marine ecosystem functioning is strongly dependant on its structure and succession (Dur et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2009; Hafferssas & Seridji, 2010). Studies conducted in the Indian sector of Southern Ocean (SO) have observed significant variation in the distribution pattern of micro and mesozooplankton groups (Jasmine et al., 2009). The community structure with special emphasis on amphipods showed significant variation between the subtropical region and the polar region. A total of twenty species of amphipods were recorded from the SO, however only two species Themisto gaudichaudi and Primno macropa, were found exclusively in the Polar region (Elizabeth et al., 2014 Personal communication).
datasets.purpose: 1. Understand the microzooplankton diversity in different sectors (PF1, PF2, SAF and STF) of SO. 2. Identify the spatial zooplankton diversity gradients in different fronts. 3. Understand the variability in food web structure. 60 4. To study the inter relationship between physical, chemical and other biological elements with secondary standing stock and diversity pattern.
datasets.project_name: Micro and Mesozooplankton Biomass and Diversity During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Oceanic Volatiles and their Impact on Atmospheric Halogens and Cloud-forming Aerosols in the Southern Ocean.
datasets.abstract: Marine microbiota (plankton) produce a great variety of metabolites and waste substances, some of which are volatiles that eventually get into the atmosphere by air-sea exchange processes and act as aersosol and cloud precursors. Evidence so far indicates that plankton influence by these means the optical properties of the atmosphere and consequently the planetary radiative budget (e.g., Lana et al. 2012), but too many unknowns remain for an accurate assessment and modelling of this natural process in both the preindustrial and the AnthropoceneEarths. The unknowns on the oceanic side arise from our poor understanding of the ecophysiological mechanisms that make marine microbiota produce volatiles. Gaining knowledge of the underlying biological processes is essential if we are to incorporate climate-biosphere feedbacks in Earth System models
datasets.purpose: a)Quantify the impacts of halogens on the chemistry of the open ocean troposphere: i.Measure halogens in the atmospheric boundary layer with MAX-DOAS and compare the data with emissions of the main source (organic - inorganic) in the marine environment. Observations made by the University of York will help constrain the iodine emissions. ii.Study the impact of reactive halogen species on the oxidation capacity through interaction with ozone (measured), dimethylsulphide (DMS) (data available from other cruises) and mercury (modelled). iii.Study the impact of iodine oxide on particle formation. b)Study the distribution of glyoxal in the atmospheric boundary layer and whether the ocean-leaving isoprene flux can explain the atmospheric concentrations.
datasets.project_name: Oceanic Volatiles and their Impact on Atmospheric Halogens and Cloud-forming Aerosols in the Southern Ocean.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Zooplankton Biomass, Diversity and Grazing During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The southern Ocean (SO) is the largest upwelling region in the world ocean but it is also the only one where the bulk of the upwelling macronutrients nitrate and phosphate is return with downwelling surface water to the ocean interior. In striking contrast, the bulk of the upwelling silicic acid is taken up by diatoms in the surface mixed layer across the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC). The low phytoplankton standing stocks in the Southern Ocean have been attributed to lower growth rates due to deep mixing of surface waters (i.e. low light regime) (Sakshaug & Hansen, 1984) and iron deficiency (Martin et al., 1991). It has also been suggested that low iron concentrations might affect mainly larger phytoplankton species (diatoms), explaining the predominance of smaller cells (nanoplankton) in Southern Ocean waters.
datasets.purpose: 1. To quantify the variability in vertical zooplankton biomass and abundance. 2 To examine the variability in vertical of zooplankton community structure and their ecological niche. 3. To understand the influencing and controlling factors for zooplankton vertical migration. 4. To estimates the phytoplankton growth rates and potential grazing pressure.
datasets.project_name: Zooplankton Biomass, Diversity and Grazing During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: SO biogeochemical cycling During V Southern Ocean Expedition
datasets.abstract: SO is of considerable interest since it plays a significant role in global biogeochemical cycling and climate change. It also plays a vital role in the context of the global carbon cycle and glacial-interglacial changes in atmospheric pCO2, due to its large nutrient reservoir, which generally never gets exhausted in open-ocean systems. Hence, large areas of SO may be regarded as typical high-nutrient/low chlorophyll regions (HNLC), probably due to limiting micronutrients such as iron (Martin et al., 1990). It is characterized by large seasonal variability in its environmental characteristics and is one of the important areas to be studied since the waters of the SO directly or indirectly affect the Indian Ocean and thus the Indian climatic regime. SO characterized by different fronts and frontal regions plays an active role in governing the distribution of chemical and biological parameters within the ocean.
datasets.purpose: 1. To understand the effect of critical elements (Fe and Co) on phytoplankton productivity. 2. To study the distribution of nutrients, total carbon and trace metals in the SO. 3. To study the variation of total suspended matter and its component composition over a day at two frontal regions.
datasets.project_name: SO biogeochemical cycling During V Southern Ocean Expedition
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Diatom Biocoenosis and Thanatocoenosis (Phytoplankton Community Structure), Carbon Dynamics and Measurements of Macro and Micro Nutrients in Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: Earlier studies have suggested that the palaeoclimatic reconstructions from continental ice cores and marine sediment cores in Polar Regions revealed a common pattern in climate events during the late Quaternary. Thus the Palaeoenvironmental reconstructions will quantify the timing and extent of short scale climate events of the Late Quaternary, comparing records from the two hemispheres. This high resolution studies will help us to evaluate the tele-connection between the northern and southern hemisphere. Different groups from NCAOR and other institutes have undertaken projects investigating the role played by the Southern ocean on global climate and relating the different geological phenomena at work and the changes in climate and global oceanic circulations by studying the microfossil like foraminifera and diatoms and employing other climatic proxies including biogenic silica, magnetic proxies and geochemical parameters.
datasets.purpose: To study the temporal variability in micropalaeontological (study of abundance and stable isotopic variation of planktic and benthic foraminifera and diatom), major, minor and trace element records during the late Quaternary.
datasets.project_name: Diatom Biocoenosis and Thanatocoenosis (Phytoplankton Community Structure), Carbon Dynamics and Measurements of Macro and Micro Nutrients in Southern Ocean
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Survey of Marine Mammals During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The Southern Ocean accounts for about 10% of the world s oceans and probably supports >50% of the worlds marine mammal biomass, including six species of pinnipeds, eight species of baleen whales, and at least seven species of odontocete whales. The various currents, gyres, eddies, and fronts of the Southern Ocean waters make highly productive, marine environment and one of the most important feeding grounds for cetaceans. Many marine mammals in the Southern Ocean feed on Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba), aggregating in foraging areas where krill are most abundant, especially in summer. The Southern Ocean provides important foraging habitat for several whale species and consequently has been declared by the International Whaling Commission as a whale sanctuary. Visual surveys of cetaceans can provide quantitative information on the abundance and distribution of cetaceans at the species level over large areas and thus identify areas of concern for management of their populations.
datasets.purpose: The objective of the present investigation is to determine the distribution, migration patterns and habitat preferences of cetaceans in the Southern Ocean.
datasets.project_name: Survey of Marine Mammals During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Spatio-temporal Variability of Aerosol and Associated Radiative Forcing - In Response to Local Meteorological Variability and Effects of Long Range Transport Over Indian Sector of Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: The in-situ produced aerosols are generally trapped in the lowermost layer of the atmosphere referred to as Planetary Boundary Layer (PBL) or Marine Atmospheric Boundary Layer (MABL)[Wilcox et al., 2016]. The BL dynamics play important role in transportation and concentration of aerosols. In spite of several field campaigns conducted in this field most of the studies are restricted in the northern sector of southern ocean. Furthermore, very less information is available explaining the role and effect of aerosols on the climate of Indian sector of southern ocean. Hence it is important to understand the basic issues related to atmospheric aerosols with respect to their physical and optical characteristics, composition, ABL dynamics and the radiative forcing to understand the impact of atmospheric aerosols comprehensively.
datasets.purpose: 1.To study spatial and temporal variability of Black Carbon (BC) mass concentration and size fraction of composite aerosols over southern ocean atmospheric domain. 2. To understand local meteorology and long range transport of atmospheric aerosols. 3. Optical characterization of aerosols by analyzing spectral variation of the columnar AOD, estimation of aerosol size spectrum (α) and atmospheric turbidity (β) parameter through ship based and satellite observations and its validation. 4. To determine the chemical composition of aerosol samples in SO. 70 5. To understand thermodynamic and stability structure within troposphere through vertical profiles of meteorological parameters over southern ocean. 6. To estimate direct aerosol radiative forcing and heating rate over southern ocean for climate studies.
datasets.project_name: Spatio-temporal Variability of Aerosol and Associated Radiative Forcing - In Response to Local Meteorological Variability and Effects of Long Range Transport Over Indian Sector of Southern Ocean
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.abstract: The phytoplankton acts major and central role in the ocean?s ecological and biogeochemical services, as they constitute the basis of the marine food web. In addition they are the key drivers in the cycling of the elements, plays role in the regulation of atmosphere carbon dioxide. The carbon uptake by phytoplankton and its export as organic matter to the oceanic interior known as the biological pump which they lowers the partial pressure of CO2 in the upper surface water of ocean.

datasets.title: Culture dependent and culture independent diversity of marine actinomycets During VII Southern Ocean Expedition
datasets.abstract: In Southern Ocean life forms have been evolved through natural selection for capable of occupying the habitats that offer protection from the desiccating conditions (de la To1Te et al., 2003) and these environments are very high in productivity compared to other ecosystem like terrestrial, aquatic and coastal ecosystem (Virginia and Wall, 1999). Microorganisms are the most abundant life forms in Antarctica and southern ocean and it have a wide diversity of cold adapted microorganisms including bacteria, arehaea, yeast and microalgae as reported earlier (Russell, 2006). Especially prokaryotes dominate many glacier ecosystems where they play a major role in the food chains, biogeochemical cycling of nutrients, and the mineralization of pollutants (Nichols et al., 1997).

datasets.title: Mg/Ca and reconstructed SST data of sediment core ABP-S4, collected from the Indian Sector of the Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: The sediment core ABP-S4 was collected from the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean (40?3?30??S; 48?5?44??E, 3665 m depth). The chronology of the core is based on AMS 14C dates. Age-depth modelling was performed using the program-Undatable. SST values were estimated using a recently developed Bayesian model- BayMag which includes multivariate non-thermal sensitivities from pH, salinity, cleaning and dissolution. The record spans a period from 3.4 Ayr BP to 39.09 Ayr BP. The data file includes age-depth constraints, measured Mg/Ca values, and estimated SST. Mg/Ca analysis was performed using ICP-OES.
datasets.purpose: This dataset provides Mg/Ca and reconstructed SST data from sediment core ABP-S4, offering insights into past oceanographic and climatic conditions in the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean

datasets.title: Physical Oceanographic Processes During VIII Southern Ocean Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The Southern Ocean (SO) is often defined as the area encompassing the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC) and regions to the south. This region is a major pathway for exchange of water properties between ocean basins, and also between the surface ocean and the deep. Pathways and mechanisms of oceanic heat and fresh water transports are critical issues in the comprehension of the present climate and its stability (Sloyan & Rintoul, 2001; Sarmiento et al., 2004). The ACC is driven by mid-latitude surface westerly winds and accounts for this large fluxes of heat, nutrients, and carbon in the climate system. At the same time, it effectively isolates the polar ocean from lower latitudes, giving rise to the coldest temperatures in the world?s ocean, deep surface mixed layers, and a large area of seasonal sea ice.
datasets.purpose: 1. To study the interannual variability of fronts and watermasses in the Indian sector of Southern Ocean along 57? 30?E. 2. To understand the small mixing rates along different fronts of the SO. 3. Comparison of XBT, XCTD and CTD for depth bias correction. 4. To study the influence of physical processes on biological production.

One of the major operations was the profiling of the water column using CTD (SeaBird Electronics, USA). This digital database contains the CTD data collected at the various locations during this cruise

datasets.title: Isotope Finger Printing of Waters of India
datasets.abstract: Realizing the importance of stable isotope in hydrology, Department of Science and Technology, Govt. of India has decided to promote the research for investigating the spatial and temporal fingerprinting of water sources of India using stable isotopes and tritium as a national program. The aim of this study is to improve understanding of the geographic and seasonal evolution of the components of the local and regional hydrological cycles, interactions between the various components and controls exercised by geographic factors and climatic forcing. The National Institute of Oceanography has taken the responsibility of collecting surface water samples from Arabian Sea and southern ocean besides collecting other upper air and surface meteorological parameters.
datasets.purpose: 1. Identifying dominant sources of water vapour supply (Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, Southern Ocean, local and long distant continental sources) at different locations within the country during different seasons.
datasets.project_name: Isotope Finger Printing of Waters of India

datasets.title: Geochemical Data from Sediment Core SOE11-GC03: Glacial-Interglacial Variations in Natural Iron Fertilization Along Eastern Antarctica
datasets.abstract: This dataset contains high-resolution geochemical data from sediment core SOE11-GC03, retrieved from the eastern continental margin of Antarctica. The data spans the last ~27,000 years, capturing glacial-interglacial cycles and their impact on micronutrient flux, natural iron fertilization, and paleoproductivity. Elemental concentrations, including proxies for productivity, weathering indices, and micronutrients are included. These parameters provide insight into the interaction between oceanographic processes, sea ice dynamics, and climate variability. The dataset is significant for advancing the understanding of Southern Ocean biogeochemistry and its role in global carbon cycling. It supports investigations into micronutrient utilization, sea ice retreat, and productivity changes during the Holocene and glacial terminations, serving as a valuable resource for reconstructing past climate dynamics in the southern polar region.
datasets.purpose: The purpose of this dataset is to provide a comprehensive geochemical record from sediment core SOE11-GC03, enabling the reconstruction of glacial-interglacial variations in natural iron fertilization, paleoproductivity, and weathering processes along the eastern Antarctic continental margin. By offering high-resolution data on micronutrient fluxes and productivity proxies over the last 27,000 years, the dataset supports studies on the interplay between oceanographic processes, sea ice dynamics, and regional climate variability.
datasets.project_name: Past Climate and Ocean Studies
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Study of paleoclimatology and paleoceanography of the Indian Sector of the Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: The proposed project aims to specifically fill this knowledge gaps by generating high resolution multiproxy reconstructions of paleoproductivity, paleotemperature, paleosalinity and oceanic circulation patterns in the key regions of the Southern Ocean regions. The present and past investigations in the Southern Ocean offer opportunity to study carbon cycle functioning in the present and during the glacial-interglacial periods. The interpretation of carbon sequestering mechanism in the past and in the near future will provide better insights about air sea carbon linking in the past and potential influence of ocean acidification in the future.
datasets.purpose: 1. Late Quaternary climatic variability and paleoproductivity in the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean utilizing microfossils and nannofossils
datasets.project_name: Study of paleoclimatology and paleoceanography of the Indian Sector of the Southern Ocean

datasets.title: Role of Antarctic krills in the biogeochemical cycle in the Indian Ocean sector of Southern Ocean
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic krill is the largest euphausiid, widely distributed in the Southern Ocean and is a key species in the Antarctic ecosystem, being the major food item for a large number of top predators such as whales, seals and sea birds. Three Species of krills namely Euphausia lucens Hansen, 1905, E. frigida Hansen, 1911 and Thysanoessa sp., were collected during the expedition. The absence of any stage of E. superba in the surface layers suggests that this species may not be migrating up to the surface while performing the vertical migration. E. frigida was the abundant species in the study area.
datasets.purpose: The distribution of krill species Euphausia lucens, E. frigida, and Thysanoessa sp. was studied during this expedition.
datasets.project_name: Role of Antarctic krills in the biogeochemical cycle in the Indian Ocean sector of Southern Ocean
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: A Note on Job Satisfaction Level of Scientists and Logistic Personnel in Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.abstract: Recently attention was paid to assess different psychological phenomena of Indian scientists in Antarctic expeditions. Prior studies were conducted to assess personality traits of Antarctic expeditioners (Dutta Roy, 1992), differential patterns of state anxiety level of scientists across their journey, stay in and return from the Antarctica (Dutta Roy and Deb, 1996). Scientists and logistic personnel visit Antarctica with defined assignments. During their work in Antarctica, a barren land, they may face some troubles in performing the job, that rnay result in some changes to their job satisfaction level. Since, no studies paid attention to the job satisfaction of Antarctic expeditioners, present study aimed at determining patterns of job satisfaction level of both scientists and logistic personnel.
datasets.purpose: The term job satisfaction was brought to the limelight by Hoppock (1935). He reviewed 32 studies on job satisfaction conducted prior to 1933 and observed that it is a combination of psychological, physiological, and environmental circumstances that cause a person to say, ?I am satisfied with my job?. It refers to one's satisfaction with phenomenological experience on job. It assesses the difference between individual's expectation and what actually individual receives. S u c h definition indicates the variety of variables that influence the satisfaction of the individual. In Antarctic expedition, availability of adequate equipment to perform job, competencies of supervisors, interpersonal relationship among co-workers, opportunity to learn new things determine job satisfaction level of the scientists and logistic personnel.
datasets.project_name: A Note on Job Satisfaction Level of Scientists and Logistic Personnel in Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

The study was carried out to assess the level of mental distress experienced by winter-over personnel of Thirteenth Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica, during the course of stay at Maitri station. The role of coping resources in handling stress is discussed.

datasets.title: Obesity, dyslipidemia and cholesterol gallstone disease during one year of Antarctic residence
datasets.abstract: Age, gender, ethnicity, geographic location, diet, obesity, diabetes mellitus and dyslipidemia are known risk factors for development of gallstone disease (GD). We describe the development of four cases of symptomatic GD including a case of acute cholecystitis in Indian Antarctic expedition members during 1 year of polar residence and their response to 6 months of ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) therapy.
datasets.purpose: Twenty subjects were evaluated at baseline and at serial intervals using clinical history, dietary assessment, anthropometry, blood investigations and ultrasonography for development of gallstone disease. Ursodeoxycholic acid and lipid lowering agents were prescribed as indicated and response to therapy measured over a period of 1 year in Antarctica.
datasets.project_name: Obesity, dyslipidemia and cholesterol gallstone disease during one year of Antarctic residence
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Personality and Temperament of Indian Antarctic Expedition Members.
datasets.abstract: Psychological effects in polar environment have been examined from several perspectives. Amongst those, personality and temperament traits have been cardinal. This study aims to investigate the personality and the temperament traits of Antarctic personnel, in addition, the correlation of temperament and personality traits. Fifteen volunteers from winter team of 25th Indian Scientific Antarctic Expedition served as participants. NEOFFI Personality test was administered at Auli, India and retested at pre and post winter season in Antarctica. The TDOT test was administered in the last two months of prolonged residence in Antarctica. There was no significant difference in the dimensions of personality from baseline to post winter season.
datasets.purpose: Considerable time and effort have been spent to identify personality characteristics related to good or poor adaptation, social cooperativeness versus destructiveness and the like in space flight or polar stations. The way in which people react to the environment is conceived of as being to a great extent personality based. Although much effort has been expended on research in selection factors for extreme and unusual environments, the findings have been essentially those predicted by common sense.
datasets.project_name: Personality and Temperament of Indian Antarctic Expedition Members.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.abstract: The proposed project envisages the generation and availability of a strong database of Vertical profile measurements of atmospheric ozone, temperatures and winds at both high latitude southern ocean hemisphere and equatorial regions in addition to aerosol and radiation measurements over these regions.The measurements thus carried out would serve as important inputs to various scientific researches on phenomena like exchange processes between the stratosphere and troposphere, effect of sudden stratospheric warming events on atmospheric parameters and their spatial and temporal variability. The effects of anthropogenic impacts and long-range transport on aerosol properties, trace species as well as role of ozone variability and its impact on weather and climate will be investigated.
datasets.purpose: To study the exchange process between the stratosphere and troposphere
datasets.project_name: Investigation of atmospheric exchange processes over the Southern Hemisphere
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: The Atmospheric electric field and condvctivity measuremfnts during the XVI Indian Antarctica expedition
datasets.abstract: Surface measurements of the atmospheric electric field and the conductivity of both polarities made at Maitri (70? 46'S, 11? 44' E,) Antarctica and along the cruise track are reported. The 20 fair -weather days average diurnal variation curve of the atmospheric electric field is single periodic with the maximum at 1300 GMT, and the minimum at 0100 GMT. It also shows a secondary but distinct maximum at 1900 GMT. The difference between the diurnal variation curve observed at Maitri and the universal varition curve observed at oceans and at the south pole is discussed with refrence to the validity of the classical global electric circuit. The electric conductivity does not show much change during a day either at Maitri or over open ocean. However, the conductivity has the minimum value at around 30?S the value of conductivity keeps increasing southward of 30?S upto 70?S and northward upto 10?S.
datasets.purpose: The measurements of the electric field and conductivity of both polarities made during our stay at Maitri (70? 46,S, 11? 44,E), Antarctica and along the cruise track.

datasets.title: A comparative Study of Glacio-meteorological Parameters, Reflectance and Surface Energy Exchange Over Different Snow-ice Media in Dronning Maud Land in East Anatrctica.
datasets.abstract: Two Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) were installed over continental shelf and continental ice surfaces in Dronning Maud Land in East Antarctica during XVII Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (ISEA). High quality glacio-meteorological data were collected round the year. A simple energy balance model based on the glaciomet parameters is formulated to calculate the energy exchange over the two types of surfaces. Surface roughness and albedo values of the two types of surfaces have been accounted for in the model. Different components of energy budget are tabulated and the results are compared for the two types of surfaces during Austral summer of 1999 ? 2000. Summer and winter energy budget are also compared and discussed for the continental ice surface. The difference in the energy balance over continental shelf and continental ice is mainly caused by differences in albedo, surface roughness and short wave extinction coefficient.
datasets.purpose: Results indicate that the main difference in summer and winter energy budget over continental ice is in the net radiation and sensitive heat fluxes during the corresponding periods. As the energy balance models are sensitive to surface reflectivity variation, albedo measurements over different snow-ice media were carried out and its dependence on solar elevation angle and cloud amount/type were investigated in detail.
datasets.project_name: A Comparative Study of Glacio-meteorological Parameters, Reflectance and Surface Energy Exchange Over Different Snow-ice Media in Dronning Maud Land in East Anatrctica.

datasets.title: Ozone Studies in Antarctica during 7th and 13th Indian Antarctic Expeditions.
datasets.abstract: Ozone programme of IMD, ozone observations and results at Dakshin Gangotri during 7th and at Maitri during 13th Indian Scientific Expeditions to Antarctica are discussed. Comparison with available data of Syowa and George Foster shows that Indian results are in agreement with those obtained by other workers. Ozone depletion phenomena at Maitri during 1994 is quite similar to that observed at Dakshin Gangotri during 1988.
datasets.purpose: India Meteorological Dept is showing keen interest on the recent developments like ozone depletion over Antarctica and India is one of the few countries in ozone monitoring and ozone depletion studies over Antarctica. There was an international collaboration for comparative observations of ozonesondes during 1993( 1st to 9th Sep'93) between Neumayer, Sanae, Maitri, Novolazaravskaya and Syowa called ROSA(Regional Ozone Soundings in Antarctica). The typical profiles of Neumayer, Maitri and Syowa on 3.9.93 are shown in Fig. 1. All the the three profiles show a peak around 60 mb and there is a sharp fall on either side. Temperature profiles also showing similar trends at all levels except near lower troposphere.
datasets.project_name: Ozone Studies in Antarctica during 7th and 13th Indian Antarctic Expeditions.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Temporal and spatial variations of meteorological parameters and energy budget of different snow-ice media in Antarctica using automatic weather station and satellite remote sensing data
datasets.abstract: Snow is the brightest substance of a considerable extent on the surface of our planet and because of its high reflectance compared to other natural surface; seasonal and perennial snow cover plays a significant role in the global energy balance. The connection between snow albedo and climate has long been recognized as an important feedback mechanism. Snow albedo feedback mechanism has been shown significantly to amplify global warming. Snow and ice cover large areas of the earth's surface, especially in the Polar Regions. Snow and ice reflect solar radiations very efficiently such that little of the incoming solar radiation is absorbed at the surface in these regions. Even so, small changes in surface reflectance can affect the Earth-atmosphere energy balance. Thus, it is clearly important to monitor and calculate the variability of the albedo of snow and ice of the continent using satellite technology and ground-based information.
datasets.purpose: 1. Dynamic Modeling for Energy Balance using RRTS and satellite
datasets.project_name: Temporal and spatial variations of meteorological parameters and energy budget of different snow-ice media in Antarctica using automatic weather station and satellite remote sensing data

datasets.title: A Confirmation of Polar Glacial Recession by Monitoring the Snout of Dakshin Gangotri Glacier in Schirmacher Range.
datasets.abstract: Dakshin Gangotri glacier in Schirmacher range is being monitored by the GSI since 1983. It was being monitored on an yearly basis from two survey stations. In the 15th expedition, 19 reference points were marked all along the periphery of the glacier and observations were taken on a monthly basis, for one full year. The cycle of advancing, bulging, calving and retreating of the glacial front were recorded. It is conclusively proved that the polar glaciers are also markedly retreating.
datasets.purpose: The movement of a polar glacier tongue, named Dakshin Gangotri (70? 45'20" S lat. and 10? 35' 05" E long.) in Schirmacher range, is being constantly monitored since 1983 (Kaul et al., 1985), to understand the dynamic changes in the continental ice front of Antarctica. This polar tongue (Fig.1) is a remnant of an earlier glacier, which was overriding the Schirmacher range and crossing it at this point towards north. Glacial striations on the rock surfaces display the palaeo- movement directions of the glacier. Two permanent survey stations 'G' and 'H' had been established earlier and the observations of the snout were taken from these points. The snout was monitored every year in the months of polar summer, (Jan or Feb). The resultant comparative profiles were drawn to record the advance/retreat during the year. One such profile, comparing the outlines of 1995 and 1996.
datasets.project_name: A Confirmation of Polar Glacial Recession by Monitoring the Snout of Dakshin Gangotri Glacier in Schirmacher Range.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Establishment of A New Meteorological Observatory at Maitri and Study of Meteorological Parameters, Ozone Depletion in Antarctic Spring and Solar Radiation during Ninth Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The Southern polar continent Antarctica is endowed with unique features such as cold temperatures, strong winds, blizzards and the vast glaciers on the earth. Meteorology is considered paramount because it can foresay the weather conditions in any particular region, The synoptic systems around Antarctica are typically inhospitable and dreadful, unlike elsewhere. Prediction of weather in this region is complicated due to unpredicted movements of upper celestial phenomenal changes. In order to get a better prediction, it is necessary to correlate the data obtained by various meteorological observatories situated in the continent, besides satellite cloud imagery.
datasets.purpose: (i) Establishing a new Meteorological Observatory at Maitri and monitoring weather conditions by keeping constant watch. (ii) Recording of 3 hourly synoptic observations and disseminating the main 6 hourly synoptic data to IMD, New Delhi for its global exchange programme. (iii) To investigate ozone depletion in the Antarctic spring season over this region. (iv) To monitor the radiation flux in the upper atmosphere. (v) To monitor surface ozone. (vi) To do other activities as were done by the previous expeditions.
datasets.project_name: Establishment of A New Meteorological Observatory at Maitri and Study of Meteorological Parameters, Ozone Depletion in Antarctic Spring and Solar Radiation during Ninth Antarctic Expedition.

datasets.title: Analysis of an Umbral Flare Observed from Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The observations in Call K of an umbral solar flare of optical importance class SF (subflare) which occurred on 12 Feb, 1990 . These observations have been correlated with the ones taken in H-alpha and in the radio region reported in Solar Geophysical Data (SGD). Though the umbral flare was small, it showed the impulsion behaviour in microwave region. We conclude that this is a special and very rare class of an umbral flare which is more energetic in microwave and radiowave regions than in the optical region.
datasets.purpose: When the sun is observed in white light, the centres of activity on the solar disk (photosphere) are visible as the well known groups of sunspots. Central dark part of the sunspot is known as umbra where strong magnetic field exists and the outer less dark part is known as the penumbra. If we observe the sun through a filter having a very narrow pass band of about, say 1 A or less, centred on the H-alpha line (the first line of the Balmer series of hydrogen, 6563 A) or of the Call K (singly ionized calcium, 3934 A), the centres of activity are seen as bright plages surrounding the sunspot groups. We then observe the higher layers in the chromosphere above the sunspots which are at about 104 K temperature. An optical flare is seen as a rapid brightening of a part of such a plage in the active centres where the magnetic field strength is more and its gradient higher than outside this region.
datasets.project_name: Analysis of an Umbral Flare Observed from Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: A Comparative Study of VLF Signals from Several Transmitters around the World as Observed from Maitri Station, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: To examine the behavior of the sunrise and sunset terminators, characteristics of the solar activities in the polar region and the possible seismic correlation with ionospheric anomalies a Stanford AWESOME VLF receiving system was installed at the Indian permanent Antarctic station Maitri during the 27th Indian scientific expedition to Antarctica. Almost five weeks of data was recorded successfully from several transmitters around the globe. The narrow-band signals show variation of the solar radiation and the signature of the prolonged day and night. We compare the signal of frequency 18.2 kHz with the same signal received at Kolkata, and we present simultaneous observation of the variation of the sunrise and sunset terminators. We compare the diurnal signal amplitude variation with the LWPC model.
datasets.purpose: The major objective was to study of the signal variation over very long path which is totally over the ocean.
datasets.project_name: A Comparative Study of VLF Signals from Several Transmitters around the World as Observed from Maitri Station, Antarctica.

datasets.title: Atmospheric Water Vapour Measurement at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Atmospheric water vapour content has been measured during 14th Indian Antarctic Expedition at Maitri (70? 46'S, 11?45'E), Antarctica. The measurements were carried out on clear sunny days during Jan.-Feb. 1995. The average precipitate water vapour at zenith was in the range 1.7- 2.4 mm.
datasets.purpose: The measurement of atmospheric water vapour plays an important role in understanding meteorology, climatology, infrared astronomy and cloud physics. The amount of atmospheric water vapour varies considerably with the temperature and relative humidity unlike other gases of the atmosphere. Water vapour is the primary absorber of thermal and near infrared radiation in the earth atmosphere and has considerable effect on radiation field, radiative albedo and the energy balance of the earth/atmospheric system.
datasets.project_name: Atmospheric Water Vapour Measurement at Maitri, Antarctica.

datasets.title: Exposure to Antarctic Summer Affects the Immunoglobulin Rhythm but Not the Oral Temperature Rhythm.
datasets.abstract: Environmental light is an important zeitgeber in humans. The long polar days of Antarctica during the summer period can disrupt the internal clock thereby desynchronizing the various bodily rhythms, which can have health implications. Hence, in the present study, in one group of six volunteers, the immunoglobulin rhythm was assessed by four hourly blood sampling. In another group of six volunteers the oral temperature rhythm was measured. The results reveal disruption of the immunoglobulin rhythm due to the influence of exogenous components and possible involvement of neuroendocrine factors. However, the oral temperature rhythm was unaffected during or after a short stay in Antarctica during the summer period. The importance of regular sleep-wake cycle and other social cues in maintaining a stable temperature rhythm is implicated.
datasets.purpose: The study was conducted on two groups of volunteers, who were members of the summer team of the 14th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica. In Group-I there were 6 subjects with a mean age of 35.5 ? 5.32 years. In these subjects the oral temperature rhythm was measured in three phases. In Group-II there were 6 subjects with mean age of 33.45 ? 3.48 years. Four hourly blood sampling was done on these subjects to estimate the circadian rhythm of IgG and IgM, in two phases before and after exposure to Antarctic summer.
datasets.project_name: Exposure to Antarctic Summer Affects the Immunoglobulin Rhythm but Not the Oral Temperature Rhythm.
