datasets.title: Diurnal and Seasonal Variation in the Surface Layer Parameters Observed at Maitri Station, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Surface layer parameters at Maitri station show a marked diurnal variation during the short austral summer. The diurnal effect in the surface temperature regime is due to the daytime heating provided by solar insolation. The surface layer over Maitri remains thermally stratified during the hours of minimum solar insolation. The surface wind regime also depicts a considerable diurnal influence alongwith the temperature regime particularly during summer months. The diurnal effect in the surface wind regime is due to the katabatic wind component. The diurnal variation in temperature and wind is observed to be maximum during summer months and decreases as winter advances. Same is the case with the surface heat flux which changes sign from positive to negative during summer months in accordance with the atmospheric stability. In winter months the diurnal effect in surface layer parameters is altogether absent because of longer- term cooling in the absence of solar radiation.
datasets.purpose: In this report we present the diumal variation in surface layer parameters for different months representing different seasons at Maitri station.
datasets.project_name: Diurnal and Seasonal Variation in the Surface Layer Parameters Observed at Maitri Station, Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Annual Cycle of Permafrost Migration in Schirmacher Oasis.
datasets.abstract: The soil in Schirmacher Oasis is poorly formed and is mostly a remnant of glacial moraines. In this soil, a pit - about a metre deep was dug and it touched the bedrock. Five thermistors were placed in it, at 20 cm intervals. From March' 96 to January '98, thermal data were recorded on a daily basis, barring highly windy days. In these two annual polar cycles, 358 sets of data have been collected. The dates of the onset of summer thawing and the migration of permafrost levels have been worked out; which could be useful in planning for buildings and foundations. The thawing dates for deeper levels appear to be consistent, irrespective of surface warming dates.
datasets.purpose: Muller (1947) has defined permafrost as "a thickness of soil or other superficial deposit, or even of bedrock, at a variable depth, in which a temperature below freezing has existed continually for a long time." The properties of permafrost vary considerably, depending on local climatic, morphological and hydrogeological conditions. The temperature in the upper layers of permafrost crosses the freezing point, due to the influence of seasonal variations. The depth and the dates of these migrations are important for planning any foundation work. Schirmacher Oasis is a rocky hill range of about 35 sq. km area, surrounded by glaciers and polar ice sheet. The glaciers have retreated, leaving behind a thin and sporadic cover of soil on an undulating terrain. The site of the present study is about 50 m north of Indian Antarctic Station, Maitri (70?45'39" S latitude and l l?44'4" E longitude) in Schirmacher Oasis. It has a cover of morainal soil of about 1 m thickness over the bedrock
datasets.project_name: Annual Cycle of Permafrost Migration in Schirmacher Oasis.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Measure of Aerosol properties and radiation to understand its effect on radiation forcing over Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic atmosphere and its constituents, particularly the aerosols and the Black Carbon in the atmosphere is currently gaining interest among the scientific community. The present knowledge and the data sets both are limited as far as the aerosol-radiation interaction of the region is concerned. Aerosols (including BC) are known to affect the radiation balance of any region. Although Polar Regions are not the source of anthropogenic aerosols the presence of aerosols including BC has already been reported over the polar regions. These aerosol particles from anthropogenic and bio-mass burning sources transported to polar regions may cause direct warming of the lower troposphere by absorption of radiation and IR emission. The soot particles of the aerosol deposited over the snow increases the surface Albedo and may contribute to an increase in snow melting.
datasets.purpose: Data collection for Aerosol Optical Depth, Radiation Flux in the UV and Broad Band and Absorbing aerosol (BC). Analysis of Data and Model calculation for Aerosol Radioactive properties including Forcing. Assess the impact of aerosols on radiation budget of Polar Regions.
datasets.project_name: Measure of Aerosol properties and radiation to understand its effect on radiation forcing over Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Response of the 30mhz and the Fluxgate Magnetometer at Maitri to Onset of Geomagnetic Disturbance.
datasets.abstract: An attempt has been made to understand the physical processes in the auroral ionosphere over MAITRI (geog. coord. 70.75o S, 52.8?E) and their response to geomagnetic disturbances. After observing the signatures of auroral ionospheric current systems on the ground magnetograms of fluxgate magnetometer, we tried to correlate these with the auroral absorption events recorded by a 30 MHz Riometer. The radio noise absorption is caused by the charged, particle precipitation in the auroral ionosphere i.e. by the secondary ionisation created in the lower ionosphere over Maitri. While passing through the region of enhanced electron density the cosmic radio noise suffers increased absorption resulting in a decrease in signal strength received by Riometer on the ground absorption events are categorized into the dawn, daytime, dusk and nighttime events and corresponding variations in the ionospheric current systems are presented here.
datasets.purpose: The Indian Institute of Geomagnetism has been operating Fluxgate Magnetometers at MAITRI (MAI with geog. coord ?0.75o S, 11.75o E, geomagnetic 62.8o S, 52.8o E coord) over the past two decades. These Fluxgate Magnetometers (FM) have been recording variations in the three orthogonal components of the surface geomagnetic field, X (north- south direction), Y (east-west) and Z (vertical), in other words known as Daily Variations (DV). A Riometer (Radio Ionospheric Opacity Meter) recording the radio signal strength at ground of the natural omnidirectional 30 MHz cosmic radio noise from the Universe, was added as an experiment in 1995, but due to faulty earthing at MAI, could not yield good data for a couple of years. With the rectification of the earthing problem, the data from the Riometer (RIO) improved considerably in 1997, and by 1998 attained great reliability.
datasets.project_name: Response of the 30mhz and the Fluxgate Magnetometer at Maitri to Onset of Geomagnetic Disturbance.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Magnetometer/ Riometer Changes Over Indian Antarctic Station Maitri, as a Pointer to Disturbances in Space.
datasets.abstract: It is observed that the just sub-auroral Indian Antarctic station Maitri is very sensitive to the electromagnetic changes in the geo environment. Observations of the three components of the geomagnetic field X, Y, Z and the 30 MHz cosmic radio noise signal recorded by Riometer (RIO) at Maitri can provide clues to the state of Space Weather, and for that matter the state of Interplanetary space. Maitri data of X, Y, Z and RIO during Jan-Feb 1999 are used to highlight this aspect.
datasets.purpose: ?Geospace Weather? can be defined as the electromagnetic state of the Earth's space environment. This encompasses the electric and magnetic fields, the particle populations and their distributions in the entire ionosphere-magnetosphere system. The Earliest recognition of Space Weather can be traced back amongst others to Gilbert (1600) for realising that the Earth's magnetic field extends into space all around in 3 dimensional form, Graham (1724) and Celsius (and Hiorter) (1741) for noticing oscillations in compass needles and in ammeters during auroral displays and de Marian (1754) for postulating that auroral and geomagnetic storms are caused by the entry of charged particles of solar origin into the geo environment.
datasets.project_name: Magnetometer/ Riometer Changes Over Indian Antarctic Station Maitri, as a Pointer to Disturbances in Space.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Studies on Seismotectonics and Geodynamical Processes between Antarctica and Southern Indian Peninsula: Continuous GPS monitoring between India and Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Global Positioning System (GPS) measurements at Maitri, Indian Antarctic Station, and Antarctica have been carried out since 1997 to study the seismotectonics and geodynamical processes between India and Antarctica. The GPS velocity fields of Maitri and other IGS stations (Casey, Davis, Seychelles, COCO, Hartebeesthoek, Yaragadee, and Tibdinbilla) in different plates relative to Kerguelen show the departure from rigid plate behaviour in a manner consistent with the mapped intra plate stress field, observations of deformations and seismicity in the region. The data show lengthening of baselines for sites Yaragadee and Tidbinbilla in Australian plate; and Seychelles and COCO in Indian plate at the rates of 5.5cm/yr, 2.8cm/yr, 5.6mm/yr and 5.5cm/yr respectively. The rate of change of COCO makes an interesting observation.
datasets.purpose: Installation of GPS arrays in and around Indian Antarctic Stations.
datasets.project_name: Studies on Seismotectonics and Geodynamical Processes between Antarctica and Southern Indian Peninsula: Continuous GPS monitoring between India and Antarctica
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Environmental Management Services at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Engineers India Limited (EIL) started its association with the Indian Antarctic Program by participating in the summer part of the 23rd Indian Antarctic Expedition (XXIII-IAE). EIL provided its services in reviewing Wastewater Management at Maitri, the permanent Indian Research Station in Antarctica. The work carried out by Environment Division of EIL for the study Wastewater Management at Maitri is covered here.
datasets.purpose: In order to carry out the study, a 10 point methodology has been adopted covering various aspects such as collecting front-end information, review of design data, obtaining operating and site specific information and their analysis to arrive at final conclusions and recommendations. Site work was initiated with collection of all available data/information with respect to existing wastewater management facilities.
datasets.project_name: Environmental Management Services at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Taxonomic and functional diversity of methanogens and methanotrophs in Antarctic lakes and tundra.
datasets.abstract: The proposed work is aimed at studying community structure of methanogenic-methanotrophic microbes in water and sediment samples of Antarctic lakes around Maitri and Bharati stations. The community structure of the above bacteria in dry and wettundra at Larsemann Hills, Eastern Antarctica based on 16s rDNA sequencing and abundance of gene/transcripts using RT-PCR will be analysed. In addition,the functional diversity of mcrA (methyl coenzyme M reductase) and pmoA(particulate methane monoxygenase) will also be studied. Both 16s rDNA and functional gene analysis will be carried out using NGS technology (IlluminaMiseq) at NCPOR.
datasets.purpose: To determine the abundance (gene/transcript) of methanogenic and methanotrophic genes (DNA) and transcripts in lake (water &sediment) and tundra (soil) samples using real time PCR.Taxonomic identification of methanogenic and methanotrophic microbes using 16s primers through culture independent approach.Functional gene diversity of mcrA (methyl coenzyme M reductase) and pmoA (particulate methane monooxygenase) using next generation sequencing.Physico-chemical characterization of lake (sediment and water) and tundra soil samples.
datasets.project_name: Taxonomic and functional diversity of methanogens and methanotrophs in Antarctic lakes and tundra.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Space Weather and Irregular Ionospheric Patches at MAITRI.
datasets.abstract: Space weather refers to conditions in geo space which are controlled by the solar activity and which can cause disruption of satellite operations, communications, navigation, and electric power distribution grids, leading to a variety of socio-economic losses. Most of the time, space weather is of little concern in our everyday lives. However, when the space environment is disturbed by the variable outputs o f the Sim, technologies that we depend on, can be affected. Space weather disturbances are generally caused by transient events in the solar atmosphere, which trigger disturbances in the Earth?s environment. Geomagnetic storms are accompanied by a variety of ionospheric disturbances, which are presumably caused by the intensification of the solar wind.
datasets.purpose: Study of Polar Cap Irregular Ionosphere patches (Polar cap patches are regions of enhanced ionization which drift across the polar cap in an anti-sunward direction from the source region near the dayside auroral oval). Ionospheric irregularities are responsible for scintillation of transionospheric radio signals.
datasets.project_name: Space Weather and Irregular Ionospheric Patches at MAITRI.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Meteorite search in Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Meteorites are a major source of information about the early history of our solar system. The East Antarctic ice sheet provides an ideal background for meteorite recovery. Vast ice fields of central Dronning Maud Land and adjacent areas need careful and painstaking exploration for search of meteorites. East Antarctic icesheet flows towards the margins of the continent; its progress is occasionally blocked by mountains, nunataks or obstructions below the surface of the ice. Presence of lateral moraines on both sides of the Somovken glacier along the contact with Humboldt and Orvin mountains would be studied in the ensuing field season. Traverses covering the Somovken glacier and other demarcated areas would be undertaken. Preliminary study of aerial photographs and the traverses taken in earlier expeditions have revealed that the Somovken glacier situated between Humboldt and Orvin mountains could be a possible locus for meteorite concentration.
datasets.purpose: To search for meteorites in central Dronning Maud Land, East Antarctica.
datasets.project_name: Meteorite search in Antarctica
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Glaciological Studies in Central Dronning Maud Land, East Antarctica during the 32nd Indian Antarctic Expedition
datasets.abstract: Dakshin Gangotri glacier located in the western part of Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica is showing recession of the snort for over two decades. However, the rate of retreat is not uniform and varies at different locations. The ice wall forming the western flank of the glacier has shown an average retreat of about 17 m between 2001 and 2009 while the snout had gone back by about 7 m (average) during the same period. Before 2001, the snout had shown a complete recession of about 3 m (average). The snout occupies valley area receiving less amount of solar radiation as compared to the western wall, which is a vertical cliff receiving maximum amount of solar radiation. The notable difference in the rate of recession in different parts of the Dakshin Gangotri glacier can be attributed to combined effect of natural factors, including meteorological parameters, ice sheet dynamics and geomorphology of that area.The trend of average annual accumulation or ablation is not uniform.
datasets.purpose: Glaciological studies in parts of the central Dronning Maud Land (CDML), East Antarctica for providing inputs towards a better understanding of climate change.
datasets.project_name: Glaciological Studies in Central Dronning Maud Land, East Antarctica during the 32nd Indian Antarctic Expedition
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Antarctica has attracted the attention of scientific community all over the world since it is one of the most important climate regimes with a potential to influence long term global climatic patterns. In order to study these, IMD?s meteorological programme is specifically aimed at preparing a data archive of meteorological parameters over Antarctica. This may also enable us to understand the global aspects of Indian weather in general and monsoon behavior in particular. World Meteorological Organization (WMO) strongly recommends that any research station established in Antarctica should run a complete meteorological observatory and deliver the obtained data through Global Telecommunication System (GTS). The daily synoptic observations recorded at Bharati, Antarctica will enter into the Global Telecommunication System (GTS) and contribute to the international efforts for weather forecasting.
datasets.purpose: To improve understanding of variability and change in Antarctic climate. Monitoring of surface climate across East Antarctica. To improve understanding of teleconnections between Antarctic and Indian Monsoon, To provide data for use in weather predictions and climate projections for India. To improve representation in numerical models of radiative, dynamical and chemical coupling processes throughout the atmosphere, focusing on energy and momentum transfer, chemical transport and links between Indian region and hemispheres.To understand the connections between ozone concentrations and characteristics of the polar vortex that will enable improved projections of the climate system response to ozone recovery, and particularly of changes to winds and storm frequencies at high southern latitudes.
datasets.project_name: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Magma-genesis, mode of emplacement and evolution of granitoids in parts of Larsemann Hills, Prydz Bay region, East Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Prydz Bay (PB) exposes three distinct terranes including the Archean-Mesoproterozoic -south Prince Chales Mountains (sPCM)-Vestfold Hills (VH), the Grenvillian -Rauer Group Islands (RGI) and Pan-African -Larsemann Hills (LH) [5,6]. The Larsemann Hills is an ice-free area in the southern part of the Prydz Bay region of East Antarctica.
datasets.purpose: To characterize and classify various granitoids in the study area (Knuckey Is., Butler Is., Manning Is., Dalkoy Is. and Progress Ganitoids in Broknes Peninsula Amanda Bay, Polarforschung and Landing Bluff). To correlate and compare the partially melted granitic phases associated with the metapelites and metabasites of the study area. To work out a model of tectono-magmatic evolution of these granitoids vis-?-vis the tectonic framework of the region.
datasets.project_name: Magma-genesis, mode of emplacement and evolution of granitoids in parts of Larsemann Hills, Prydz Bay region, East Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Glaciological Studies in Central Dronning Maud Land, East Antarctica during the 33rd Indian Antarctic Expedition
datasets.abstract: The Polar Regions have been the focus of glaciological studies due to their sensitivity towards the global environmental and impact of climate change. Studies of ongoing nature are being conducted by the Geological Survey of India on the Polar Ice Sheet and the Ice shelf in the Schirmacher Region of the central Dronning Maud Land, and adjoining ice shelf in the north. The response of Polar Ice Sheet to climate change is being monitored since 1983 through continuous observations on the fluctuation of the Dakshin Gangotri (DG) Glacier snout. Since 2001, these measurements have been extended further to the entire ice front west of the snout.The movement of the glacier is recorded by measuring the distance of the glacial wall from fixed ground points. During the period 1983-1993, the DG Glacier receded by 7 m. Between 1996 and 2011 the glacier retreated at an average of 0.72 m per annum. Measurements on the Dakshin Gangotri (DG) glacier snout shows 118.49 cm net annual recession for the gl
datasets.purpose: Glaciological studies in parts of the central Dronning Maud Land (CDML), East Antarctica for providing inputs towards a better understanding of global climate change.
datasets.project_name: Glaciological Studies in Central Dronning Maud Land, East Antarctica during the 33rd Indian Antarctic Expedition
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Winter Period Communication Services at Maitri.
datasets.abstract: A team from DEAL, (DRDO), Dehradun provided real-time communication to the 27th Indian Antarctic Expedition. The continuous communication with the rest of the world has been extended in the form of voice, as well as data, communication. A great milestone was reached in the expedition by SAC and ECIL after commissioning of the Earth Station at Maitri; the team from DEAL interacted with SAC and ECIL teams for operating of the Earth Station link with NCAOR, Goa. This report describes the details of DEAL communication support at Maitri during the winter period.
datasets.purpose: The main objective of DEAL Team during the 27th expedition was to provide communication support to the expedition members. It was also planned to activate the Repeater Station, which was installed earlier by previous DEAL contingents. Another important task was to provide LAN /Internet nodes in all rooms and summer labs.
datasets.project_name: Winter Period Communication Services at Maitri.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Trend of Depositional Patterns on Ice Shelf Near Dakshin Gangotri Station.
datasets.abstract: Snow accumulation/ablation on the ice shelf is being monitored through a network of stakes near Dakshin Gangotri Station, since 1986. This study is aimed at finding the changes at the surface of the shelf ice. During the 15th expedition, it was found that all the old stakes were uprooted, possibly due to blizzards. Because of this, the continuity of the observation was broken and it was necessary to set up a new set of stakes for monitoring of ice shelf. A systematic network of 25 stakes has been installed in Feb 96 and ten sets of observations were taken by the wintering team of GSI, to study pre-winter and post-winter patterns of deposition.
datasets.purpose: In the 5th expedition, Kaul et al. (1986) had fixed a network of 9 stakes on ice-shelf, about a km away from Dakshin Gangotri station. This network was upgraded during subsequent expeditions, as and when required, and a continuity of observations was maintained on the ice shelf, studying the various patterns of accumulation and ablation. In the summer of the 15th expedition, the GSI team found that each and every one of the old stakes was uprooted. This could be either due to human interference, or due an extraordinarily severe blizzard. Whatever the reason may be, it has broken the continuity of scientific observations on the shelf during the summer of 1996. During February 96, GSI team has fixed up a new set of 25 stakes, each separated by a distance of 50 m. Thus, a representative area of 200 m x200 m has been marked out on the shelf. The pattern of stakes' fixation.
datasets.project_name: Trend of Depositional Patterns on Ice Shelf Near Dakshin Gangotri Station.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Study of Ozone Hole Over Maitri, Antarctica During 2002.
datasets.abstract: Total column ozone has been measured using Microtop Sunphotometer at Maitri, Antarctica, during 21st Indian Antarctic Scientific Expedition (2002 ? 2003). The Maitri observations were also compared with TOMs data as well as nearby Russian station data and were found to be in good agreement. The water vapour has also been measured on the way from Goa, India to Maitri, Antarctica on the ship Magdalena Oldendroff. The ozone hole during spring of 2002 over Maitri did something unusual reflecting the unusual behaviour of the planetary waves in the Southern Hemisphere, which confirmed the roll of capricious weather in the opining and closing of ozone hole. The observation shows that the ozone hole in the year 2002 was not as deep as that of the previous years. The minimum value of total ozone of about 185 DU was observed in the last week of September during 2002 and exceptionally high values of about 420 DU were observed during the ozone hole period.
datasets.purpose: Ozone is one of the most important constituents in the atmosphere and in spite of its low concentration, a few ppmv, it plays an important role not only in the chemistry of this region but also it affects dynamics and biological activity near the surface. The amount of ozone over any particular place depends not only on photochemical balance, but also on the stratospheric climate, the winds that transport the ozone. The stratosphere itself is dependent on ozone for its existence. The energy absorbed by ozone in the course of creation and destruction of its layer warms the surrounding atmosphere creating temperature inversion.
datasets.project_name: Study of Ozone Hole Over Maitri, Antarctica During 2002.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Absolute Gravity Measurements at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: During the 23rd Indian Antarctic expedition, absolute gravity measurements (AG) are made at Maitri, Indian station in Antarctica. This was first AG in the Dronning Maud Land, Antarctica coincidentally just before the Finnish Geodetic Institute (FGI) measurements at Novolazarevskaya, Russian station near Maitri.
datasets.purpose: (i) establishing reference gravity station for future gravimetric surveys, (ii) for studying temporal gravity changes related to Antarctic ice mass loss.
datasets.project_name: Absolute Gravity Measurements at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Role of trace elements geochemistry in different phases of metamorphism andpartial melting of rocks from Schirmacher Oasis, cDML, East Antarctica with emphasis on metapelites.
datasets.abstract: Various methods are used to unravel the history of individual rocks and their constituent minerals. Evidence includes microstructural information, such as mineral and fluid inclusions within porphyroblasts and replacement relations among minerals, and chemical information, such as compositional zoning in mineral grains. Using these data with petrogenetic grids and thermobarometry, PT conditions have been determined by earlier workers in the area. Metamorphism ranges from middle amphibolite to granulite facies and due to the high temperatures reached partial melting of metapelites due biotite or muscovite dehydration results in the generation of mesosomes and leucosomes akin to migmatization. The partial melting of basic but especially mica bearing pelitic rocks is a complex process that is continuous over a wide range of temperature.
datasets.purpose: To understand the nature of partial melting of metabasic and metapelitic rocks of Schirmacher as well as the field relationship between the melts and their parent rocks.To study the geochemical nature (redistribution of trace and REE) of major and accessory phases in the melts and source rocks. To characterize the role of accessory and major minerals in controlling the composition of residual rocks and the partial melt products.
datasets.project_name: Role of trace elements geochemistry in different phases of metamorphism andpartial melting of rocks from Schirmacher Oasis, cDML, East Antarctica with emphasis on metapelites.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Report on the Participation by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in the Tenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic continent can be expected to provide reference levels for all environmental and pollution studies due to its remoteness and restricted human activities. The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre has participated in the Xth Expedition primarily to collect background baseline data on natural radioactivity, heavy metal concentration in soil and water, and biological specimens. While radioactivity data and some limited heavy metal concentration data have already been collected on air, water and soil samples from participation in 8th and 9th expeditions: this is the first time BARC made attempts to collect biological samples as well. Fairly complete data base has been built up on all these samples and these are presented in this report. The analytical procedures followed at BARC were mainly by the use of standard chemicals and approved standardisation techniques in case of inorganic parameters and standard reference gases, wherever required.
datasets.purpose: Man's impact on the oceanic environment has always been the cause for great concern. Several investigations on the natural radioactivity levels and on the heavy metal concentrations over the ocean as well as on remote locations have been carried out by various nations in the world. In order to obtain a background baseline data over the South Indian ocean and on the Antarctic continent, extensive sampling has been carried out on air, water, soil, and other environmental samples from BARC participation in the Xth Expedition during November 27,1990 to March 26, 1991.
datasets.project_name: Report on the Participation by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in the Tenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Logistic Activity Carried Out by the 20th Indian Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.abstract: The 20th Indian Antarctic Expedition had a logistics team of 13 members drawn from the Indian Army. The team primarily was responsible for providing logistic back up to the Indian Antarctic Scientific Expedition and to maintain and run all the life support systems at the Indian Antarctic base-Maitri.
datasets.purpose: 1. Upkeep of station infrastructure and all its life support systems.
datasets.project_name: Logistic Activity Carried Out by the 20th Indian Antarctic Expedition.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Radio Noise Measurement in HF/VHF Band at Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Long distance communication from Antarctica is heavily dependent on HP propagation which, in turn, is influenced by local and non-terrestrial noise levels. Present study shows that local noise level in Antarctica is much less as compared to latter. The study has been conducted keeping in background the noise level at different frequencies in a city like Calcutta.
datasets.purpose: To understand the mechanism of in transmitter and receiver performance, actual noise level prevailing around Maitri station in Antarctica is taken into account.
datasets.project_name: Radio Noise Measurement in HF/VHF Band at Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Impact on Space-weather events on Polar Region Ionosphere
datasets.abstract: Almost open vertical Earth's magnetic field line at polar region area provides an opportunity to study the interaction of solar wind with the Earths thermosphere and its adverse effects on magnetosphere and ionosphere. The excessive amount of energy is deposited over the high latitude region due to particle precipitation and initiated the joule's heating process. On being heated, the ionosphere lifted upwards and created outward flow of ionospheric plasma from the polar region to low latitude region which is known to be as Travelling Ionospheric disturbances (TIDS). The TIDS are often associated with molecular enriched chemical compositions and transported to lower latitude within a few hours by storm time. The equator-ward wind associated with TIDS causes the vertical motion of ionized layer over low-latitude region along the slope geomagnetic field lines and thus leads to the increase in the height of ionospheric layers and perturb the low latitude ionosphere in different ways.
datasets.purpose: Morphological study of Polar region Ionosphere i.e. Day to day behavior of different ionospheric parameters like bottom side ionospheric plasma density, variation of critical frequency and height of different ionospheric layers. Investigation of solar wind thermospheric magnetospheric ionospheric coupling over polar region during high solar activity period with special emphasis on adverse space weather conditions.
datasets.project_name: Impact on Space- weather events on Polar Region Ionosphere
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Meteorological Studies at Maitri during Thirteenth Indian Antarctic Expedition (1994).
datasets.abstract: Meteorological studies conducted at Maitri during 1994 are discussed in brief. August was the coldest month with lowest monthly mean air temperature -26.0 Deg C and extreme lowest air temperature -29.1 Deg C of the year. The occurrence of maximum and minimum pressure are having a clear tendency. Strongest wind of 65 knots gusting to about 80 kts was recorded during August. Cloud, precipitation, Aurora global solar radiation and net terrestrial radiation are also discussed in brief.
datasets.purpose: Meteorological programme of Thirteenth Antarctic Expedition was mainly the continuation of the long term programme of IMD introduced in earlier expeditions to enable the collection of surface and upper air observations for preparing the climatology of the area and to study the inter annual and inter seasonal variations of the weather over Antarctica and also their relationships with the Indian weather; radiation observations with surface based and balloon borne instruments for estimating the radiation budget; measurements of vertical profiles of ozone as part of an international programme for the investigation of ozone-hole occurrence over Antarctica during the spring alongwith atmospheric turbidity measurements; the reception of cloud imageries from the polar orbiting weather satellites and radio facsimile weather charts broadcast by the forecasting offices in the region as part of the weather services for logistic and scientific programmes of the expedition.
datasets.project_name: Meteorological Studies at Maitri during Thirteenth Indian Antarctic Expedition (1994).
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Hormonal Profile of Human Subjects Exposed to Antarctic Summer.
datasets.abstract: The harsh challenging and extreme photoperiodic environment of Antarctica provides an ideal setting for studies of many human physiological and psychological variables. Of particular interest is the possibility of hormonal changes as one of the causative factors for these variations. A pilot study was conducted on summer expedition members to determine the hormonal profile of peripheral blood. The data suggest increased levels of prolactin and growth hormone, and decreased levels of Cortisol, triiodothyronine and thyroxine.
datasets.purpose: Antarctica has been considered a natural laboratory for studying the effect of stresses on human health and behaviour. The Antarctic environment presents extremes of environmental stress to sojourners to this land. Above all, the continuous day or night plays a major role in adaptation of members of Antarctic expedition, who spend either summer or winter months in Antarctica. Besides these there are other psychoemotional stresses like social isolation, small close community living, hypo and hyperkinesia and sexual deprivation which complicate the normal activity and adaptation at polar station.
datasets.project_name: Hormonal Profile of Human Subjects Exposed to Antarctic Summer.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Ice Sheet dynamics from Schirmarcher Oasis to Wohlthat Mountains, cDML, East Antarctica and their stress pattern
datasets.abstract: After the establishment of its station in central Dronning Maud Land (cDML), GSI initiated glaciological programs to determine behavior of Polar ice sheet. The beginning was made by monitoring the Polar ice sheet front in the Schirmacher Oasis margin to understand the impact of glacier dynamics and climate change.To augment the glaciological database in central Dronning Maud Land, a pilot project was taken up on the Polar ice sheet between Schirmacher Oasis and Wohlthat Mountains during 2016-17. The thickness of the ice sheet was estimated using GPR and the glacier flow velocity was determined using DGPS. The snow and ice thickness for most part in this route is more than 600 m. Ground data for snow accumulation and ablation using stake networks and meteorological parameters using Automatic Weather stations (AWS) was also collected.
datasets.purpose: To provide input for climate change impact assessment. To study the ice sheet dynamics in the area. Estimation of surface mass balance of part of EAIS. Attempt to calculate influx and outflux of ice from the catchment area of the region.
datasets.project_name: Ice Sheet dynamics from Schimarcher Oasis to Wohlthat Mountains, cDML, east Antarctica and their stress pattern
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: First Attempt at Motorised Ice Core Drilling during the Antarctic Summer Season.
datasets.abstract: In the 22nd Indian Antarctic Expedition, year 2002-03, GSI had sent a two-member team for Ice Core drilling work. For the first time, this was to be attempted during the summer season, as all the earlier operations of motorised Ice Core drilling were confined to the wintering period of previous expeditions. Moreover, the existing drilling machine was extensively upgraded by the suppliers in Japan, and this was to be the first field trial of various new sub-systems of the machine.
datasets.purpose: A. Transportation, positioning, assembling and installation of the new drilling machine at a suitable field site.
datasets.project_name: First Attempt at Motorised Ice Core Drilling during the Antarctic Summer Season.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Effect of Cold, Isolation and Ultraviolet Radiation Stress on Human Immune System.
datasets.abstract: Stressful environment conditions are a major determinant in immune reactivity. This effect is pronounced in Antarctica expeditioners where they are exposed for long to the isolation, cold and UV radiation stress. Whether these stresses alter the immune system or not, was studied in expedition members at Maitri. Various parameters like Immunoglobulin, Lymphocyte counts, Cytokine and 1, 25-hydroxy Vitamin D-3 were estimated to assess the functional status of the immune cells. Data gathered indicate Antarctic isolation is associated with alterations in the immune system due immunity. These findings have important long-term health implications.
datasets.purpose: The proposed study is undertaken to evaluate and understand the role of UV radiation in modulating the immune response directly or indirectly through vitamin D involvement and to whether the isolation and cold stress supplement this effect.
datasets.project_name: Effect of Cold, Isolation and Ultraviolet Radiation Stress on Human Immune System.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Laser heterodyne system at Maitri, Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The ozone depletion in general and ozone hole phenomenon over Antarctica during spring in particular has generated a surge of interest in the measurement of ozone using various techniques. A High-Tech Laser Heterodyne System using a 1 GHz Acousto-optic spectrometer as back end has been designed and developed at National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi to monitor ozone and other trace species in the atmosphere. The Laser Heterodyne System has been successfully operated at Maitri Lo obtain ozone line spectra at 1043.1775 cm with an ultra high spectral resolution. The line spectra thus obtained with high spectral resolution in trun has been used to get vertical profiles of ozone in the atmosphere using inversion technique developed at NPL for Antarctic conditions. A liquid nitrogen plant was also installed at Maitri. In the present communication the salient feature of the Laser Heterodyne System, Acousto-optic spectrometer, liquid nitrogen plant and results obtained are discussed in detail
datasets.purpose: To study of minor constituents in the atmosphere is of vital interest to understand the structure of troposhere and stratosphere.
datasets.project_name: Laser heterodyne system at Maitri, Antarctica
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: The Meteorological Programme Carried Out During Eleventh Indian Expedition to Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: India Meteorological Department has an on-going meteorological programme in the Antarctic Expeditions. During the eleventh expedition, two new sub programmes viz.,Slow rising Low Level Radiosonde and Pilot Balloon ascents were added on experimental basis. In this report data pertaining to surface weather, vertical distribution of ozone and global solar radiation have been presented and discussed. Data on radiometersonde and low level radiosonde ascents and sunphotorneter observations could not be included as these are still being processed. Pilot Balloon ascents were not successful due to early bursting of balloon and difficulty in tracking in cold environment.
datasets.purpose: The meteorological programme of India Meteorological Department, in Antarctica, is of on-going nature. During the eleventh expedition, however, two new sub-programmes were included. These are Low Level Slow Rising Radiosonde ascents (LLSR-RS) for determining the temperature and humidity profiles in the lowest few kilometres of the atmosphere and Pilot Balloon (PB) ascents for determining the upper level winds. Both the programmes had been included on an experimental basis. The on-going observational programmes included continuous surface weather watch, weekly measurement of vertical distribution of ozone, and fortnightly measurement of infra-red radiation fluxes in the upper atmosphere. During onward and return cruise of the expedition from India to Antarctica and back, daily recording of surface and upper air observations formed part of the programme.
datasets.project_name: The Meteorological Programme Carried Out During Eleventh Indian Expedition to Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Alteration of Immunoglobulin and Temperature Rhythm During Winter-over Stay in Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The alien photoperiodicity of Antarctica can disrupt the biological clock, thereby desynchronizing the various bodily rhythms, which can have health implications. This study is an attempt to find out whether the circadian rhythm disruption could be a reason for the immunosuppression observed during Antarctic stay. In the present study, in one group of six volunteers, the immunoglobulin rhythm was assessed. In another group of six volunteers the oral temperature, activity and heart rate rhythms were measured. Disruption and desynchronization of the temperature rhythm with respect to activity and heart rate rhythms was noted. In the other group, disruption of the serum immunoglobulin rhythm was noted irrespective of the season. Our results clearly indicate that the decrease in the serum immunoglobulins IgG and IgM are associated with disruption of their circadian rhythm. Involvement of neuroendocrine factors is postulated.
datasets.purpose: The human subjects included in this study were all Indian, male members of the 15th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica who were on winter-over assignment. The objectives of the study were briefed to all the members of the expedition and only those who volunteered for the study were included. Out of the 25 winter-over members two groups of 6 volunteers each were included in the study. Group-I had a mean age of 33.51 ? 5.42 years and mean body weight 68.47 ? 6.25 kg in whom the circadian rhythm of body temperature, activity and heart rate were studied. In Group-II, with mean age 34.17 ? 2.73 years and mean body weight 67.17 ? 7.22 kgs, the circadian rhythm of immunoglobulin was studied.
datasets.project_name: Alteration of Immunoglobulin and Temperature Rhythm During Winter-over Stay in Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Validation of remote sensing and model based high-resolution ice-sheet and glacial landform science products for parts of Antarctic
datasets.abstract: This project is follow up of earlier study which has been carried by IIRS to identify and map the various ice sheet features and glacier landforms associated with high wind speed, glacier flow etc., in parts of Antarctic using high resolution optical Cartosat-2 and RISAT-1 FRS 1 datasets.The proposed campaign will also collect samples in such BIAs about roughness, wind velocity and surface snow depth, density and wetness at different times at different sample sites. The features such as nunatak, wind scoops, Sastrugi etc. are formed in ice sheets and glacier areas due to persistent high winds. The area under study in Antarctica falls under very high wind speeds or gale category. Also during proposed campaigns, crevasses depth and ice layers mapping using GPR, along with wind speed/directions and temperature will also be measured in such areas to validate the AMPS, Antarctic Mesoscale Prediction System and RISAT-1 based wind speed estimates and crevasses morphology and locations.
datasets.purpose: Ground observations and validation to verify the remote sensing and model based science products of wind vectors, ice sheet features and glaciers and accumulation and ablation zones formed due to wind.
datasets.project_name: Validation of remote sensing and model based high-resolution ice-sheet and glacial landform science products for parts of Antarctic
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Study of Very Low Frequency (VLF) Phenomena at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Ground based observations of Very Low Frequency (VLF) electromagnetic signals at the Indian station Maitri (70?46 'S, 11?44'E) in Antarctica have been described in detailed. The ELF and VLF recording experiment was successfully installed during the 19th expedition and observations were carried out during Jan-March, 2000 using a T-type antenna and loop type antenna in E-W and N-S directions.
datasets.purpose: 1. The continuous recording of whistlers at Antarctic with the help of digital systems interfaced with computer during summer and winter months.
datasets.project_name: Study of Very Low Frequency (VLF) Phenomena at Maitri, Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Cognitive performance during long-term residence in a polar environment
datasets.abstract: The objective of this study was to determine whether there was significant change in cognitive performance by prolonged duration of residence in polar environment. We examined volunteers (N 18260;4 23, scientific and logistic personnel) who spent fourteen months of continuous stay at Maitri - The Indian research base in Antarctica (70 45 0 S, 11 44 0 E). Cognitive measures (tests of task acquisition, delayed recognition, attention and concentration, and digit symbol substitution) were obtained at the beginning (second month), the middle (seventh month) and the final (twelfth month) phases of prolonged residence in Antarctica. A repeated-measures MANOVA was conducted and the findings indicated a significant increase in percent accuracy in performance of task acquisition, delayed recognition and digit symbol tests that assessed recognition memory and learning.
datasets.purpose: This study attempted to examine cognitive performance over a long-duration of residence in polar environment. Findings indicated positive as well as neutral effect on cognitive performance of winter-over residents.
datasets.project_name: Cognitive performance during long-term residence in a polar environment
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Magnetic Pulsations Over Antarctica: Results From the Three-station Triangulation Experiment.
datasets.abstract: Results from the magnetic field observations carried out during the summer campaign of the XX Indian Antarctic Expedition (2000-2001) are presented in this work. Simultaneous data from three locations (Maitri, Dakshin Gangotri and the third near Sigurd Mountain) were made use of in order to identify the ground magnetic signatures of the distant geo space processes that occurred on 24 January 2001. An isolated pulsation event (a westward propagating disturbance) in the Pi3 category was recorded at all the three stations during this period. Triangulation of magnetic records reveals velocities of this waveform to be ~1 km/s. The present work clearly highlights the importance of continuing magnetic field measurements in the icy continent, as space weather is an important area that is gaining attention in recent times.
datasets.purpose: The geographical location of Maitri is unique in that under quiet geomagnetic conditions the station is under the influence of the mid latitude ionospheric Sq current system. As the magnetic disturbances grow due to the enhanced solar wind-magnetosphere interaction, the atmosphere over Maitri comes increasingly under the auroral oval. The auroral oval expands under such conditions to envelop the sky over Maitri.
datasets.project_name: Magnetic Pulsations Over Antarctica: Results From the Three-station Triangulation Experiment.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Observation of meteorological parameter and ozone observation
datasets.abstract: Antarctica has attracted the attention of the scientific community all over the world since it is one of the most important climate regimes with a potential to influence long-term global climatic patterns. In order to study these, IMD s meteorological programme is specifically aimed at preparing a data archive of meteorological parameters over Antarctica. This may also enable us to understand the global aspects of Indian weather in general and monsoon behaviour in particular. The daily synoptic observations recorded at Maitri, Antarctica enter into the Global Telecommunication System (GTS) and contribute to the international efforts for weather forecasting. Continuation of surface weather observations at Maitri will provide necessary input for understanding the variation in the Antarctica atmospheric circulation patterns, which have influence over global climate.
datasets.purpose: Study of Antarctic Meteorology and Atmospheric ozone hole phenomenon.
datasets.project_name: Observation of meteorological parameter and ozone observation
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Meteorological Programme During Summer Period of Tenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic weather influences the global climate to a great extent. In order to study meteorological features over Antarctica and correlate these with Indian weather, the meteorological observational programme of IMD has been a regular component of each Indian expedition to Antarctica. The programme has been augmented from time to time for obtaining various types of data.
datasets.purpose: (i) Regular surface and upper-air observations during enroute cruises and at ice-shelf.
datasets.project_name: Meteorological Programme During Summer Period of Tenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: The Measurement of Ozone in the Atmosphere Over Maitriin Antarctica by Laser Heterodyne Spectrometer.
datasets.abstract: The measurements of ultra-high resolution absorption line spectra of ozone at V3 band near 9.5(μm) has been obtained by laser heterodyne spectrometer using carbon dioxide laser as a local oscillator in Maitri (70? 46' S, 11?45' E) Antarctica. The observations were made from 15 Jan. to 20 Feb. 95 on clear available sunny days. The vertical concentration profile of ozone has been retrieved through inversion of the measured absorption line profile. In the present communication results obtained are discussed.
datasets.purpose: In the recent years the global ozone depletion and ozone hole phenomenon over Antarctica has intensified ozone research around the world. Ozone, a minor constituents of the atmosphere is important because it protects life on the earth from harmful part of solar ultra-violet radiation and also significant for controlling stratospheric temperature. Total ozone in the atmosphere has been measured globally with the help of Dobson- spectrometers by monitoring the absorption of solar ultra-violet radiation at selected wavelengths in 280-340 nm wavelength range. Ozone measurements has also been carried out by ozonesonds placed on rockets and balloons. On global basis ozone has been monitored by satellite using total ozone mapping spectrometers (TOMS) also.
datasets.project_name: The Measurement of Ozone in the Atmosphere Over Maitriin Antarctica by Laser Heterodyne Spectrometer.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Climate Change Research and Low Latitude High Latitude Coupling
datasets.abstract: Long-term, multi-disciplinary, multi-institutional initiative to characteristic the radioactive, chemical, dynamical and electro dynamical processes themselves and their coupling with the low and equatorial processes is being conceived as a collaborative effort between SPL, NCPOR and Goa University. The experiments would be added in a phased manner, as the infrastructure develops and research matures. The integrated experiment is proposed for a period of five years from 2012. The financial commitment as well as the manpower required for the smooth implementation of the program will be shared between SPL, NCPOR and Goa University
datasets.purpose: The proposal in the area of polar atmosphere includes studies on atmospheric Aerosols, chemistry, clouds, radiation, atmospheric boundary layer and thermodynamics. Due to large surface reflectance over the Polar Regions, even a small amount of absorbing aerosols over the Antarctica ice and snow can cause warming of the earth-atmosphere system, unlike over other parts of the globe. Deposition of soot on ice will reduce the surface reflectance, heat the surface due to absorption of solar radiation and accelerate ice melting, associated with global warming. Characterization of polar aerosols and understanding the chemistry, water vapor, clouds and hydro logical cycle, and radiation budget of the polar regions is quite pertinent to climate change research. Atmospheric boundary layer process plays a pivotal role in the exchange of energy and mass between the surface and free-troposphere. In this context, a set of experiments are proposed for understanding a comprehensive picture of aerosol.
datasets.project_name: Climate Change Research and Low Latitude High Latitude Coupling.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Ice dynamics and mass balance of Dalk glacier, Larsemann Hills
datasets.abstract: Ice sheets and glaciers are the most important hydrological resources and play major role in the global climate system. With the prospect of climate change and sea level rise, it is important to monitor and understand the glacier/ice dynamics of Ice sheet. Analysis of different parameters such as ice fluxes, mass balance and surface topography are main components of glacier studies. Considering the huge ice area, hostile environment and required of high accuracy data, it is challenging rather impossible to carry field measurements of whole ice sheet. But at the same time it is crucial to estimate and monitor the entire ice sheet. With the advent of new and advanced technologies various models and satellite remote sensing data has made it feasible to overcome the complex and challenging studies of ice sheet. However these advanced based remote sensing studies involved various processes and results are mainly based on methods used and interpretations. But without validating the processed
datasets.purpose: Measurement of glacier mass balance, atmospheric parameters and its interaction with glacier surface based on energy balance model To estimate glacier flux by monitoring ice flow, thickness and bed topography of Dalk glacier basin . To understand the processes of glacier dynamics of Dalk glacier
datasets.project_name: Ice dynamics and mass balance of Dalk glacier, Larsemann Hills
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctic, Bharati
datasets.abstract: Antarctica has attracted the attention of scientific community all over the world since it is one of the most important climate regimes with a potential to influence long term global climatic patterns. In order to study these, IMDs meteorological programme is specifically aimed at preparing a data archive of meteorological parameters over Antarctica. This may also enable us to understand the global aspects of Indian weather in general and monsoon behavior in particular. World Meteorological Organization (WMO) strongly recommends that any research station established in Antarctica should run a complete meteorological observatory and deliver the obtained data through Global Telecommunication System (GTS). The daily synoptic observations recorded at Bharati, Antarctica will enter into the Global Telecommunication System (GTS) and contribute to the international efforts for weather forecasting.
datasets.purpose: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctica.Weather forecast for Indian Antarctic Stations and surrounding region
datasets.project_name: Characterizing atmospheric processes, variability and change in Antarctic, Bharati

datasets.title: Study of Physico-chemical characteristics of Aerosols and snow chemistry over Antarctica
datasets.abstract: The present project essentially deals with measurements of physical and chemical properties of aerosols and estimate of direct forcing due to aerosols in the Antarctic region. It is proposed to undertake field experiments to characterize aerosols by means of using high volume samplers i.e., TSP, PM2.5 and PM10, low volume cascade impactor for size distribution of chemical species and continued aerosol mass size analyzer simultaneously. Continuous measurements of Black Carbon (BC) will be made using Aethalometer. Also, snow samples will be collected to study its chemical composition.
datasets.purpose: To characterize polar aerosol and snow in terms of physico- chemical properties
datasets.project_name: Study of Physico-chemical characteristics of Aerosols and snow chemistry over Antarctica
datasets.scientist_name: Dr. P S P Rao P S P Rao Rao

datasets.title: Fire Protection - Indian Stations at Antarctica: Maitri and Dakshin Gangotri Hangar Accommodation.
datasets.abstract: Fire is the greatest safety hazard at Antarctica because of its dry climate. The fire protection system at Indian Antarctic Stations - Maitri and Dakshin Gangotri- has been evaluated and the weak points identified. Recommendations have been made for safety of men and material and fire drills proposed.
datasets.purpose: During past nine expeditions various problems on "fire safety" of men and property have been experienced by Indian Expeditions to Antarctica. The basic reasons for the various problems on fire and safety faced at Antarctica are due to the hostile weather conditions as this continent is the coldest, windiest and driest in the world. Besides these, its rich oxygen content further aggravates the hostile nature of environment from fire safety point of view. Defence Institute of Fire Research was assigned the job to study the adequacy, possible improvement and efficient support of "fire safe" condition for men and property at Antarctica - Maitri and Dakshin Gangotri hangar accommodation.
datasets.project_name: Fire Protection - Indian Stations at Antarctica: Maitri and Dakshin Gangotri Hangar Accommodation.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Constraining the retreat and advancement history of East Antarctica Ice Sheet (EAIS) during Late Quaternary using OSL Surface Exposure dating technique in parts of Larsemann Hills area
datasets.abstract: The quaternary period has been recognized by cyclic climatic variations in the form of glacial-interglacial cycles (Shackleton and Opdyke, 1973; Imbrie et al., 1984; Chappel and Shackleton 1986; Shackleton 1987, Lisiecki, and. Raymo, 2005). In Polar region terrestrial setup, records of such paleoclimate fluctuations is meager. However, admirable inferences on such climatic variations and its impact in Late Quaternary climate change were drawn from ice cores constraining past 740ka (EPICA, 2004). Collectively, Marine and lake sediment data is valuable in depicting regional as well as global paleoclimate variations. The Larsemann Hills includes ~50 Km2 of an ice free area of rocky peninsula and islands in Prydz Bay, East Antarctica which predominantly constituted of Proterozoic meta-pelitic cordierite and gneisses (Stuwe et al 1989).
datasets.purpose: To attempt building up of chronology of glacial advance and retreat through Late Quaternary To assess the credibility of technique in East Antarctica ice free areas.To develop protocols of surface exposure dating by OSL using lithology and depth to time-dependent luminescence bleaching profile.
datasets.project_name: Constraining the retreat and advancement history of East Antarctica Ice Sheet (EAIS) during Late Quaternary using OSL Surface Exposure dating technique in parts of Larsemann Hills area
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Meteorological Studies-Surface carried out during Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
datasets.abstract: Antarctica continent influences the general circulation pattern over the globe and is supposed to provide significant forcing to the future climate changes due to its huge ice shield covering most part of the continent. Weather over Antarctica is a real challenge to the meteorologist participating in the Indian Scientific Expedition. A permanently manned meteorological observatory equipped with the instruments to monitor weather system exist at the Indian Antarctic station MAITRI
datasets.purpose: Daily, seasonal and annual variation of atmospheric pressure, surface air temperature, surface ozone snowfall and clouds. The changes in weather parameters with reference to the specific synoptic situations. Radiation observations and its budget

datasets.title: Structural Assessment of Maitri Building at Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: Structural assessment of Maitri building in Antarctica was carried out by two scientists of SERC during the XXIIIIAE. This report gives the details of work carried out, defects, damage and deterioration found in the structure, and observations made during the study.
datasets.purpose: 1. Detailed visual examination of the structure, identification of locations which require further detailed inspection/examination. 2. Collection of samples of the materials used in the construction of the structure and collection of any other relevant data and information relevant to the structure.3. Collection of data from accelerometers using impact hammer technique. 4. Preparation of report giving details of the condition assessment

datasets.title: Thermoregulatory Effects of Tropical Man in Antarctica With Reference to Special Clothing.
datasets.abstract: Untamed icy wilderness of Antarctica is a physiological challenge tosojourners for coping of cold (Edholam, 1960). Thermal status prevails at outdoor is antilogy to comfort. The comfort is achieved in Antarctica by balancing heat-loss and heat gain. One of the ways it can be achieved is by selecting proper clothing, which in turn helps to balance, the heat gained from exercise and sunlight against the heat loss to the cold winds, sky and terrain. But, if the required clothing adjustments is inadequate or delayed, man becomes too hot or too cold for comfort (Bud et al., 1966, Wyndham et al., 1969). Frequent stimulation of cold and warm would affect the underlying vascular system. Most outdoor occupations in Antarctica require greater expenditure of energy than their counterparts in tropical or Temperate Zone. This is the result of the nature of terrain underfoot, wind resistance, and bulky heavy cloth (Bountelier et aL, 1981)
datasets.purpose: 1) This project is aimed to investigate the thermoregulatory effect of tropical sojourners in Antarctic subzero climate with reference to special clothing taking into consideration of climatic variables of cooling power indices. T h e inputs of the study would help to predict required clothing insulation (IR.EQ) while working in outdoor Antarctic environment with respect to bio meteriological indices with a view to ensure comfortability. Thus present study will help to maintain thermal homeostasis in real life extreme cold environment with proper clothing. Thus present study in real life extreme cold environment will help to reduce the physiological problems to maintain homeostasis as well as to ameliorate mental function.2) Physiological evaluation of different personal cold protective ensembles in Ant-arctic field conditions.
datasets.project_name: Thermoregulatory Effects of Tropical Man in Antarctica With Reference to Special Clothing.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Evaluation of Physical Activity on Exposure to Antarctic Environment.
datasets.abstract: The Antarctic environment presents extremes of meteorological elements to the members of expedition, A study was conducted to analyze the mechanisms of decreased performance of subjects in Antarctica, for which the first author participated in the Tenth Indian Scientific Expedition. Harvard step test was performed on seventeen members and their heart rate, blood pressure, oral temperature and skin temperature. Two recordings were taken viz. basal (in the ship) and the other after 8 weeks of the Antarctic stay. A cold chamber simulation study, back at India, was conducted on rats to study the effect of cold exposure alone as the primary factor affecting the physical performance. A significant reduction in Physical Fitness Index was observed in men after Antarctic stay. Whereas, in rats there was an improvement after cold acclimatization. The Hypodynamia was more marked than anticipated in men and cold exposure alone cannot be the sole contributing factor.
datasets.purpose: Life at a polar station involves a continued and high level of physical activity. All station personnel help with domestic chores which often involve quite heavy manual labour, digging snow, carrying loads around the station, apart from attending to their assigned jobs at the station. The energy cost of performing any task in polar region is quite high because of the difficulties in working in heavy clothing and travelling in the harshest known environmental conditions which limit the physical efficiency of the worker. Although extensive studies have been conducted to evaluate the changes in body functions induced by various forms of stresses in Antarctica, most of the researchers have devoted their effort to study the state of individual function system.
datasets.project_name: Evaluation of Physical Activity on Exposure to Antarctic Environment.
datasets.scientist_org: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

datasets.title: Aerosol Characteristics over parts of East Antarctica.
datasets.abstract: The properties of marine and Antarctic aerosols, their dependence on meteorological, geographical and human influences are examined using measured spectral aerosol optical depth (AOD), total mass concentration (MT) and mass concentrations of black carbon aerosol (MB), in the marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL) from coastal India and Antarctica and over two distinct coastal locations of Antarctica; Maitri (70.77 S, 11.73 E, 123 m m.s.l.) and Bharati (69.40 S, 76.20 E, 48 m m.s.l.), during southern hemispheric(SH) summer (December to March) of 2007-2008, as a part of the 27th Indian Antarctic Expedition, during International Polar Year (IPY).
datasets.purpose: Measurements of aerosol optical depth (AOD), total mass of composite aerosols (MT) and black carbon (BC) mass concentration (MB) were made over the oceanic regions between coastal India to Antarctica and at the Indian stations in Antarctica, Maitri and Bharati, during the 27th Indian Antarctic Expedition in the International Polar Year (2007-2008).
datasets.project_name: Aerosol Characteristics over parts of East Antarctica.

datasets.title: Glaciological Studies During the XVIII Expedition.
datasets.abstract: Geological studies on shelf ice, polar ice tongue and icebergs were carried out on a routine basis as part of a long term programme of these elements. S o m e variations in the accumulation/ablation pattern over shelf ice are noticed during 1999 austral summer. A near steady state of recession of the snout of Dakshin Gangotri Glacier is indicated. The monitoring of icebergs in Southern Ocean was carried out between 45? and 70? south latitude on way to Antarctica and also during return voyage. T h e observations revealed that the maximum concentration of icebergs lies in two distinct zones separated by a less frequented area.

datasets.title: Process based simulation modeling of phytoplankton organic sulphur cycling in the marginal ice edge zone of Antarctic region
datasets.abstract: The one of the major green house gases is Dimethylsulphur (DMS). The major source of DMS in seawater particularly in Arctic and Antarctic region is phytoplankton. It is currently believed that DMS is produced in vivo by the enzymatic cleavage of an algal produced precursor, dimethylsufoniopropionate (DMSP), which yields DMS and acrylic acid on a one to one basis. Major DMS and DMSP production seems to be confined to dinoflagellates and prymnesiophytes. Based on these relationships, it is evident that DMS and DMSP will vary temporarily and spatially, depending on the species composition of the flora and the environmental factors controlling their abundance. The determination of DMS concentrations along with prevailing physical and phytoplankton physiological conditions would then be mandatory for estimating the flux of DMS to the Antarctic atmosphere.
datasets.purpose: 1. To examine the variability of the ice edge bloom in terms of primary production and dominant species with respect to environmental variables in order to understand the factors potentially controlling the bloom.
